verdict_note: onDisappear clears loadingDetail and onAppear re-arms from the reconciler above; the cancelled completion block can no longer strand 解析对话…. Covered by the frame-work-performance detail fixture.

summary: activate 在 busyID == nil 时直接 return，但成对操作（更新/查询流量）在自身完成回调里把 busyID 置回 nil —— 并发第二次点击时该守卫是空操作，仍会触发 reloadConfig 并重启内核。
evidence: L87-97: `guard busyID == nil else { return }` 之后立刻 `store.browse(sub.id)`；`busyID` 只在 L127-131（更新节点配置）与 L135-139（查询流量）被写。L88 的守卫读的是 `@State busyID`，而写入发生在两处 `Task { busyID = sub.id … busyID = nil }` 的异步 completion 里，两次点击之间 SwiftUI 已把 busyID 清回 nil，守卫读到的永远是 nil。
failure: 用户在「更新节点配置」菜单项仍在下载时点到「启用」：busyID 已被前一个任务写为 nil，guard 通过，随后 L92-96 若 manager 未运行会同时改写 `vpnEnabled` / `vpnSystemProxyEnabled` 并 `reloadConfig()`，一次点击触发内核重启（控制端口 9097 与 mixed-port 需等旧核退出），页面出现「启动中…」并丢掉刚启动的内核。
fix: 把 busy 态做成成对的真源（例如 `activeOperationID: UUID?`，只在唯一入口 `withBusy { }` 里设置/清除），并让 activate 在 `manager.state == .starting` 之外也检查 `activeOperationID != nil`；或至少把 L88 的守卫改为检查 `manager.launchTask != nil` 之类的真实进行中状态，而不是自身刚被清空的 busyID。
verdict_note: Root cause was wider than the activate guard: three loose @State flags (busyID, queryingAll, adding) were written inside Task closures, whose bodies run a main-actor turn after the click, so any second click in the same event batch passed every guard — and activate additionally could not see the restart it itself started. Replaced with SubscriptionBusy, a value type holding a single Owner (.add / .queryAll / .update(UUID)): claim() is called synchronously in each click (menu paths via startBusy, the sheet save before its Task, delete/activate guard against isIdle), release(owner) only frees the lock if the releasing operation still holds it (a straggler cannot clear a newer claim), and activate's guard now reads busy.isIdle + manager.state != .starting (reloadConfig sets .starting synchronously). Covered by Tests/vpn-subscription-reentry-regressions.py: the production lock is sliced and executed (single claimant, owner-scoped release, straggler rejection, finding-37 interleaving shown), the section wiring is pinned, and 4 mutants trip (activate dropping the restart check, release freeing any owner, menu path setting a local flag, delete alert skipping the lock).

summary: 暂停时 pendingRows 会重复累计同一 revision 的新行：entries.count 不变时 intra-revision early-exit 缺失，doc 里说是幂等但守卫条件只看了 visibleRows。
evidence: L717-719: `if !followTail, let lastSeenID { pendingRows += result.rows.reduce(0) { $0 + ($1.id > lastSeenID ? 1 : 0) } }`；L722: `if key.mode != .detail || followTail || lastSeenID == nil || entries.isEmpty { visibleRows = result.rows }`。暂停后 `requestKey == key` 且 early-exit 已发生（L699/L717 之间）。Tests/vpn-domain-log-regressions.py:471-473 断言同一 revision 不重复累计，但夹具 `cache.log.entries = Array(batch[1_000..<3_000])` 每次换数组（id 从 1001…3000 变成 2001…3000 再变），所以 `entries.count` 变了，走的是「新 revision」路径。生产环境里 ring 满时 entries.count 固定为 2000、只有 id 滚动，正是该测试没覆盖的形状。
failure: 日志 ring 已满 2000 行、用户暂停跟随并向历史页翻了一页；此后每来 1 行新记录，ring 仍保留 2000 行（count 不变）、`result.rows` 里 `id > lastSeenID` 仍只得 1 条 —— 每 tick 都把同一条再计一次。60 s 内来 100 条即显示「100 条新记录」，且数字持续翻倍增长；用户在暂停页看到的计数不再等于实际未读行数。
fix: 在 L717 的累加前加上与 L722 相同的「本次快照是否换过」判定，例如记录上一次参与累计的 `entries.last?.id`，只有它变化时才累加；或把 L722 的条件提前到一个 `let freshSnapshot = ...` 布尔并同时用于两处。
verdict_note: Code-traced, then pinned by test. The claim was that a full ring (entries.count fixed at 2,000, ids rolling) would recount the same rows on a post-pause recompute. It cannot: `lastSeenID = entries.last?.id` at the end of `recompute()` advances unconditionally, including on the frames where `visibleRows` is frozen, and ids only grow. Successive runs therefore partition the id range — a repeat run over one snapshot adds exactly 0, and each forward-rolling flush adds exactly its new arrivals (the evicted rows leave the ring, so no arrival is ever scanned twice). A double count would require a run that counts rows without advancing `lastSeenID`, and no such path exists (`resetFollow()` clears `lastSeenID` but also zeroes `pendingRows`; the resume button does both; `log.clear()` empties `entries`). The claim's 60 s scenario holds revision constant while entries changed, which production never does — every flush bumps `revision`, and the .task(id:) key restarts. Tests/vpn-domain-log-regressions.py now drives the exact full-ring shape directly: id-rolling snapshots at a fixed key, 50 consecutive flushes count exactly 50, and a same-snapshot repeat adds zero; deleting the advance line or the per-id predicate both trip the new preconditions. No production change: the L717-719 comment now documents the partition argument instead of overclaiming an 'early-exit' guard.

summary: withAnimation(Theme.Animation.bouncy) on the hover flag makes every hover flip in a swarm cluster run the whole hosting view's layout + display list for the ~0.4-0.6 s of the spring — including the freshly-laid-out tile under the cursor.
evidence: AgentSwarmView.swift:324-326 — `let next: String? = hovering ? child.id : ...; guard next != hoveredId else { return }; withAnimation(Theme.Animation.bouncy) { hoveredId = next }`. THEME: Theme.swift:339 `static let bouncy = SwiftUI.Animation.bouncy(duration: 0.24, extraBounce: 0.16)` — a bouncy spring settles later than its 0.24 s duration. The codebase's own measured rule, written next to the identical pattern it removed (Interaction.swift:329-338): `.animation(_:value:)` beside a per-update value had `runAnimationGroup:` inside `NSHostingView.layout()` at 31 % of main-thread samples and `stepIdle` at 56 %, because "an in-flight transaction makes the display cycle run the whole hosting view's layout + display list", and docs/technical/05-view-layer.md:15 promises "全部状态驱动，无常驻时间线". `hoverTile`/`HoverState` (UiverseSurfaces.swift:30-55, Interaction.swift:142-152) do exactly this job with NO withAnimation, and the tile the pointer is entering is always freshly laid out (inflight-animation-regressions.py:335-340 records hover flips as layout-heavy).
failure: A pointer crossing a 2-row strip (9 cards, SessionsView.swift:941-945) or a 6x10 cluster (60 cards) fires one open→close pair per card boundary; each pair re-runs layout for the hosting view for the spring's full lifetime. At 120 Hz ProMotion that is ~50-70 display cycles of whole-window layout for a 6 pt scale bump on one 68x24 card. The current damage is bounded only because this code deliberately kept out the per-frame cost (no neighbouring `SpriteView`/`Canvas`) — it is the remaining worst idle-vs-hover delta on the sessions page.
fix: Keep the edge-trigger guard at :325 and drive the flag parent-side, as the rest of the app does: hold `hoveredId` where `hovered` is already read (line 41) and pass a per-child `hovered`/binding into `childCard`, so the flag write happens outside any `withAnimation` and the surfaces that want motion animate their own leaves (`Theme.Motion.state`). Minimal version in-file: swap `withAnimation(Theme.Animation.bouncy) { hoveredId = next }` for `hoveredId = next` and put `Theme.Animation.bouncy` on `scaleEffect`/opacity at line 317 (settles in ~0.1-0.2 s instead of holding a transaction).
verdict_note: Code: the cluster's `withAnimation(Theme.Animation.bouncy)` around the `hoveredId` write is gone — the flag flips plainly, the border eases on its own keyed on the *card's* `isHovered` (`Theme.Motion.state`, 0.15 s ease, not a spring), and the 1.06 scale is applied in one frame (the `SignatureGlyph` shape: a text-bearing subtree is not put behind an in-flight transaction, which is what made every display cycle re-run the hosting view's layout for the spring's lifetime). The edge-trigger guard is unchanged. Hover motion is preserved: border colour + width + fill + dot still answer the pointer, now instantly like `hoverTile`/`IconChip`.

summary: 表格编辑的撤销注册指向 navigator.activeView?.undoManager，但该视图在编辑器重建后会被释放，导致 registerUndo 落入新的空 UndoManager 或 nil，撤销栈断裂
evidence: private func change(_ update: (inout DocumentTable) -> Void) { controller.change(undoManager: navigator.activeView?.undoManager, update) }（第 187 行）。navigator.activeView 是 activeID.flatMap { views[$0]?.view }（DocumentInlineEditor.swift:109），views 只存弱引用（第 105 行 WeakView）。表格 body 每次 model.cells 变化时重排 clusters（第 56-64 行），活跃单元格的 editor 是 NSViewRepresentable；SwiftUI 在 ForEach 身份变化时会拆除并重建 DocumentTextView，旧的 undoManager 随之消失。controller.change 里 undoManager?.registerUndo(withTarget: self)（第 22 行）在 undoManager 为 nil 时静默不注册，publish() 仍执行。
failure: 用户编辑单元格 A 后点 Tab 跳到最后一格触发 insertRow（第 152 行 change），configure() 重排 order 并让 editor 重建；此后在任意单元格做列宽/合并/删除行操作，change 传入的 undoManager 为 nil，Cmd+Z 无任何可撤销步骤——表格的结构变更（增删行列、合并、框线）全部不可撤销，而 UI 文案「尺寸与结构变化进入原生撤销栈」（docs/design/surfaces/feishu-documents.md:29）与实现不符。
fix: 让 DocumentTableController 持有自己的 UndoManager（或由父视图注入稳定的 UndoManager 引用），在 controller 内部 registerUndo，而不是每次从 navigator.activeView 取瞬时视图的 undoManager。
verdict_note: Code: the structure-change undo stack now resolves `activeView?.window?.undoManager ?? firstView?.window?.undoManager ?? NSApp.keyWindow?.undoManager` (DocumentFocusNavigator.structureUndoManager), and both writers — `change(_:)` and the resize-drag end — route through it. Why `.window`: measured with real AppKit views, every NSTextView in a window reports the same `window.undoManager`, so the stack survives the editor rebuilds SwiftUI performs when cell identity changes; and a view's own `undoManager` while unmounted is a private dead-end manager the menu cannot reach. The finding's nil case is real and was reproduced before the fix: `navigator.activeID` only fills when a cell is focused and dangles after a re-parse replaces the cells, so a first structure operation (right-click on a fresh table, or a column drag as the first click) registered into nothing. Tests/feishu-documents-regressions.py now pins it: with no cell focused, a structure change lands on the fixture window's stack, undo restores the width, and a rebuilt editor under the same cell id resolves to the same manager. Reverting the routing to `activeView?.undoManager` trips the new precondition.

summary: Tab 边界导航依赖 navigator.order 的字典序，而 activateLink/navigate 使用全表 UUID；Tab 从合并单元格向前移动时可能跳到错误单元格
evidence: private func navigate(_ cell: DocumentTable.Cell, direction: Int) -> Bool { if navigator.move(from: cell.id.uuidString, direction: direction) ... }（第 149-150 行）。DocumentFocusNavigator.move（DocumentInlineEditor.swift:112-118）用 order.firstIndex(of: id) + direction 取下一个 id，再用 views[...] 弱引用找视图。order 由 configure() 生成：model.cells.sorted { $0.row == $1.row ? $0.column < $1.column : $0.row < $1.row }.map { $0.id.uuidString }（第 90 行）。但 insertRow/insertColumn/fillHoles（DocumentTable.swift:122-139、111-121）会向 cells 追加新单元格而不重排，configure() 在每次 model.cells.map(\.id) 变化时重跑（第 86 行）——排序本身正确。问题在 DocumentTextBox 的 onBoundary 只在 selection.location == 0 / upperBound == 长度 时触发（DocumentInlineEditor.swift:48-49），而 Tab 由 insertTab: 无条件触发（第 46 行）：在编辑中途按 Tab 会直接跳走并丢弃当前 IME 组合文本（hasMarkedText guard 仅在 textDidChange 里）。
failure: 中文输入法组合中（marked text 未上屏）按 Tab：insertTab → parent.onBoundary(1) → navigator.move 把焦点切到下一格，组合文本丢失；表格单元格内正常输入 IME 时 Tab 是常见误触，出现丢字。
fix: 在 Coordinator.textView(_:doCommandBy:) 的 insertTab:/insertBacktab: 分支前加 guard !textView.hasMarkedText() else { return false }，或在 navigate 里检查 activeView?.hasMarkedText()。
verdict_note: Code: the delegate's `doCommandBy` now commits an open IME composition (`unmarkText()`) before announcing any boundary move (Tab / Shift-Tab / edge arrows). Measured in the fixture: with marked text live, AppKit queues `insertTab:` to the delegate and the marked text survives the move — it rides into a view that is no longer first responder, and `textDidChange` deliberately skips marked text, so the composed characters never reached the model and were lost. `unmarkText` commits the composition in place (fixture: string keeps the composed text, delegate fire count increments, the subsequent boundary move sees the committed value). The review's suggested alternative — `guard !hasMarkedText() else { return false }` — was rejected after measurement: declining the command lets the *default* `insertTab:` run, which inserts a literal tab character into the cell (measured), the worse half of the same bug. Tests/feishu-documents-regressions.py drives the production coordinator: Tab at the edge with marked text must announce the move, clear `hasMarkedText`, and publish the composed string; removing the unmark trips the precondition.

summary: onDisappear 只在编辑中提交，导致「输入后直接切换设置分类」静默丢弃用户输入；同时失效的草稿保留到下次进入
evidence: .onDisappear { if editing { commit() } }（第 31 行）。SettingsView 用 switch state.category 重建内容（Sources/ClaudeBar/Views/Pages/SettingsView.swift:31-36），且 ScrollView 带 .id(state.category)（第 45 行），所以切换分类会让 ExchangeRateTile 离开视图树触发 onDisappear。commit()（第 84-100 行）是唯一把 draft 写进 prefs.manualUSDToCNY 的路径；editing=true 期间 TextField 绑定 draft（第 40 行），没有 onChange(of: draft) 提前提交。另外 commit 的非空但非法分支不重置 editing，draft 也保留。
failure: 用户点开数字 → 输入 7.35 → 不回车、不失焦，直接点左侧「外观」（或 .id(category) 让 ScrollView 重建）→ onDisappear 时 editing 仍为 true，commit() 把 manualUSDToCNY 设为 7.35，computed effectiveRate 变成手动值——但用户从未按确认；更糟的是若用户已经点进编辑又离开（editing=true），下次回来时 draft 会以旧值预填（第 57 行 的按钮分支才刷新），或撤销料：若用户在编辑中离开后本意是放弃编辑，commit 反而写入手动汇率，使「更新」按钮永久禁用（第 28 行 fx.isManual）。
fix: 在 commit() 增加对「离开即放弃」的显式分支（例如由 onDisappear 调用 cancel()：editing=false; draft=""），并把 onDisappear 改为 { if editing { cancel() } }；若维持提交语义，至少在 commit 非法分支里把 editing 复位已做，需再补 draft 清空的统一出口。
verdict_note: Measured: the mechanism the finding describes is real — an NSHostingView probe (ScrollView `.id(category)` teardown with `editing == true`) fires `onDisappear` and runs the commit exactly once. But the behaviour it describes is the row's documented and deliberate semantics, not a defect: the field's own comment states 'Losing focus is a commit, not a cancel … there is no other way to finish editing the preference', the `.onChange(of: rateFocused)` blur path already commits in exactly this situation, and `.onDisappear` was added in 620c375 so teardown preserves that rule instead of silently dropping the edit. Two of the finding's supporting claims are also stale against the current source: `commit()` sets `editing = false` first, and the entry branch refreshes `draft` from `effectiveRate` on every entry, so no stale draft survives. Clicking the number is documented as entering manual mode ('点数字可设置手动汇率'), so committing the shown value on the way out is the affordance the user exercised.

summary: The cursorData permission-revocation block is dead code: nothing calls refresh() when the switch flips, so the last ledger reading survives and the money row still renders while the switch is off.
evidence:
Lines 115-125 clear everything when the gate says no:
```
guard PermissionGate.allows(.cursorData) else {
    task?.cancel(); task = nil; loading = false
    self.rows = [:]; self.window = nil; truncated = false
    fetchedAt = nil; note = nil
    return
}
```
Callers of `refresh` are only `ProviderStore.swift:1184` (from `requestSettlement()`) and `CursorTokenUsageCard.swift:100` (`.task(id: window) { refresh() }`). Neither is triggered by a `.permissionDidChange` notification: `ProviderStore`'s observer (ProviderStore.swift:681-694) switches on `.widgetData` / `.cursorData` and only calls `refreshCursorSessions()` for the latter — it never re-runs `requestSettlement()`. `CursorUsageStore` solves exactly this with a dedicated observer (CursorUsageStore.swift:47-57: `if PermissionGate.allows(.cursorData) { self.start(); self.refresh() } else { self.stop() }`); `CursorLedgerStore` has no equivalent. A repo-wide grep for `cursorLedgerDidChange|isStale|ledger.window` outside this file returns only observers of its own success post and view reads.
failure: User has a reading on screen (rows/window/fetchedAt populated), then turns off 读取 Cursor 会话 in Settings → no refresh() call is made → `rows`/`window` stay populated, `CursorTokenUsageCard.swift:80` keeps drawing the money and tokens from `ledger.rows`, the warm-start copy stays on disk, and the gate block above never executes. Re-launching keeps showing the persisted reading as well (the init at lines 70-75 loads the cache before any gate check — same as `CursorUsageStore`, but there the stop() observer eventually clears it).
fix: Add the missing revocation path: observe `.permissionDidChange` for `.cursorData` (as `CursorUsageStore` does) and call `CursorLedgerStore.shared.refresh(window:billingCycle:)` on re-enable; on disable, clear `rows`/`window`/`fetchedAt`/`note`, cancel `task`, and delete `cursor-ledger.json`. Minimal shape: a `private var permissionObserver: NSObjectProtocol?` set up in `init`, mirroring CursorUsageStore.swift:47-57.
verdict_note: Code: `CursorLedgerStore` now observes `.permissionDidChange` for `.cursorData` (the `CursorUsageStore.start()` shape) and acts on both directions — `revoke()` cancels the in-flight task, clears rows/window/truncated/fetchedAt/note/loading and deletes the warm-start file (`LedgerCache.clear()`), `revive()` re-reads the window the page last asked for (`lastRequestedWindow`, recorded before the gate so a request made while off still names it). The warm start itself is now gated on the switch — with it off the persisted reading must not be drawn even for the frame before the first refresh. The `refresh` path still clears on the gate as before, so the two directions share one code path. Test: new suite `cursor-ledger-lifecycle` (`Tests/cursor-ledger-lifecycle-regressions.py`, registered in `make test`) slices the store verbatim with a continuation transport; it asserts revocation clears the live reading *and* the file, a read completing after revocation cannot republish, a request while off is remembered but never read, a regrant re-reads the last requested window, and — in a separate process per gate answer — that a seeded cache file loads only when the switch allows. Four mutants fail (observer removed; file kept; regrant not re-reading; warm start ungated).

summary: `(recency >= ? OR checkpointAt >= ?)` forces a full index-table scan on every 2.5 s poll; the checkpoint arm is provably redundant with the Swift-side liveness predicate.
evidence:
SQL at lines 203-209 (and the child query at 296-301):
```
WHERE isArchived = 0 AND isSubagent = 0
  AND (recency >= ? OR checkpointAt >= ?)
```
`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on this machine's real DB (13.8 GB state.vscdb, 875 composerHeaders rows, index `idx_composerHeaders_1 ON (recency, composerId)`) yields `SCAN composerHeaders USING INDEX idx_composerHeaders_1` — no range seek. No index covers `checkpointAt`, so the OR is not index-usable. A synthetic 50k-row table with the same DDL reproduces it: production OR-form 5.15 ms (SCAN) vs `recency >= ?` only 0.11 ms (SEARCH) — ~47x. Swift-side check: the row predicate never uses the SQL's checkpoint arm either — line 246 computes `updatedAt = max(submittedAt, terminalCurrent ? 0 : checkpointAt, scan.modifiedAt)` and line 255 `isAlive: updatedAt > cutoff`, where `submittedAt` falls back to the column recency and `checkpointAt` is `max(column, JSON mirror)`. Cross-checking 875 real rows with that predicate: 0 rows are `isAlive` while excluded by `recency >= cutoff` alone (and column checkpointAt == JSON `conversationCheckpointLastUpdatedAt` in all 611 row pairs that carry both).
failure: Steady-state: two full scans of composerHeaders (main + subagent query) per `fetchActive()` call, i.e. per session poll (2.5 s busy / 5 s idle / 8 s hidden). On a 500k-row long-lived install this is ~50 ms of SQLite CPU per poll on a background thread, waking every 2.5 s; the query also cannot shrink below O(rows) as Cursor accumulates composers, so the cost grows with account age even though the recent set stays at a handful.
fix: Drop the checkpoint arm from both WHERE clauses (`AND recency >= ?`), keep `checkpointAt` in the SELECT list — the checkpoint clock still rescues a long run through `updatedAt`/`isAlive`, and the row is selected because its `recency` moved when the run started. If a genuinely checkpoint-only row must be caught, add a dedicated index or a second short query restricted by an indexed `checkpointAt`, not an OR.
verdict_note: 58040bd: OR checkpointAt arm removed from both polls (index scan -> range scan); measured 611 real rows and the 09-28 composer

summary: scanTail JSON-decodes the entire 96 KB tail (~67 records) although every consumed state is decided by the tail end; measured 1.4-1.6 ms per file, ~10 ms per poll for the typical visible set.
failure: Every session poll (2.5-8 s, all day) decodes ~9.6 KB x N sessions of JSON that cannot change the published state; on Cursor installations with many recently-active composers the cost is tens of ms of utility-thread CPU per poll with the associated energy wakeups, for a result identical to the cheap scan.

Optionally skip the read entirely when `unfinishedRunAt == 0` and the file mtime is older than `turnLiveWindowMs` (on this machine that prefilter leaves 0 of 4 recent heads to read).

summary: model is empty for long-lived Codex sessions because both the 32 KB head and the 512 KB tail miss the nearest turn_context
evidence: Line 626 reads only 32 KB (`readHead(path: path, bytes: 32_000)`) and `readHead` stops at the first chunk that contains a newline (line 702-707), so for a rollout whose first line (session_meta) is ~23 KB the head holds session_meta plus one partial line. Line 635 falls back to `headModel(in: head)` (lines 720-729), and line 627's tail scan only ever sees the last `codexTailWindow = 512_000` bytes (line 715, start computed at line 757). Replayed over this machine's real corpus (~/.codex/sessions, 24 rollouts): for 7 of 24 rollouts -- including the 44.5 MB session that is currently being written and the 2.5 MB one from 2026-10-04 -- the first turn_context record sits at byte 102,011 while the head ends at 32,000, and the last turn_context is 0.8-2.1 MB before EOF, outside the 512 KB window, so both routes return "". Meanwhile `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite` `threads.model` is populated for all 24 unarchived rows (e.g. gpt-6.1-sol for rollout 01a10603), and `IndexedThread` (line 430) already carries the row.
failure: ExternalSessionInfo.model == "" for the sessions the user is running now -> ExternalSessionCardView.swift:78 renders the cwd instead of the model (`session.model.isEmpty ? session.cwd : session.model`), IslandComponents.swift:236 drops the "model · 运行中" line, SessionsView.swift:394/826/1000 print the empty/placeholder string. Deterministic on 29% of this machine's rollouts and on exactly the newest, longest ones.
fix: Add `model` to the index SELECT (line 553-556) and `IndexedThread`, then in `indexedCodexSessions` use `parsed?.model` ?? row.model (line 515). For the legacy no-index path, read a deeper head (e.g. continue past the first line until the first turn_context or 256 KB) instead of stopping at the first newline chunk. Add a `model != ""` precondition to Tests/codex-session-regressions.py, which today pins titles/activity/stall but never the model.
verdict_note: Code: `readThreadIndex` now selects the `model` column when the table has it (optional like `thread_source` — older tables must not lose the whole index path), `IndexedThread` carries it, and `codexFields` folds the routes in currency order: (1) the newest `turn_context` from the tail window (a thread that switched models mid-life shows the model it is on now), (2) the index row's `model`, (3) the shallow head then a bounded 256 KB `firstModel` read — the legacy no-index walk's only route. The ordinal is computed (`hasThreadSource ? 7 : 6`) rather than hard-coded. Measured on this machine's corpus: 7 of 24 rollouts — among them the 44.5 MB session and the 2.5 MB one — have their first turn_context at byte ~102 KB (past the 32 KB head read, whose first line already runs ~23 KB) and their newest megabytes before EOF (past the 512 KB tail window), so both old routes returned "". Test: `codex-session-regressions.py` now seeds three shapes — `long-lived` (index `model` is the only route), `deep-head` (no index column; the deeper head read finds it), `switched` (the tail's newest turn_context must outrank the index) — plus a no-turn_context negative; four mutants fail (no index hint, index before tail, no deeper read, wrong column ordinal). A read-only probe against the real ~/.codex was attempted but this session's process cannot open that SQLite file (prepare rc=14), so the real-corpus re-measurement stays as the review's own numbers.

summary: 发现门控被 `||` 优先级拆成两个独立条件，attribution 关闭时仍会跑全进程表扫描，结果随即被丢弃
evidence: 第 398 行原文：`if wantsAttribution, now - lastDiscoveryAt >= discoveryInterval || lastDiscoveryAt == 0 {`。Swift 的 `,` 比 `||` 绑定更松，实际语义是 `(wantsAttribution && now - lastDiscoveryAt >= 10) || lastDiscoveryAt == 0`，而不是注释/设计意图的 `wantsAttribution && (lastDiscoveryAt == 0 || now - lastDiscoveryAt >= 10)`。`lastDiscoveryAt` 只在 400 行被写为当前 uptime；`setAgentPIDs`（334-344）在 pid 集合变化时把 `lastDiscoveryAt = 0`。第 499 行 `guard wantsAttribution else { publish(... byKey: [:], shares: []) ; return }` 在 `index.buildChildIndex()`（514）之前，所以这一 tick 的扫描结果没有任何消费方。实测本机进程表规模：`proc_listallpids(nil, 0)` 返回 579，`/bin/ps -axo pid=,rss=,comm=` 563 行。
failure: 窗口不可见（`UIWakePolicy.hasVisibleWindow == false`，timer 走 6/12 s 档）时，`ProviderStore.refreshSessions` 仍每 8 s 调一次 `setAgentPIDs`；任何会话启动/退出都会改变 pid 集合 → `lastDiscoveryAt = 0` → 下一 tick 右侧为真 → 后台跑完整扫描（每个 pid 一次 `proc_name` + 一次 `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO`，每个 node 还要一次 `KERN_PROCARGS2`），随后在 499 行把 `byKey` 清空发布。用户什么都看不到，采样器却按最贵路径走了一遍，并且这与 `start()` 注释里“Nobody's watching → suspend it”的承诺相反。
fix: 把条件加上括号：`if wantsAttribution, lastDiscoveryAt == 0 || now - lastDiscoveryAt >= discoveryInterval {`（即 `wantsAttribution && (...)`）。
verdict_note: Measured with a standalone -O probe of the exact condition shape: Swift's `if a, b || c` is a condition *list* — `a` AND (`b || c`) — so `||` already binds inside the second element. With `wantsAttribution = false` the body does not run at any `lastDiscoveryAt`; with it true and `lastDiscoveryAt == 0` the body runs. The claim that `||` splits the comma into two independent conditions does not hold, so the discovery scan is already gated on attribution.

summary: node 进程的 Codex 判定读的是 KERN_PROCARGS2 整块（含环境变量），argv 或 env 里出现 'codex' 的普通 node 会被当成 Codex 会话占位
evidence: 第 998-1011 行取整块：`var size = 0; sysctl(&mib, 3, nil, &size, ...)`，`scratch.argv = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: size)`，然后 `return text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("codex")`。实测（ctypes 复现同样的 sysctl）：用 `env CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codexrepro/codex-home` 启动的 `/usr/local/bin/node -e 'setTimeout(()=>{},30000)'`，KERN_PROCARGS2 块 4684 字节且明文含 `CODEX_HOME`——该缓冲区在 argv 之后就是 `KEY=value` 环境段（实测打印 `COLORTERM=truecolor`、`COMMAND_MODE=unix2003`）。调用方第 922 行 `lower.hasPrefix("node")` 命中后即走这里。本应用自己就注入这样的环境：MigrationStorage.swift:245 `case .codex: environment = ["CODEX_HOME=" + locations.codex.path]`，路径形如 `.../claude-bar-codex-sessions`。
failure: 任何带 `CODEX_HOME=<...codex...>` 或 argv 里含 codex 的 node 进程（迁移桥的子进程、用户自己起的 codex-cli 包装、IDE 的 codex 扩展）会被收进 `codexByCwd`；第 528-535 行把它写进 `byKey[.cwd(...)]` 并 `claimed.formUnion(group)`，于是 (1) Codex 家族份额凭空增大，(2) `cursorPIDs` 在第 522 行被 `filter { !claimed.contains($0) }` 排除——同一 cwd 下真正的 Cursor 进程会被永久剥离，`.cursor` chip 显示 “—”（ResourceStrip.swift:459）。今天本机（pid 772 node）argv/env 不含 codex，所以是潜伏缺陷而非现网必然，这也是 confidence=medium 的原因。
fix: 只匹配 argv 段：跳过第一个 NUL 之前的路径，取参数区（到第一个形如 `NAME=value` 的字节或前 4 KB）再判断；不要对整块 argv+env 做 localizedCaseInsensitiveContains。
verdict_note: f007c8b/81c3c9c: argvMentionsCodex now parses argc and scans argv only (env skipped); process-argv regression suite

summary: cwd 键两侧不对称：内核路径的 /private 前缀只在目录仍存在时被折叠，Codex 会话行在目录消失后永远显示 “—”。
evidence: ProcessSampler.swift:931 `let key = (cwd as NSString).standardizingPath`（内核 buffter 给出的是 `/private/var/...`），而视图侧是 38-39 `Key.standardizedCwd(session.cwd)`。实测（-O 编译，精确复刻这两个函数）：目录存在时 `/private/var/folders/…/T/keyprobe-7440` → `/var/folders/…`，与视图键一致；目录被删后同一进程的内核 cwd 仍是 `/private/var/…`，但 standardizingPath 不再折叠 → sampler 键 `/private/var/folders/…`、view 键 `/var/folders/…`，实测输出 “MATCH: false”。`~/…/.codex/sessions` 里 14 份 rollout 的 `session_meta.cwd` 正是 `/var/folders/lj/…/T`（另 9 份是 `/tmp`，同样在 /private/tmp 删除后失配），而 workspace 临时目录在自动化跑完后会被清理。
failure: Codex 曾在 /var/folders 或 /tmp 下（迁移、自动化、临时 workspace）工作 → 临时目录被清理 → 该 Codex 行 `sampler.byKey[.cwd(...)]` 永远为 nil，SessionLoadChip 常驻 “—”，与机器负载无关；重启 App 也不会自愈（每次扫描都重新取被删目录的 /private 拼写）。
fix: 两侧用同一规范化：抽一个函数，先 standardizingPath，若结果仍以 "/private/" 开头则去掉该前缀（或在 scan 侧对内核路径做与 Key.standardizedCwd 相同的预处理），保证同一 cwd 在两种实存状态下产生同一 Key。
verdict_note: `ProcessSampler.Key.canonicalCwd` is now the single spelling for both sides: it standardizes and folds the three published `/private` root-symlink prefixes (`/etc`, `/tmp`, `/var`) at the *leading* component only, while a deeper `/private/...` path is left alone. `ProcessIndex.scan` builds its `byCwd` keys through it, so a kernel-reported `/private/var/...` matches a session row's `/var/...` even after the directory is gone. `process-cpu-regressions.py` slices the function and asserts 10 mappings including the negative cases.

summary: 电池 IOKit 读取位于 `guard wantsAttribution` 之上，无窗口的后台档每 6–12 s 醒来只为读一个没人看的电量读数。
evidence: tick 在 452 行无条件 `let battery = HardwareSensors.batteryStatus()`，而 `guard wantsAttribution` 在 499 行才分流；后台档周期由 379-391 给出（无 scope 前台 6 s、后台 12 s）。实测同一 IOKit 形状的读取（IOServiceGetMatchingService(AppleSmartBattery)+IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperties）为 0.314 ms/次（200 次平均）；UIWakePolicy.swift:27-30 说明无可见窗口时进程仍常驻。按 6 s 档计：每日 ~14 400 次 × 0.31 ms ≈ 4.4 s 的唤醒尾巴 + 约 1.6 ms/s 摊薄占用，且它是每 tick 唯一必付的“贵读”。
failure: 用户合上窗口整天不打开 App → 采样线程仍按 6–12 s 唤醒并做 IORegistry 往返，属可完全消除的常驻能耗；结果只是被 publish 到没人观察的 `host`。
fix: 把 452 行降到 499 行之后（attribution 分支内）读取；或在此处复用上次读数（host.battery* 已是值类型），只在 wantsAttribution 时重读——注释里“电量 mark 是常驻的”对应的是 popup 打开的场景，那时 wantsAttribution 必为真。
verdict_note: `tick()` now refreshes the battery reading only while a visible-surface tier is active (`wantsDevices`), on a 5 s gate, and reuses the last sample otherwise; the background 6–12 s tier no longer opens the IOKit service. The published `Snapshot` still carries the cached values every tick, so the popup's first frame renders a real percentage. Verified by `make build` + `make test TEST="process-cpu measured-performance interaction-performance"`.

summary: compaction persists *pending* rows, so a request still streaming when a compaction fires is written to disk twice under the same id — once as `"end":""` by the compaction, once sealed by `finish` — and the loader keeps both rows.
evidence: Line 436 `let snapshot = rows` takes the whole ring, pending rows included (a row is in `rows` from `begin`, line 254, but is not on disk until `finish`). Line 439 `snapshot.compactMap { encode($0) }` then writes those pending rows out. `finish` appends unconditionally (line 302) once the request ends. Measured on this machine: `~/Library/Application Support/ClaudeBar/logs/proxy.jsonl` = 500 rows / 172 KB, `grep -c '"end":""'` = 2, and ids 95246 / 95254 each appear on two adjacent lines (line 458 pending `'end':''`, line 459 sealed `'end':'2026-09-30T10:16:19Z'`). Loading such a file (loadHistory line 213-226, decode line 469-506, both ids > 0 with different `end` values) appends *both* rows to `rows`, and `ProxyLogView` renders `ForEach(filtered)` keyed on `row.id` (Views/Pages/ProxyLogView.swift:175) plus `scrollTo(last.id)` (line 240-245).
failure: Every traffic burst that quiets down for 2 s while a second request is still streaming (the normal case: `streamSSE` calls go out while another finishes) writes one pending line, and the eventual `finish` appends a second line for the same id. After the next launch the ring holds two entries with identical `id`: SwiftUI's `ForEach` gets duplicate identities (undefined behaviour — wrong row reused/animated), `scrollTo(last.id)` can target the stale copy, and 复制 emits the same call twice in one console line pair. Left unchecked this grows by one duplicate per compaction window.
fix: Write only sealed rows in compaction: line 439 becomes `snapshot.compactMap { $0.endedAt == nil ? nil : encode($0) }`; and keep `loadHistory` tolerant by deduping on id (keep the row with the non-nil `endedAt`), since older sidecars already contain such pairs.
verdict_note: Measured with a standalone -O slice of the production class (temporary dirs only): a sidecar with a duplicate id and an unsealed row loads as 2 rows, the later line wins, the orphan is sealed with `interrupted`; `{"id":18446744073709551615,…}` no longer traps the next `begin` (next id 1); a 700-call burst leaves exactly 500 sealed, unique, ordered lines on disk that reload as the same 500; `clear` removes the file and the next append recreates exactly one line; a note-only `finish` still exports its buckets.

summary: `nextID` is derived from the sidecar's own `id` with no upper bound, and `begin()` then does `nextID += 1`; a corrupt or hostile `id` of 18446744073709551615 (accepted because `decode` only checks `id > 0` after the lossy `NSNumber.uint64Value` conversion) makes the next request trap on UInt64 overflow inside the proxy's forwarding path.
evidence: Line 221: `nextID = (history.map(\.id).max() ?? 0) + 1`; line 234-235: `let id = nextID; nextID += 1`; line 472-473: `let id = (obj["id"] as? NSNumber)?.uint64Value ?? 0; guard id > 0`. Verified with swift: the JSON literal `18446744073709551615` decodes to NSNumber.uint64Value == UInt64.max, and `UInt64.max + 1` is a runtime trap under -O.
failure: A single line `{"id":18446744073709551615,...}` in proxy.jsonl (path traversal aside, the file is user-writable and survives `clear`'s removeItem only if removal failed) makes the first proxied request after launch trap in `ProxyAccessLog.begin`, taking the proxy and the app down.
fix: Clamp while reading: `nextID = min(history.map(\.id).max() ?? 0, 1 << 62) + 1`, and reject ids above a sane ceiling in `decode` rather than only `id > 0`.
verdict_note: Measured with a standalone -O slice of the production class (temporary dirs only): a sidecar with a duplicate id and an unsealed row loads as 2 rows, the later line wins, the orphan is sealed with `interrupted`; `{"id":18446744073709551615,…}` no longer traps the next `begin` (next id 1); a 700-call burst leaves exactly 500 sealed, unique, ordered lines on disk that reload as the same 500; `clear` removes the file and the next append recreates exactly one line; a note-only `finish` still exports its buckets.

summary: First-prompt head read reopens and rescans the transcript head on every poll whose transcript stamp changed, and 19/124 real local transcripts burn the full 512KB budget every scan.
evidence: firstHumanPrompt(for:) (lines 348-380) does its own FileHandle open plus a 16KB-chunked scan up to maximumHead=512_000, and fetchContext's ContextScan carries `title: firstHumanPrompt(for: session)` (line 587). The ProviderStore.enrich cache branch (Models/ProviderStore.swift:452-465) only reuses firstPrompt when size AND mtime both match and size>0; any write (mtime granularity) or a same-size rewrite invalidates, so an actively-written session re-scans every 2.5s-5s. Measured on this machine: 124 local transcripts, 19 have no human-origin record in the first 6MB and therefore run the loop to its 512KB bound and still return "" (line 379), and 2 have their first human prompt at 77KB and 219KB — past the first chunk. The comment at line 353-355 ('Prompts live well inside the first few records') holds only for the median case.
failure: N live sessions x (1-2 FileHandle opens + up to 512KB decode) per poll, every 2.5s busy / 5s idle / 8s hidden, on top of the 96KB tail read — for a session like the measured 219KB-prompt ones the head scan is the single most expensive part of the scan and its answer never changes.
fix: Pass the transcript stamp (size+mtime) into the scan and skip the head read when unchanged — the prompt is immutable once found; and stop the chunk loop after the first chunk that yields a human prompt or whose last line is complete.
verdict_note: `SessionMonitor.firstHumanPrompt` takes the transcript identity (the same size+mtime pair `ProviderStore` already stamps) and answers from a sessionId-keyed cache when it matches; `fetchContext` passes the stamp it was given. A miss is not cached (the file may still be growing toward the prompt), and a caller that cannot supply a stamp reads without caching. `session-scan-regressions.py` drives the cache both ways: same stamp answers from memory (proved by rewriting the file between calls), a moved stamp re-reads. 22/22 checks pass.

summary: Years outside the published window reuse the 2030 row set, which is already wrong for 2032+: the app announces 清明 on 2032-04-04 while the table says (4,5), and announces 立春 on 2033-02-03 — a winter day — exactly the date the regression pins as evidence that reuse is harmless.
evidence: Lines 96-100: `private static func schedule(for year: Int) -> [(Int, Int)] { let clamped = min(2030, max(2026, year)); return published[clamped] ?? published[2026]! }` — every year >= 2031 silently reads the 2030 rows. The header (lines 8-14) justifies this with "Dates for 2026–2030 come from the Hong Kong Observatory" and "Outside the table the nearest year is reused: a one-day drift cannot move a season". I re-derived every term with the NOAA low-precision apparent solar longitude (l = 285 + 15k, the same family `SkyAstronomy.snapshot` uses) and cross-validated the solver against all 120 committed 2026-2030 rows: 0 mismatches. Then: 2031 雨水/惊蛰/春分/立夏/芒种/立秋/白露 are all one day later than the reused 2030 row; 2032 清明 crossing = 2032-04-04 13:19 CST while the table row 7 is (4,5); 2033 立春 crossing = 2033-02-03 20:41 CST while the table row 2 is (2,4); 2032 and 2036 have 11 wrong rows each. `Tests/solar-term-regressions.py:76-77` asserts `SolarTerm.term(on: date("2033-02-04"), calendar:) == .springBegins` and calls it "Outside the table the nearest published year is reused" — with the real 2033 crossing on 02-03 20:41, that assertion encodes the defect rather than catching it. The same clamp also sends every pre-2026 date to the 2026 rows (a 2025-01-04 minute reads as 小寒). `published[2026]!` is unreachable: 2026 is always a key and `clamped` is in [2026, 2030].
failure: On 2032-04-04 (any timezone) `SolarTerm.term` returns `.brightAndClear` although the true crossing is 2032-04-04 13:19 CST, so the greeting card prints 清明 verse on an ordinary 4 April for ~13 h beforehand; on 2033-02-03 it prints 立春 (and `season(on:)` returns `.spring`) through the last evening of winter. The failure is silent, clock-stable and gets worse each year past 2030, and the fixture that should catch it sits on a date that passes either way.
fix: Replace the clamp with one of: (a) extend `published` by the 2031-2036 HKO rows (the four-year cadence already alternates, so ~24 rows per year), or (b) keep the table only as cache and compute the day from the crossing longitude already trusted elsewhere — solve l = 285+15k with the same low-precision Sun and take the civil day at the table's zone. At minimum, when `year` falls outside the published range, add a decade lower table or drop `?? published[2026]!` and document the clamped years as approximate. Extend the regression to every year the table claims to serve, and change the beyond-window probe to a year whose real term day differs from the reused row (e.g. assert 立春 on 2033-02-03 once the table is right) so it no longer passes on the reused row by construction.
verdict_note: The HKO series was fetched through 2036 and the table extended to match (2026–2036, 2027–2030 verified identical to the rows already committed); `schedule` clamps to the new edge. `solar-term-regressions.py` now checks all 24 terms × 11 years against the HKO transcription, and pins 2033-02-03 as 立春 — the day the 2030 row's reuse got wrong.

evidence: StreamAssembler.swift:147-163 picks the shape per event: subsetHit = positive(inputDetails cached_tokens, promptDetails cached_tokens, usage prompt_cache_hit_tokens); siblingRead = positive(usage cache_read_input_tokens); then `if let subsetHit { ... setPrompt(total: prompt, includesCacheRead: true) } else if siblingRead != nil || siblingWrite != nil { ... setPrompt(total: prompt, includesCacheRead: false) } else { setPrompt(total: prompt, includesCacheRead: true) }`. setPrompt (201-209) only rewrites promptTotal/promptIncludesCacheRead when total != nil, then recomputes `input = max(0, total - hit)` with `hit = promptIncludesCacheRead ? (cacheRead ?? 0) : 0`. I compiled this exact type out of the file and ran it: event 1 {input_tokens:1000, output_tokens:10, cache_read_input_tokens:9000, cache_creation_input_tokens:500} -> input=1000 read=9000 total=10510; event 2 {input_tokens:1000, output_tokens:300} -> input=0 read=9000 total=9800 (true fresh input 1000).
failure: An Anthropic-shaped relay that sends the cache fields on message_start but a plain input_tokens on message_delta, or any repeated usage block lacking the cache fields, leaves promptIncludesCacheRead true with a stale cacheRead of 9000, so input is re-derived as max(0, 1000 - 9000) = 0. The Traffic inspector and the access-log 入 column show 0 fresh input where the truth is 1000, and the four-bucket total drops from 10510 to 9800, so the token columns and downstream pricing silently disagree with the upstream.
fix: Latch the shape once per stream: in setPrompt keep the remembered flag unless this event actually carried a cache-shaped signal (only assign promptIncludesCacheRead when hadCacheSignal), or reset promptIncludesCacheRead to the current event's shape whenever no cache field was present.
summary: applyResponses re-decides the prompt shape on every event, so a later event with no cache fields keeps the stale includes-cache flag and zeroes the fresh-input bucket

evidence: ProxyCaptureStore.swift:1143-1148 calls tokenIfNeeded on every streamed event, computing assembler.content.count + assembler.reasoning.count before and after each append (lines 1072, 1080, 1088). String.count on a native Swift string is O(n): measured 10.3 us at 10 KB, 103 us at 100 KB, 1048 us at 1 MB. A stand-in of the same shape measured 300 KB streamed in 30-char chunks at 4 ms without the counts vs 3366 ms with them, and 1 MB at 11 ms vs 36 s. Separately, pendingLive[id] = CaptureLive(content: assembler.content, ...) at line 294 and streams.live[id] = live alias the buffer, so each later content += is a definite full copy: the same harness measured 27 ms vs an ideal 4 ms for a 200 KB stream at 4-char deltas.

summary: Compaction of the claims ledger advances `lines` to `ledger.count` even when the atomic rewrite fails, so subsequent appends never trigger compaction again and the file grows without bound
evidence: L154-160: `if lines * 2 > ledger.count + 4096 { let compacted = encode(ledger.keys.sorted().map { Claim(id: $0, owner: ledger[$0]!) }, []); if (try? Data(compacted.utf8).write(to: FilePaths.usageClaimsJSONL, options: .atomic)) != nil { lines = ledger.count }; return }`. The file exists on this machine at ~/Library/Application Support/ClaudeBar/logs/usage-claims.jsonl at 32,064,895 bytes / 154,548 lines (wc -l), and it is fully id-sorted (checked every line: 0 out-of-order ids), i.e. compaction has already run here. With `lines = ledger.count` inside the `if`, any failure of the atomic write (disk full, quota, permission repair in flight — the write is the app's own log dir, not a read the guard covers) leaves `lines` at the old value only when the rewrite fails... but the rewrite CREATES the file: a transcript corpus whose ids number near 4,096 triggers `lines*2 > ledger.count+4096` with its FIRST pass (e.g. a fresh install with 4,000 records: lines=0, 0 > 8096 is false, so the first store appends; a reset plus fresh corpus reaches lines=0 first too). The unrecoverable path is narrower and real: after a compaction succeeds, `lines = ledger.count == 0` when the file was deleted/reset, then every later append leaves `lines` at the tombstone/appended count, never the on-disk line count.
failure: A ledger whose in-memory state was reset while the on-disk file survived (or any atomic-write failure inside the compaction branch) leaves `lines` diverged from the real line count; the file then only ever grows by appends and is never rewritten, ending at the multi-MB whole-file read this machine already shows on every process start. The compaction path is setup-free to break because `lines` is only ever incremented by `appended.count + tombstones.count`, never by the actual bytes appended by another writer or by a pre-existing file after `reset()`.
fix: Set `lines = ledger.count` only after a verified write: capture the byte count, and on failure leave `lines` unchanged (or recompute `lines` from the file size on the next `loadLocked`).
verdict_note: c54d6c7: lines advanced only by a verified write; failed compaction falls through to append

summary: Every `owner(of:)` on a cold cache reads the whole claims file with `Data(contentsOf:)` and decodes every line, synchronously, on the calling index pass; a deleted/renamed transcript before the first pass makes that state unbounded
evidence: L175-179: `private static func loadLocked() { guard !loaded else { return }; loaded = true; guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: FilePaths.usageClaimsJSONL) else { return } }` then a per-line `JSONDecoder().decode`. All entry points (`owner`, `owned`, `record`, `begin`) take `lock` then call `loadLocked()`. The file is 32 MB / 154,548 lines on this machine (measured).
failure: First `UsageClaims.owner(of:)` of a pass reads and JSON-decodes 154k lines while holding `UsageClaims.lock`; `UsageIndex.updateIndex()` calls this once per candidate file that actually re-parses, so in a temp/.dev corpus (or a user with no ledger yet) the whole 32 MB corpus file is parsed one-time. The cost is invisible in the SQLite path thread, but any pass that re-parses many Claude files pays the decode under the lock. The failure is a one-time stall proportional to the ledger, not to changed bytes.
fix: Keep a compact index on disk (or read the ledger once at pass start and pass it into the pass), and drop the `guard !loaded` full parse from `owner(of:)`'s per-id path.
verdict_note: Code: the claims file's load is now a byte scanner (`UsageClaims.fastClaim`) with a `JSONDecoder` fallback for any line that is not exactly the shape `flushLocked` writes — same key order, same `\/`-only escaping, no trailing bytes, valid UTF-8. Anything else (swapped keys, whitespace, extra keys, `\uXXXX` or `\"` escapes, junk tail, truncated line) returns nil and is decoded by the real decoder, so the scanner can only be a faster route to the same answer. Measured on this machine's real ledger (37 MB / 178,883 lines): the full load falls from 558–584 ms to 362–376 ms (three runs each, old path reconstructed beside the new), and it remains a one-time cost per process — `guard !loaded` means `owner(of:)` pays the load once, then a dictionary lookup (measured 8.1 ms for 100k lookups ≈ 81 ns each), so the review's 'every owner(of:) reads the whole file' describes only the first call, which runs on the index pass's background thread (ProviderStore.refreshUsage's Task.detached). The review's suggested on-disk index was considered and rejected in this shape: a second on-disk artifact now needs invalidation, compaction timing and a recovery rule for divergence, to save part of a one-time background read the scanner already cut by ~35%. Tests/usage-index-regressions.py diffs the two routes line-by-line on a 20k-id generated ledger plus 12 adversarial lines, and three mutants — keeping the backslash of `/`, eating `\"`, and dropping the end-of-line shape check — each trip it.

summary: 每个 Claude 转录的每次追加都整文件重读、重切行、全量 JSON 解析（含 UsageClaims 重算），而非像 Codex 那样只解析新增字节。
evidence: 第 764-766 行只在 mtime+size 完全相同时才跳过；第 774 行的增量分支被 `if isCodex` 限定，注释写明「Claude assistant lines can rewrite the same message.id ... only Codex is append-delta」。因此 Claude 走 811 行 `guard let data = FileManager.default.contents(atPath: file.path)` → `completeLines` → `parseClaude`（1279 行逐行 JSONSerialization）→ `claimClaude` 全量重放。实测本机语料：~/.claude/projects 共 2154 个 .jsonl / 3.7GB，其中 69 个 >5MB、7 个 >20MB，最大的 110MB / 43844 行；对 110MB 文件做同样的逐行 json.loads 实测 389ms。仍在增长的 84MB 会话（ed2cc86c...jsonl，10/6 01:22 仍在写）每次追加都会整读+整解析一遍。触发频率：ProviderStore.startUsageWatcher 的 FSEvents 回调（UsageFSWatcher 仅 0.4s debounce）→ refreshUsage(rescan: true) → updateIndex()，活跃会话写一行 assistant 记录就会走一次。
failure: 用户在长会话里持续对话 → 每次追加 assistant 行都触发对最大转录（80-110MB）的完整读盘+JSON 解析（每次 ~0.2-0.4s 后台 CPU、后台读放大到整文件），叠加每次会话面板/用量页刷新；本机这类文件有 7 个，单次爆发的后台成本从「追加几十 KB」膨胀到「数百 MB 读 + 数万行解析」。
fix: 给 Claude 保留 last-wins 语义的前提下改成尾部增量：只解析 offset 之后的新增字节，把尾部出现的 message.id 先与 `UsageClaims.owned(by: path)` 比对——无碰撞（都是新 id）则直接 addRollup；只要有一个 id 已被本文件登记（partial→final 重写或跨文件重放），才回退到现在的整文件重解析。这样常见追加从 O(文件大小) 降到 O(新增字节)，语义不变。
verdict_note: Code, in three layers. (1) The dominant cost the review did not name: `parseClaude` spent most of its time in `ISO8601DateFormatter` — measured 25.7 µs per stamp against 2.9 µs for the line's JSONSerialization — so `isoDate` now tries `fastStamp` first: a byte-level reader for exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.fff]Z`, equivalent including the formatter's truncation of fractions to milliseconds, refusing every other shape (offsets, 1-digit month, 24:00, ≥4 fractional digits, lowercase t/z) back to the formatter. On a 13 MB / 30k-line synthetic transcript of the live sessions' size class, `parseClaude` fell 3332 → 454 ms and a first index 3483 → 603 ms; on the real 139 MB live transcript, the first index is 1281 ms. (2) The review's Claude tail-append proposal, with its own guard made precise: a chunk folds additively only when none of its ids is one `UsageClaims` already books for that file; any reprint (measured: 64% of assistant lines reprint an earlier id, almost always the immediately preceding line, and 100% of the duplicate pairs are gap-1) falls through to the full reparse, whose last-wins fold is the only thing that can replace a partial's numbers with the final ones. Measured on the real transcript: a pure append pass costs 6 ms against 1236 ms for a reprint pass — and since the live stream's typical append IS a reprint of the last line, the honest headline is the fastStamp win, not the append path. (3) `fetchOfficialCodex` memoizes each rollout's official/non-official verdict on (mtime, size) from the `files` row, the same shape `fetchSessionFamilies` uses; 50 calls over 200 rollouts fell 210.6 → 25.8 ms. Tests/usage-index-regressions.py drives all three: the append/reprint/sandwich totals, a 40k-stamp fastStamp differential plus 16 adversarial shapes, and provider-rewrite/deletion invalidation of the official memo; mutants (swap month/day, +1 ms on the fraction, no memo, no id guard) each trip it.

summary: Rerun 自旋：refresh() 在 inflight 非空时只置 rerun=true 不设 loading，失败分支又不重置 note；嵌套的 refresh() 立刻被仍在飞行的旧 task 挡住再置 rerun，随后无人置回。
evidence: 867 行 `self.inflight = nil` 在 `if self.rerun { self.rerun = false; self.refresh() }` 之前（864-865 行）执行，所以嵌套 refresh() 进入 `guard inflight == nil`（808 行）时 self.inflight 仍指向正在收尾的那个 task，于是 `rerun = true; return` —— 这一轮请求从未发出，且没有任何后续触发会再消费它。同一 guard 也让 CurrentLocation 的失败回调 refreshFromCity 有时被吞：refreshFromCity(834) 同样只置 rerun 不置 loading。
failure: 用户在天气请求在飞行中改城市（SettingsView 538/547 行 commitWeatherCity/commitAmapKey 调 WeatherStore.refresh()）或一次定位回调与一轮定时刷新重叠 → 外层 guard 置 rerun=true 返回，flight 结束后的嵌套 refresh() 只把 rerun 置回 true，fetch 一次都没跑 → 卡片永久停在旧城市的读数，直到下一次 15 分钟定时或手动点击才恢复。

summary: navigationRequest 在 willSet 投递时被清除，guard 永远失败，被路由过的请求留在 store 上，下次窗口重建时重放
evidence: MainWindowView.swift:89-91 `.onReceive(providerStore.$navigationRequest.compactMap { $0 }) { request in route(request) }`；route 同步调用 `providerStore.clearNavigation(request)`（:120）。`clearNavigation` 的定义是 `guard navigationRequest == taken else { return }`（ProviderStore.swift:205-207），而 `@Published` 在 willSet 里投递：payload 是新值、属性仍hold旧值——仓库自己两处写明这一点（TrafficView.swift:410-411 “`$live` emits in `willSet`, when the property still holds the previous batch”；ProxyLogView.swift:97 “@Published emits before assignment”）。因此 onReceive 回调里 `providerStore.navigationRequest` 还是上一个请求（或 nil），`nil/old == taken` 不成立，clear 直接 return，请求在赋值落地后永久留在 store 里。ProviderStore.swift:203-204 的注释恰恰承诺 “a later reopen (or a revisit of the page) cannot replay it”。
failure: 点击 popup「管理模型」（`.editor(.providers)`）→ 请求被路由但没被清除 → 用户切到别的页并关闭主窗口 → 从 Dock 图标或 popup「打开主窗口」重开（`showWindow()`，不带目的地）→ `MainWindowController.installContent` 新建 NSHostingView，`@Published` 把陈旧请求重放给新订阅者 → 窗口跳到「模型」页并且 ProvidersView 的 provider 编辑弹窗自行弹出；纯 `.page` 请求（帮助/VPN）则让重开落到上次中继的页而不是 `lastPage` 记住的页。

[])) { let rows = await Task.detached(priority: .utility) { UsageIndex.fetchOfficialCodex(in: interval) }.value ... }` — the task id embeds the whole codex model array, so every publish with changed tokens restarts it. FileHandle(forReadingFrom: ...); let header = try? handle.read(upToCount: 65_536); try? handle.close(); guard header, UsageProviderAttribution.isOfficialCodex(metadata: header) ... }` — one open + 64 KiB read per transcript per call, with no header cache. UsageFSWatcher debounces at 0.4 s (UsageFSWatcher.swift:87) and ProviderStore.swift:1234 calls refreshUsage(rescan: true) on every fire, so during an active Codex session this runs ~2.5x/s. The same file already keeps exactly the cache this loop lacks: UsageIndex.swift:396-415 memoizes a SessionHeader keyed by (path, mtime, size) for fetchSessionFamilies.
failure: A month window containing ~200 Codex rollout files, with one session writing: each FSEvents-driven republish triggers a detached scan of all 200 files → ~200 opens + ~12.8 MB of header reads per pass, several passes per second, for a verdict that only depends on each file's first line (mtime/size already in `files`/`rollup` metadata).
fix: Memoize the official/non-official verdict per path keyed on (mtime, size) — same shape as `sessionHeaders` in fetchSessionFamilies — or key the view task on the interval alone and refetch only when `usageIndexDidRefresh` fires, so transcript churn no longer re-walks headers.
verdict_note: Same change as finding 59's third layer (they are two views of one loop): `fetchOfficialCodex` no longer reads a header per rollout per call. The verdict is memoized per path on the (mtime, size) already carried by the file's `files` row — the identical key `fetchSessionFamilies` uses for its `sessionHeaders` — with the SQL extended to join `files` for those two columns. Measured with 200 synthetic openai rollouts: 50 repeated calls fell from 210.6 ms to 25.8 ms (4.21 → 0.52 ms per call), i.e. the per-call cost is now the SQL query, not 200 file opens. A rewritten provider flips the verdict on the next call (asserted), a deleted rollout drops it (asserted, plus the byPath filter keeps the memo bounded), and `reloadPersistence` clears it like every other per-process cache. The view-side half of the review's fix (re-keying the UsageView task) was not needed once the scan itself is O(1) per rollout: the task still restarts on publish, but a restart now costs one query.

summary: dismiss() 只清 query，不清空 filtered/selection；面板关闭后 refreshItems() 的守卫(get isPresented)使旧 @State 一直存活到下两次失效信号，且选中行会继续引用已退出的会话。
evidence: dismiss() 里只有 `query = ""`（第 280–285 行），items/filtered/selection 保持关闭那一刻的值。面板由 MainWindowView 常驻 overlay 持有（MainWindowView.swift:99 `if showCommandPalette { CommandPalette(...) }`，同一身份），视图不随关闭销毁。下次 onReceive 失效（第 126–129 行）先 `guard isPresented else { return }`，因此不刷新；下一次开启 onAppear 顺序是 `searchFocused = true` 然后 `refreshItems(reselect: true)`（第 116–119 行），ViewModel 更新在 onAppear 之后，所以首个渲染帧用的是上次会话留下的 filtered/selection，之后才被换成新列表。
failure: 打开面板 → 搜索并停止在会话 A 的选中行（selection = "claude:1234"）→ dismissed → 该会话退出（PID 可能被系统复用）→ 再次按 ⌘K：首帧仍显示上次的过滤列表并把 A 高亮为当前选中项；此时立即按回车会在新列表尚未生效前触发旧条目（或旧 PID）。
fix: 在 dismiss() 中一并重置派生状态：`query = ""` 后加 `filtered = []; selection = nil`（或让 buildItems 后的 refreshResults 一定执行，并在 onAppear 里先赋 items/filtered 再设 searchFocused）。
verdict_note: Measured with an `NSHostingView` probe of `MainWindowView`'s exact wiring (one `@State` fact mirrored through `withAnimation`, `if isPresented` gating the palette): a close→re-open gap matrix [0, 20, 50, 80, 120, 160, 500] ms shows the panel unmounts only past the fade — every gap under 500 ms **re-adopts the instance silently**: no `onDisappear`, no re-mount, `onAppear` never runs again. So the finding's premise is real but its path was wrong: the hazard is not 'the next open's first frame' for a remounted palette (that path is clean), it is the re-adopted instance whose `filtered` still holds the previous search's rows while `dismiss()` has already cleared the query box they were filtered against — drawing a subset under an empty box, firing on a return the user cannot see a reason for. Code: added `.onChange(of: isPresented)` in `body` — open edge only — that restores focus and calls `refreshItems(reselect: true)`; the mount path keeps its own `onAppear`. `dismiss()` deliberately still touches only the query (clearing `filtered` there wipes the list under the fade-out's last frame), with the reasoning recorded at the site. Test: new suite `command-palette-reopen` (registered in `make test`) asserts both source shape (both refresh points, open-edge guard, dismiss touches only the query) and the behaviour: the gap matrix above, with a `staleFrames == 0` invariant. Mutants: removing the reopen refresh fails the source section; adding `filtered = []` to `dismiss` fails the fade-out assertion.

summary: MCP child processes are only SIGTERM'd; there is no grace-period SIGKILL, and the pipe reader is detached before the signal, so a server that ignores SIGTERM stays alive with an undrained pipe.
evidence: MCPToolDiscovery.swift:45-49 `func stop() { ... if let process, process.isRunning { process.terminate() } ... }` (SIGTERM only), while the `defer` at 204-206 has already run `output.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = nil` before `session.stop()`. The codebase's own precedent for an owned child is FeishuCLI.swift:71-78: `process.terminate()` then a 2 s `asyncAfter` that escalates to `kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)`.
failure: A JVM/npx-wrapped MCP server that traps or ignores SIGTERM keeps running after the connector sheet is dismissed. Nothing drains its stdout any more, so once it writes past the 64 KB pipe buffer it blocks in `write` and never exits. Tests/backend-performance-regressions.py:135-150 asserts the pid dies after cancel, but the mock child exits on SIGTERM, so this arm is untested.
fix: In `stop()`, after `process.terminate()` schedule a 2 s check on `cancellationQueue` that calls `kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)` if it is still running (copy FeishuCLI.swift:71-78).

summary: The SSE fallback materialises the entire (up to 2 MB) response as a String and re-serialises every `data:` line to find the payload, and all of this parsing runs on the presenter's actor (the connector sheet's MainActor task).
evidence: MCPToolDiscovery.swift:143 `guard data.count < 2_000_000`, then 146 `let text = String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)` and 147-151 `for line in text.components(separatedBy: .newlines) where line.hasPrefix("data:") { ... Data(payload.utf8) ... JSONSerialization.jsonObject(...) }`. The direct path (144) fails for any `text/event-stream` reply, which is the normal MCP streamable-HTTP shape given the `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` header at line 135. Caller: ConnectorDetailSheet.swift:248 `let discovered = try await MCPToolDiscovery.list(...)` inside SwiftUI `.task` (ConnectorDetailSheet.swift:90-92), i.e. the main actor; `listHTTP` is a plain static func with no detached hop.
failure: Every tool-list read allocates a second full copy of the body (~1x-2x the payload) plus one `Data`/`JSONSerialization` per SSE line, and the whole parse executes on the main actor while the sheet renders — a 1 MB `tools/list` reply produces a visible hitch in the popover, where splitting*2 the raw Data on 0x0A and decoding only the candidate line would be one pass and no String copy.
fix: Iterate `data.split(separator: 0x0A)`, test the `data:` prefix on the bytes, and decode only candidate lines; wrap the parse (`JSONSerialization` + line scan) in `Task.detached(priority: .utility)` so it leaves the caller's actor.

summary: Only the stdio transport has a regression; the whole HTTP/SSE branch (session header, notification, pagination, SSE line parsing) is untested.
evidence: `grep -rn "listHTTP|postHTTP|Mcp-Session-Id" Tests` returns nothing; Tests/backend-performance-regressions.py:20-21 includes MCPToolDiscovery.swift in the compiled slice but the mock at 190-210 speaks newline-delimited JSON over stdin/stdout only, and its `nextCursor` fixture (line 202) drives the stdio pagination loop.
failure: The SSE fallback at MCPToolDiscovery.swift:147-151 (the per-line `Data(payload.utf8)` re-encode and the id check) and the 500-tool/10-page caps at 111-124 and 231-244 can break silently; a remote MCP server returning `text/event-stream` would surface only as a user-visible 无法读取的工具列表.
fix: Extend the existing temp-file mock into an HTTP mode: a tiny local HTTP server (or a `URLProtocol` stub spliced into the same harness) that answers `initialize`/`tools/list` as `data:`-framed SSE with a `Mcp-Session-Id`, and assert pagination, `nextCursor` handling and the SSE id match.

summary: A single malformed model row makes the whole `[ModelConfig]` decode fail, and the provider silently ends up with an empty `models` array that the next save persists.
evidence: Provider.swift:108-110 `if let newModels = try? c.decode([ModelConfig].self, forKey: .models) { models = newModels } else if let oldModelNames = try? c.decode([String].self, forKey: .models) { ... } else { models = [] }`. `ModelConfig.init(from:)` at Provider.swift:50 does `name = try c.decode(String.self, forKey: .name)`, which throws for one row missing/typed-wrong `name`; the `try?` is around the array, so one bad element discards all of them. `saveProviders()` (ProviderStore.swift:755-766) then writes the empty list back.
failure: A hand-edited `claude-bar-providers.json` where one model object lacks `"name"` (or an external tool writes a numeric name) -> that vendor loads with `models == []` (not just the one row), `ProviderCardState.isReady` (ProviderControls.swift:20-27) reports 待完善, activation writes an empty `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, and the next save makes the loss permanent.
fix: Decode element-wise: `let raw = try c.decodeIfPresent([FailableModelConfig].self, forKey: .models)` with a wrapper whose `init(from:)` does `try? ModelConfig(from: decoder)`, or decode into `[AnyCodable]` and `compactMap`.

summary: Two different Claude<->Codex base-URL mappings exist for the same conversion: ProviderBridge rewrites the URL (catalogue lookup, then per-host tables, then generic rules), while ProviderProfileSync copies the source URL verbatim for vendors with no catalogue entry.
evidence: ProviderBridge.swift:73-89 `toClaude` sets `baseURL: anthropicCompatibleURL(source.baseURL)` and line 49-71 `toCodex` sets `baseURL: openaiCompatibleURL(source.baseURL)`. The other conversion path is ProviderProfileSync.swift:236-243 `makeClaude` / 227-234 `makeCodex`, which call `fillClaude`/`fillCodex`; ProviderProfileSync.swift:276-280 `if creating, let endpoint = entry?.claude { twin.baseURL = endpoint.baseURL } else if creating { twin.baseURL = source.baseURL }`. Both run on the same rows on the same profileID (ProviderBridge.swift:87 `profileID: source.profileID`).
failure: A custom (non-catalogue) Codex relay saved as `https://relay.example/v1` already has a Claude twin at `https://relay.example/v1` (created by ProviderProfileSync in the background). The user taps 导入 Claude (ProvidersView.swift:199): `toClaude` -> `anthropicCompatibleURL` hits the rule at ProviderBridge.swift:266-272 (`URL(string:s).path == "/v1"` -> drop the path) and writes a second Claude row at `https://relay.example` for the same profileID. Two rows, same profile, different upstream: whichever row is activated last decides what settings.json contains, and the two clients stop agreeing on the endpoint.
fix: Make `toCodex`/`toClaude` call the same rule the sync path uses: `catalogEntry?.codex?.baseURL ?? source.baseURL` (sync's behaviour), i.e. delete the host tables in `openaiCompatibleURL`/`anthropicCompatibleURL` and keep only `ProviderCatalogEntry.matching(baseURL:)?.codex/.claude`.

summary: Import overwrites the destination provider's key/URL on a name-only match, while the live sync path deliberately only fills empty keys — the two rules for the same pair of rows disagree.
evidence: ProviderBridge.swift:121-129 `if let idx = existing.firstIndex(where: { matches($0, incoming) }) { ... if !incoming.apiKey.isEmpty { existing[idx].apiKey = incoming.apiKey } ... }` and the Claude twin at 145-153. `matches` (281-291) returns true on `name.caseInsensitiveCompare == .orderedSame` alone, before any URL comparison. The other direction, ProviderProfileSync.swift:109-112: `if claudeKey.isEmpty, !codexKey.isEmpty { claude.authToken = codexKey }` / `if codexKey.isEmpty, !claudeKey.isEmpty { codex.apiKey = claudeKey }` — fill-only.
failure: A Codex row named "OpenRouter" pointing at relay A (key K1) and a Claude row named "OpenRouter" pointing at relay B (key K2). Tapping 导入 Claude overwrites the Claude row's K2 with K1 without any URL match, silently re-pointing a working vendor at another account's key. ProviderProfileSync, running on the same rows, would never do that.
fix: Gate the overwrite on identity, not just name: `if !incoming.apiKey.isEmpty, normalizeURL(existing[idx].baseURL) == normalizeURL(incoming.baseURL) { ... }` (or only assign when the destination key is empty, matching ProviderProfileSync:109-112).

summary: No regression compiles any of the Claude<->Codex conversion helpers, so the URL/key drift above cannot be caught by the test suite.
evidence: `grep -rn "codexModel(|claudeModel(|stripClaudeModelSuffix|claudeModelName|openaiCompatibleURL|anthropicCompatibleURL" Tests` returns only Tests/proxy-upstream-regressions.py:60 (the string `"test-model[1M]"`). Tests/proxy-upstream-regressions.py:15-18 explicitly cuts the Disk section out of ProviderBridge.swift and only exercises `toCodex` through `resolvedThirdPartyOpenAI`; `toClaude` is never executed anywhere (Tests/migration_bridge_harness.py:135 cuts ProviderCatalog at `struct ProviderSetupDraft`).
failure: Finding 1's divergence (custom relay `https://relay.example/v1` -> `https://relay.example` via import vs verbatim via sync) and the `[1M]`/suffix mapping can regress without any test failing; the existing harness proves only that `stripClaudeModelSuffix` runs somewhere in the fallback path.
fix: Add a slice harness in the style of Tests/local-endpoint-regressions.py that compiles ProviderBridge.swift + Provider.swift + CodexProvider.swift and asserts: toCodex/toClaude round-trip of `glm-5.2[1M]` (name without suffix, `[1M]` restored for >=1M windows) and that an uncatalogued `https://relay.example/v1` maps to the same URL on both paths.

summary: A per-request proxy hot path linearly scans all 23 catalogue entries and rebuilds two URLComponents per entry, on every Responses request, when the answer is fixed at compile time.
evidence: ProviderCatalog.swift:251-256 `static func supportsNativeResponses(baseURL: String) -> Bool { all.contains { entry in guard let endpoint = entry.codex, endpoint.wireAPI == "responses" else { return false }; return identityURL(endpoint.baseURL) == identityURL(baseURL) } }`, with `identityURL` (174-190) constructing `URLComponents`, trimming, and rebuilding a String. Callers: CodexProxyServer.swift:402 `CodexProxyTransform.shouldBridgeToChat(baseURL:wireAPI:model:)` (per proxied OpenAI request) and CodexProviderStore.swift:108 (per provider on load).
failure: Every Responses-dialect request that is not already `wireAPI == chat` pays up to 23 iterations and up to 46 `URLComponents` parses + 23 String builds to answer a constant question; a streaming turn makes several such requests per second, so the same 46 parses repeat per request instead of once per process.
fix: Precompute next to `endpointIndex` (160-168): `private static let nativeResponsesURLs: Set<String> = Set(all.compactMap { $0.codex }.filter { $0.wireAPI == "responses" }.map { identityURL($0.baseURL) })` and return `nativeResponsesURLs.contains(identityURL(baseURL))`.

summary: 5 秒轮询只能读到 ~90 秒前的日志快照：store 的重建条件被 90 秒重叠窗口反向钳住，耳机电量更新最多滞后约 95 秒（平均约 47 秒），与 5 秒心跳和 180 秒 isStale 的承诺不符。
evidence: 轮询窗口：line 294 `let since = lastLogReadAt.map { max(fullWindow, $0.addingTimeInterval(-90)) } ?? fullWindow`，每次成功轮询把 lastLogReadAt 设为 now（line 298）。重建门：line 611 `if let held = store, let built = storeBuiltAt, since <= built {` … line 622 `storeBuiltAt = Date()`。因为 since = lastLogReadAt-90，重建后约 90 秒内 since 恒 ≤ built，于是整个窗口都走复用分支；而 600-607 行注释自己确认『entries written after OSLogStore.local() returned are invisible to it』，Tests/audio-accessory-regressions.py:119-121 也用 `frozen == baseline` 把这个快照语义锁死了。定时器周期见 line 226 `t.schedule(deadline: .now(), repeating: 5.0, leeway: .seconds(1))`。
failure: 稳态、日志源健康、面板可见：t0 建 store；t0+5…t0+95 每个 5 秒 tick 都复用同一快照，期间写入的 CBPowerSource/BatteryCenter 行（如 56%→55%、入盒充电）对查询不可见；直到第 19 次 tick（since 超过 built）才重建并批量补上，最坏 ~95 秒、平均 ~47 秒才显示。对比之下 60 秒一次的 system_profiler（line 325-333，TTL 30/300 秒）会掩盖拓扑和粗粒度电量，因此表象是『偶尔跳变』而不是明显卡死，更难定位。
fix: 把重建触发与查询窗口解耦：保留 90 秒重叠用于捞晚写条目，但复用条件加一个年龄上限，例如 `if let held = store, let built = storeBuiltAt, since <= built, Date().timeIntervalSince(built) < 10 {`（并在超龄时走重建分支）。代价从『每 ~95 秒 0.65 秒建店 + 18×0.15 秒复用』变成『每 10 秒 0.65 秒建店』，把可见新鲜度从 ≤95 秒压到 ≤10 秒，utility 队列占用仍在个位数百分比（数字取自本文件 604-607 行自述的实测）。

summary: `Server`'s single mutable `deadline` becomes a cumulative budget for every `thread/list` page, so a scan that outlives it returns a short fork list — and the identical page loop is written twice.
evidence: Line 125 computes `let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(timeout)` (30 s by default, line 88) and `Server` stores it once (line 160); every `call` passes the same value: `try collector.response(id: id, until: deadline)` (line 178). `threadIds(forkedFrom:)` makes up to 20 `thread/list` calls per `archived` flag with `limit: 200` (lines 202-213), i.e. up to 40 requests sharing one fixed deadline. `JSONLineCollector.response` gives each caller the full budget (it `break`s only when `Date() < deadline` fails, line 52/62), so `MCPToolDiscovery.listSync` (lines 219-237) can afford, per request, what `CodexAppServerClient` spreads across a whole scan. `removed` (line 90) is discarded one frame up: `_ = try? CodexAppServerClient.remove(threadId: session.sessionId)` at ProviderStore.swift:143, and `Removal` has no other reader anywhere in Sources.
failure: A Codex install with enough threads to page past (or a slow first page) → the deadline expires mid-scan, `_ = try server.call(...)` drops the error, `threadIds(forkedFrom:)` returns the forks found so far (or none), `thread/delete` on the target hits `forked history still references it`, and the code falls back to `thread/archive` while the UI re-scans at line 149 and shows the thread still present. The user's cleanup silently degrades and the `Removal.archived` message exists only to say so — to nobody.
fix: Give each `call` its own budget as `MCPToolDiscovery` does (`until: Date().addingTimeInterval(requestTimeout)` inside `Server.call`) so a slow single page cannot eat the scan; and thread the returned `Removal` out of `ProviderStore.cleanUpExternalSession` (ProviderStore.swift:143) so the `.archived` case is reported rather than dropped.

summary: A model row whose `totalCents` is missing or unparsable silently books $0 for that model, and the window total then under-reports with no signal even though the payload carries its own totals to check against.
evidence: `parseAggregated` defaults the money field: `costCents: CursorUsageFetcher.number(entry["totalCents"]) ?? 0` (line 187), and `Snapshot.totalCents`/the UI then just sum rows (`var totalCents: Double { rows.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.costCents } }`, line 88). The captured live payload in Tests/fixtures/cursor-ledger-probe.swift carries `"totalCostCents":5093.26252` (plus `totalInputTokens` etc.) alongside the per-row figures, and nothing in the file ever reads it. The zero also reaches the tile: `ParserDoc`'s guard is bypassed in production — UsageView.swift:262 does `ModelPricing.Cost(usd: $0.costCents / 100)` inline, so a 0-cent row renders 「Cursor 实扣 $0.00」 via `settlementRow` (UsageModelCard.swift:186-214), while the tested helper `CursorLedger.cost(cents:)` (lines 299-302) returns nil for `cents <= 0` and the fixture asserts `CursorLedger.cost(cents: 0) == nil` (“no charge is no figure, not $0.00”).
failure: Cursor renames/moves the money key (or one model's entry arrives with a non-numeric `totalCents`, e.g. a stringified `"0"` that parses but is wrong): the model is displayed as charged $0.00 and the window total is silently short by that row — the same class of confidently-wrong number as the documented $53.51-vs-$57.72 aggregate/ledger gap, but with no failure at all (the read is recorded as a success).
fix: Read `root["totalCostCents"]` in `parseAggregated` and, when the per-row sum differs by more than a cent, return nil (a failed window) rather than a short total; and replace the inline `Cost(usd: $0.costCents / 100)` in UsageView.swift:262 with the already-tested `CursorLedger.cost(cents:)` so a zero/missing charge suppresses the 实扣 row instead of printing $0.00.

summary: The ledger reading is cached by window only; switching Cursor accounts leaves the previous account's per-model charges on screen for up to 6 hours because nothing identifies whose money it is.
evidence: refresh's freshness gate only compares the window: `if !isStale(for: plan.window), let fetchedAt, Date().timeIntervalSince(fetchedAt) < Self.freshWindow { return }` (lines 129-131), and the persisted cache carries no account key — `private struct Stored { var rows: [CursorLedger.Row]; var windowStart: Date; var windowEnd: Date; var truncated: Bool; var at: Date }` (lines 285-291). `CursorDB.readCredentials()` is re-read inside every probe (line 191-193) and returns `subject` (CursorDB.swift:102), but the reader (`CursorLedgerReader.read`, lines 186-208) uses only `credentials.accessToken` and discards `subject`.
failure: User signs into a second Cursor account (or Cursor rotates to a different workspace/plan) while the app keeps running, then opens 用量 on 当前月: the window (calendar month) is byte-identical, `fetchedAt` is < 6 h old and the reading is not stale, so `refresh` returns without any network read and `UsageView`/`CursorTokenUsageCard` keep rendering the previous account's per-model 实扣 money under the current window label. Same after relaunch, because `init` rehydrates `fetchedAt` from `cursor-ledger.json` (lines 65-75).
fix: Store the credential subject used for the read (in `Stored` and in the store's live state) and treat a change as stale: in `refresh`, compare `<current subject>` (from the same `readCredentials()` the reader already performs, hoisted before the guards) with the stored one and bypass the freshness/coalescing early returns when they differ.

summary: Sub-composer rows whose value JSON lacks `composerId` take the `?? ""` fallback, get an impossible transcript path, and two of them under one parent collide in a ForEach keyed by composerId.
evidence: The parent query reads the id from the column — `let composerId = CursorDB.cString(stmt, 0)` (line 217) — while `fetchSubagents` selects only `value, checkpointAt` (line 297) and recovers the id from the blob with a silent fallback: `let composerId = (obj["composerId"] as? String) ?? ""` (line 312). `CursorSubagentInfo` is `Identifiable` by that value — `var id: String { composerId }` (line 126) — and entries are appended with no dedupe: `map[parent, default: []].append(info)` (line 337). The transcript URL is then built from the empty id both as the subagent path and as the fallback: `appendingPathComponent("subagents/\(composerId).jsonl")` (line 326) and `FilePaths.cursorTranscriptURL(cwd: cwd, composerId: composerId)` (line 329), i.e. `…/agent-transcripts//.jsonl`. The regression fixture never exercises this: its `add()` always injects `"composerId": id` into the blob (Tests/cursor-turn-regressions.py).
failure: A sub-composer whose `value` blob omits `composerId` (a shape difference the file already admits exists between the two read paths) is listed with an empty `activity` and `done` status — the `scan.modifiedAt == 0` fallback also fails because its URL is `agent-transcripts/<encoded-cwd>/.jsonl` — and when two such rows share a parent, `ForEach(session.subagents)` (SessionsView.swift:626, and CursorSessionCardView via SessionsPanel) receives two elements with the same id `""`, so SwiftUI diffing produces undefined/duplicated child-agent rows while the parent's activity line counts them twice.
fix: Skip rows without an id (`guard let composerId = obj["composerId"] as? String, !composerId.isEmpty else { continue }`) and de-duplicate per parent (`if map[parent]?.contains(where: { $0.composerId == composerId }) != true`) — or read `composerId` as an extra column in the sub query the way the parent path does.

failure: Legacy fallback path (index unreadable/absent) + a rollout tree whose month directories are not zero-padded (the case the code's own comment names) + a cutoff that falls in a later month, e.g. today 2026-10-06 → cutoffYear 2026 / cutoffMonth 10. `2026/09` sorts first, 9 < 10 breaks immediately, and `2026/12`, `2026/11`, `2026/10` are never walked — the newest days of the current year's rollouts disappear from the Codex list (and from `activeExternalCount`) exactly when the index is unavailable, while older years are still walked in full (the guard `yearValue == cutoffYear` is false there, so no break). Recovering requires the index to become readable again.
fix: Drop the early `break` and only skip that one directory (`if yearValue == cutoffYear && monthValue < cutoffMonth { continue }`), or sort months numerically (`months.sorted { (Int($0) ?? -1) > (Int($1) ?? -1) }`) before the loop so the break predicate matches the iteration order. Same for the year loop, whose `.sorted().reversed()` is only accidentally correct among 4-digit names.
summary: The legacy walk's month pruning breaks on lexicographic directory order while comparing numerically, so months newer than the cutoff are skipped when month names are not zero-padded

failure: Codex is mid-turn with several rollouts changing between polls: scan A enters the row loop, misses the file cache, and reads 512 KB–24 MB per changed file with `indexLock` held; scan B (the 2.5 s/5 s poll or a manual refresh landing in the same window) blocks on `indexLock` for the whole I/O pass instead of doing its own reads, and the 10 s memo check cannot even be evaluated until A finishes — polls queue up behind file I/O rather than behind the small critical section they were locked for.
fix: Keep `indexLock` only around the memo check and the `rows`/`indexRows` read (copy `let rows = ...` inside the lock), then release it and run the `fileMeta`/`codexFields` row loop outside, as the legacy path already does.
summary: indexLock is held across the whole per-row file I/O loop (up to 24 MB of reads per changed file), so overlapping scans serialize on disk I/O and the 10 s memo can only be re-checked after the previous scan's reads finish
