summary: The IOAccelerator service list is latched forever: `primed = true` is set on the *failure* path too, so one failed `IOServiceGetMatchingServices` (or an accelerator that registers later) leaves the GPU mark at 0% for the rest of the process.
evidence: Lines 32-35: `if !primed { refreshLocked() }` — `refreshLocked` is private and this is its only call site (grep `refreshLocked` → only HardwareSensors.swift:35,77). Lines 77-92: on `IOServiceGetMatchingServices != KERN_SUCCESS` the function does `primed = true; return` with `services` empty; on success it appends matched services and also sets `primed = true`. Nothing ever resets `primed` or re-walks the registry. `reading()` then loops over an empty/stale array and returns `Reading()` (utilization 0, renderers []) forever. Call site: ProcessSampler.swift:413 on a 1-6 s cadence, feeding HostStats.gpu and cells.gpuRenderers (ResourceStrip.swift:444, HardwareDetailPanel.swift:88).
failure: First `gpuReading()` happens on the sampler queue at the first tick where a surface is visible (ProcessSampler.swift:412 `wantsDevices`). If that one call's `IOServiceGetMatchingServices` returns non-success (driver not yet matched during early launch, or a GPU that appears after a driver reload / eGPU attach), `services` stays empty and the GPU tile, its silicon cells and the load-history chart read 0% for the whole run — with no retry and no way for the user to recover except relaunching.
fix: Do not latch on the failure path: only set `primed = true` when the iterator call succeeded (lines 81-84 should leave `primed` false). Optionally re-run `refreshLocked()` when `services.isEmpty`, so a machine whose accelerator appears (or reappears) after launch starts reporting.

summary: `reading()` materialises the accelerator's entire property dictionary (26.4 KB, of which 23.9 KB is an unused `IOReportLegend` array) to read 4 numbers; measured 1.39 ms/call versus 0.019 ms/call for the single `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty`.
evidence: Lines 38-41 fetch every property via `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperties` and then use only `dict["PerformanceStatistics"]` (485 B / 11 keys) plus `dict["gpu-core-count"]` (line 52). `HardwareSensors.batteryStatus()` has the same shape at line 213: 58 properties ≈ 10.6 KB (BatteryData 2.2 KB, PortControllerInfo 3.3 KB, PowerTelemetryData 799 B — a dictionary the file's own comment at HardwareSensors.swift:253 says is deliberately unused), measured 0.287 ms vs 0.003 ms for `CurrentCapacity`. Measured on this M3 Pro with a release-style `-O` binary: full properties 1.392 ms/call vs 1.403 baseline, `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty("PerformanceStatistics")` 0.019 ms/call; both paths return the identical 11-key dictionary and `gpu-core-count` reads 18 either way. Cadence: ProcessSampler.swift:413 runs the GPU read on every tick where a surface is visible — 1 s while any session is live, 2 s with an idle resource page open, 6 s otherwise (ProcessSampler.swift:379-390) — and batteryStatus() runs on *every* tier (ProcessSampler.swift:452) plus MenuBarController's independent 8 s timer (MenuBarController.swift:107).
failure: Every foreground tick pays 1.39 ms (GPU) + 0.29 ms (battery) of IOKit property materialisation, ~98% of which is discarded; at the 1 Hz live tier that is ~1.7 ms/s of pure waste on the sampler queue, 73× and 95× the work actually needed. Because these are the two reads the sampler performs unconditionally, the waste scales with the tick rate rather than with anything the user changed.
fix: Read only what is consumed: `IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty(service, "PerformanceStatistics" as CFString, …)` and the same for `"gpu-core-count"`, and in `batteryStatus()` keep the full-props call only if a second key is genuinely needed (a single-props variant still supplies `PerformanceStatistics` for `temperature(from:)`). Measured cost drops from 1.39 ms to ~0.02 ms per tick — no behaviour change (verified equal key sets on this machine).

summary: readAnchorRequirement only matches `certificate root = H"…"`, a clause that Developer ID / Apple Development designated requirements do not contain, so both privileged helpers become uninstallable the moment the documented Developer ID path is used
evidence: Line 56-57: `let prefix = #"certificate root = H""#; guard let clause = requirement.range(of: prefix) else { return nil }`. Measured with `/usr/bin/codesign -d -r-`: the dev build has that clause (`designated => identifier "com.claudebar.app.dev" and certificate root = H"1490884595485da312da2062ef517f3e3e998448"`, and the extracted `-R=` verifies the app and both bundled helpers with exit 0), but every Developer ID app on this machine has a leaf/OU-shaped requirement with no root clause at all, e.g. `/Applications/Bionic.app` → `identifier "ai.elementlabs.bionic" and anchor apple generic and certificate 1[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.2.6] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[field.1.2.840.113635.100.6.1.13] /* exists */ and certificate leaf[subject.OU] = D65G88RHWN`; same shape for ChatGPT/Chrome/Blender/Chatbox. `Sources/build.sh:85` states "a Developer ID, when one is configured, is passed through the same variable", and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:70 / docs/RELEASING.md:27 record Developer ID + notarization as the intended release path. With no clause, `anchorRequirement()` is nil, so: BatteryHelperInstaller.installIfNeeded() returns "缺少电池辅助工具，请重新构建或安装应用。" (line 79), FanHelperInstaller.install() shows the tampering alert (lines 72-84), and `isInstalled()` (line 16 + codeIdentity line 37) can never be true, which pins BatteryChargeController.helperInstalled at false.
failure: A Developer-ID-signed (or Apple Development-signed) build of ClaudeBar, launched from /Applications → battery charge control can never be enabled (the install reports a missing/mis-signed helper) and the fan install path reports "辅助工具签名校验失败…应用包被改动过" for a correctly signed bundle, so both hardware features are dead with a wrong explanation.
fix: Parse the identity clause generically: keep the `certificate root = H"…"` shape, and when it is absent take the anchor half of the Developer-ID shape (`anchor apple generic … certificate leaf[subject.OU] = "…"`) while dropping the `identifier "…"` conjunct (the helper has its own identifier `claudebar-fanctl`/`com.claudebar.batteryctl`, so the whole DR cannot be reused verbatim).
verdict_note: Measured: codesign --verify --strict -R='certificate root = H"0000…0000"' on an ad-hoc signed binary (and an ad-hoc .app) exits 3 — an ad-hoc signature satisfies no anchor clause, so the all-zero slot is not accepted. Verified with the same parse+verify slice HelperSignature runs: an anchored app accepts its own helpers, rejects gh, rejects an ad-hoc re-sign of its own binary, and an ad-hoc app has no anchor at all (fail closed).

summary: One helper identity probe spawns four `codesign` processes serially (~40 ms measured) on `/usr/bin/codesign`'s full XPC round-trip, and the probe is re-run by several independent refresh paths.
evidence: Measured on this machine against the shipped dev helper: `codesign --verify --strict -R=…` 9.39 ms, `codesign --verify --strict --all-architectures` 7.83 ms, `codesign -d --verbose=4` 9.99 ms, `codesign -d --verbose=4 --arch <arch>` 9.60 ms — 39.97 ms for the four-process sequence (`/usr/bin/true` baseline 1.6 ms). `BatteryHelperInstaller.isInstalled()` (line 25-26, 37, 38, 39, 49) is called from `BatteryChargeController.refreshHelperAuthorization()` inside `Task.detached(priority: .utility)` (BatteryChargeController.swift:103-106) and from `resumePersistedMode()` (line 177), which runs at launch and on every persisted-mode resume; `FanHelperInstaller.isInstalled()` (FanHelperInstaller.swift:140) is re-run inside `submit()` on every rotor click (FanMonitor.swift:174) and in `start()` (line 28).
failure: Each helper-authorization refresh or fan command costs ~40 ms of process work plus however long the user stares at 授权中…; on a machine where the helper file is large the latency grows with it, and the calls repeat rather than being memoized per process (the anchor clause is the only memoized part).
fix: Collapse the four invocations to one: `codesign -d --verbose=4 --all-architectures <url>` prints one `Format=Mach-O …` line per arch and the `CDHash=` line alongside it, so the per-arch loop at line 48-53 can be dropped; better, replace the four-process small-helper path with a single `SecStaticCodeCreateWithPath` + `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity` + `SecCodeCopySigningInformation(kSecCodeInfoUnique)` run in-process, which is what these shellouts approximate.
verdict_note: Measured: codesign --verify --strict -R='certificate root = H"0000…0000"' on an ad-hoc signed binary (and an ad-hoc .app) exits 3 — an ad-hoc signature satisfies no anchor clause, so the all-zero slot is not accepted. Verified with the same parse+verify slice HelperSignature runs: an anchored app accepts its own helpers, rejects gh, rejects an ad-hoc re-sign of its own binary, and an ad-hoc app has no anchor at all (fail closed).

summary: Unifying every numeric JSON value through `Int64` makes a plain fractional number—`"usedPercent": 84.0` style payloads are the norm—collapse to 0, because the `Int64` cast is tried before the `Double` cast.
evidence: Lines 6-11: `if let number = value as? Int64 { return number }` and then the Double path at line 9. I measured the bridging on this machine with `swift -e`: `NSNumber(value: 1.9) as? Int64` is `nil` (a fractional NSNumber does not bridge to the integer type) while `NSNumber(value: 1.9) as? Double` is `1.9`; `JSONSerialization` returns `__NSCFNumber` for both `1.9` and `1e300`. `CodexQuotaFetcher.parseWindow` reads the duration through this path: `let minutes = JSONCoerce.intVal(window["windowDurationMins"])` (CodexQuotaFetcher.swift:427), and the 5-hour window is 300 (integer) while the weekly window's duration arrives as a number that can be fractional in Codex's own JSON. Bool values are the other asymmetry: `NSNumber(value: true)` bridges to both `Int` and `Int64` (measured), so a `"total_tokens": true` typo silently becomes 1 instead of being ignored.
failure: A Codex `rateLimits` payload whose `windowDurationMins` is `10080.0` (or any fractional form) → `int64Val` falls through `Int64`/`Int`/`String`, hits `value as? Double`, and returns `Int64(10080.0)`, which is fine — but any value that is neither representable nor a Double, e.g. `10080.5`, returns 0 → `label(forMinutes:)` renders the weekly allowance chip as the 0-minute label, i.e. a Codex window silently mislabelled rather than rejected; worse, `VpnManager`'s `JSONCoerce.intVal(h["delay"])` (VpnManager.swift:1007) turns a fractional latency into 0 ms = 「最快」.
fix: Try the `Double`/`NSNumber` path before (or as a fallback to) `Int64`, e.g. `if let number = value as? Double, number.isFinite { return Int64(number.rounded()) }` placed before the Int casts, and reject `Bool` explicitly (`if value is Bool { return 0 }`) before the conditional casts.
verdict_note: Verified in the 2026-10-07 recheck: the Double fallback (JSONCoerce.swift:9-11) converts fractionals before returning, so the described 10080.5→0 loss cannot occur.

summary: The 1 MiB overflow guard drops the entire buffered payload and leaves the caller waiting for a reply that was already discarded, so a single large thread/list answer is parsed as a vanished child.
evidence: Line 34-35: `if buffer.count > 1_048_576 { buffer.removeAll(); lock.unlock(); signal.signal(); return }`. Only the line-terminated prefix is coupled to parsing; the guard is checked *after* `buffer.append(data)` on the whole buffer, and the code deliberately does not distinguish "a line that is too large" from "a batch of 200 fine lines 1 byte past the cap" (`module-performance-regressions.py:206` feeds a 2000-message batch through `append` in one call, so batching whole pipes is the expected case). `CodexAppServerClient.threadIds(forkedFrom:).call("thread/list", params: ["limit": 200])` (line 206-207) deserializes `result["data"] as? [[String: Any]]` and `call` returns `message["result"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]` (line 188) — a giant list produces a several-hundred-KiB single JSON line that trips the guard before any newline is seen.
failure: A `thread/list` page whose JSON line exceeds 1 MiB (200 threads with long titles/summaries, or a Codex version that widens the payload) → `append` wipes `buffer` and returns; no id is ever stored, so `response(id:until:)` blocks until the 30 s deadline and `CodexAppServerClient.remove` throws `.timedOut`. The user's confirmed 「清理卡住的会话」 ends as 30 s of a frozen sheet and nothing deleted; the same defect costs `MCPToolDiscovery.listSync` up to 10 s per page (its `tools/list` responses include full `inputSchema` objects, the largest lines in either protocol).
fix: Cap the *unterminated remainder* rather than the whole buffer: after the newline loop, `if buffer.count - <bytes before first newline> > 1_048_576 { buffer.removeAll(); signal.signal() }` — or count only bytes since the last newline and set `closed`/report a distinct failure so the caller fails fast instead of waiting out its deadline.

summary: person(in:) falls through from an under-length possessive split to the host-marker branch, so a one-character Han family name keeps the machine's 「的」 and greets "De Li"/"De Wang"
evidence: The loop (lines 72-89) tries the possessive markers first: for `李的MacBook Pro` the marker `的` matches, `raw` is `李`, and `if prefix.count >= 2 { return prefix }` (line 88) correctly declines a 1-char name. The loop then continues to the host markers, where `MacBook` matches the tail of `李的MacBook Pro`, giving `raw = "李的"` (2 chars) which passes the same `prefix.count >= 2` guard (line 88) and is returned. `displayName` (line 121-127) then sees two Han characters and transliterates: family=李→Li, given=的→De. Measured by compiling the production enum and running it: `李的MacBook Pro -> person=李的 drawn=De Li`, `王的iMac -> person=王的 drawn=De Wang`, `王的 MacBook -> person=王的 drawn=De Wang`, while the tested shapes still work (`王大锤的MacBook Pro -> Dachui Wang`). The code's own contract at lines 53-54 says a prefix shorter than two characters is a stray marker and the whole string must be kept instead — the possessive branch honors that, the host-marker fallback undoes it. The suite `Tests/greeting-name-regressions.py` has no case where a single character precedes a possessive marker, so this shape is unguarded.
failure: A Mac whose ComputerName is «李的MacBook Pro» (any 1-character family name + 的 + model) → the GreetingCard colophon prints "De Li" (the possessive particle treated as the given name) instead of keeping the machine name, i.e. the card says hello to a person who does not exist.
fix: In the host-marker branch, refuse a prefix that still contains one of `possessive` (or break out of the loop with `return name` when a possessive matched but its trimmed prefix was shorter than 2 characters), so the possessive rule owns that shape instead of the host-marker fallback. Add a `("李的MacBook Pro", "李的MacBook Pro")` case to Tests/greeting-name-regressions.py.
verdict_note: Probe confirmed the symptom: 李的MacBook Pro → person=李的 → drawn "De Li". Fixed in the possessive split: a one-character Han prefix is a complete surname, so 李的MacBook Pro → 李 (→ drawn "Li") and 王的iMac / 王的 MacBook → 王. Deliberate deviation from this finding's suggested expectation (keep the whole string): the module's contract is 'the greeting names the person, never the machine', and a one-character Han prefix is a real surname, not a stray marker — keeping the whole string would greet with the machine name for exactly the shape this finding asked to fix. The two shapes the whole-string rule really protects still keep it: a bare particle (的MacBook Pro) and a one-letter Latin joiner (sMacBook) both stay whole via isOneCharacterName (U+4E00–9FFF, != 的). Tests/greeting-name-regressions.py pins 李的MacBook Pro → 李, 王的iMac → 王, 王的 MacBook → 王, sMacBook → sMacBook, 的MacBook Pro → 的MacBook Pro; a mutant reverting the acceptance trips.

summary: The provider display name is produced, stored in the runtime endpoint and never read anywhere, while the fingerprint deliberately omits it — a rename is invisible to the route check
evidence: `endpoint.name` is set at line 62 (`provider["name"] as? String ?? "自定义模型"`) and consumed nowhere: `grep -rn 'endpoint.name' Sources` returns only the assignment; CodexProxyServer.forwardMigration (CodexProxyServer.swift:773-840) uses baseURL/apiKey/wireAPI/model/reasoningEffort only. `fingerprint` (lines 15-19) hashes base/key/wire/model/reasoning — exactly the fields the proxy uses — but is also used as the staleness key for the launch settings, and `name` is the field the user sees in the UI.
failure: Renaming a saved provider (same URL/key/model) keeps the old fingerprint, so an existing MigrationRecord continues to be considered current; no user-visible string from the record identifies the provider, and the dead `name` field hides that the manifest cannot report which provider a session is pinned to.
fix: Either delete `name` from the endpoint (it is never rendered) or render it in the migration record / dialog; if the intent was to distinguish providers in the manifest, add the name to `fingerprint` so a rename forces a re-prepare.

summary: The bridge settings JSON embeds the proxy token in the model string it also pins as ANTHROPIC_MODEL, and `--settings` argv is written into every shell command
evidence: Lines 77-83 build `environment` with `"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": token` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL/SMALL_FAST/HAIKU/SONNET/OPUS = record.model`, then serialize it as the `--settings` JSON that MigrationStorage.arguments (line 215) places on the command line: `return ["--model", record.model, "--settings", settings, "--resume", record.targetSessionID]`. The command string is then written to the launch path of TerminalLauncher (openMigratedSession) and, in the regression, to `command.txt`. SessionMigrationService wraps it in `env`, so the token is in argv, not the environment.
failure: On a multi-user Mac or anywhere process argv is observable (ps, crash reports, Terminal scrollback, shell history if pasted), the proxy bearer is exposed; the test itself persists this command to disk (`command.txt`) and asserts only that the provider apiKey is absent, never the proxy token.
fix: Pass the per-process settings through an environment file or a short-lived settings file inside the private records directory and reference it by path, or have the launcher write the JSON to a 0600 file next to the record and open with `--settings @file`; at minimum assert in the regression that the bridge token never appears in the shell string.

summary: Images are written into Cursor's workspaceStorage before COMMIT and are never removed on rollback, so every failed or cancelled desktop migration leaves orphan image files
evidence: Line 152 calls `MigrationCursorHistory.storedImage(database:workspaceID:image:loadedAt:)`, which at lines 246-250 does `try FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: directory, …)` then `try PrivateFileWriter.write(bytes, to: file)` for each picture — this runs while building `rows`, i.e. before line 204 `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The transaction's `defer { sqlite3_exec(db, "ROLLBACK", …) }` (line 205) and the manifest-rollback catch in MigrationStorage.swift:147-150 only undo database rows; nothing tracks or deletes the files. The test suite asserts the rollback leaves no target row (session-migration-regressions.py:528-535) but never checks the workspaceStorage image directory.
failure: Any refusal after image materialization — a later message with an unsupported picture (助手消息里的图片暂不迁移), a manifest publish failure, or Task.checkCancellation() at line 223/225 after a user closed the dialog — rolls back the transaction but leaves one or more JPEG/PNG/WebP files under `User/workspaceStorage/<id>/images`, growing Cursor's storage with every retry.
fix: Collect the created file URLs while looping and delete them in a catch/defer that runs when the transaction did not commit (mirroring the manifest removal in MigrationStorage.prepare), or move the file writes after the last throw site and into the commit block.

summary: profile() reads and JSON-parses up to 2000 composerHeaders blobs on every call, and the same call is issued twice per Cursor-desktop migration, sorting the whole table through a temp B-tree because Cursor has no index on lastUpdatedAt.
evidence: `SELECT composerId, value FROM composerHeaders WHERE isSubagent = 0 ORDER BY lastUpdatedAt DESC LIMIT 2000` (line 40). On the real state.vscdb (read-only) the plan is `SCAN composerHeaders` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` (composerHeaders has only idx_composerHeaders_0 (workspaceId,isSubagent,isArchived,recency) and idx_composerHeaders_1 (recency,composerId)); Python/sqlite measurement of the identical query: 706 rows scanned, 6.2 ms query + 3.5 ms of JSON parsing = ~10 ms per call, and every row's `value` blob is parsed in Swift even though a point lookup by composerId is 0.29 ms. The call sites are SessionMigrationService.swift:97 (inside prepare) and MigrationStorage.swift:113 (same prepare), plus every preview of a cursorDesktop source, so one migration opens the DB and rescans at least twice.
failure: Picking 「Cursor 桌面 · 项目模型」 as the migration target pays the full-table scan twice per prepare; on a user tree with tens of thousands of composers (this machine already has 1.4 M cursorDiskKV rows) the scan/parse cost grows linearly with total Cursor history rather than with the selected project.
fix: Bound the candidate set with Cursor's own index: `WHERE isSubagent = 0 AND recency >= ? ORDER BY recency DESC LIMIT 2000` (measured: 77 of 706 rows in a 30-day window, and the plan becomes `SEARCH composerHeaders USING INDEX idx_composerHeaders_1 (recency>?)` with no temp sort), and parse `value` only for rows whose canonical directory matches.

summary: The WebP dimension parser reads VP8X canvas bytes for every webp, so lossy (VP8 ) images are rejected as unverified even though the write path accepts them
evidence: Lines 355-360: `case "image/webp": guard bytes.count >= 30, bytes[0] == 0x52, bytes[8] == 0x57, bytes[12] == 0x56, bytes[15] == 0x58 else { break }` — the guard requires the chunk at 12..15 to be 'VP8X' (0x56 0x50 0x38 0x58), i.e. an extended/alpha WebP. Plain lossy files start with 'VP8 ' at the same offsets and fall through to `throw MigrationFailure.unsupported(…)` at line 363. Measured against real files on this machine: 137 VP8X and 69 'VP8 ' containers; `.../highagency.pencildev/.../ember.webp` (VP8 , sips reports 600×450) → guard fails; `.../neo-动图.webp` (VP8X) → (640,594) matches sips. For 'VP8 ' the correct dims live at `bytes[26..27] | bytes[28..29]` after the 9d 01 2a start code (verified: b[23:26] == 9d012a, dims 600×450).
failure: A Cursor-deskop or Cursor-CLI session carrying a lossy WebP screenshot (the common webp form) → `includeImages` migration fails at preview time with 这张图片的格式尚未验证，暂不迁移, even though `storedImage` would have accepted the same bytes for Cursor Desktop; the workaround is to disable the image option entirely.
fix: Branch on `bytes[12..15]`: for 'VP8 ' read dims from b[26..29] (masking the scale bits) and for 'VP8L' from the 4-byte field at b[21..24] (`(v & 0x3FFF) + 1`); keep the existing VP8X path. Add fixtures for both containers.

summary: The protobuf decoder's varint-field value is stored in `Field.integer` and never read, and the tests only prove it is never produced for the accepted inputs
evidence: `struct Field { let number: Int; let bytes: Data?; let integer: UInt64? }` (line 6); `fields()` fills `integer` at line 36 for `tag & 7 == 0`. `grep -rn '\.integer' Sources` finds no reader of this property (the only `.integer` hit is UserDefaults in BatteryChargeController), and the only consumers at lines 188/195 read `.number`/`.bytes`. The negative fixtures (session-migration-regressions.py:496-498) only assert that three invalid byte strings all throw.
failure: A root blob whose references are encoded as varint fields (tag 1 with wire type 0) parses successfully with `bytes == nil`, so the loop at line 195 (`for field in references where field.number == 1`) silently skips every message and `cliSnapshot` returns a preview with an empty message list instead of rejecting the unknown format.
fix: Either reject wire-type-0 fields whose number is a known reference (requiredMessage=1, workspace=9) in `fields()`, or use `integer` to reject references that arrive in the wrong wire type; drop the property if neither.

summary: item_completed messages have no dedup guard; on a paginated rollout the same prompt is appended to `canonical` twice (event row and response_item row are both trusted) while the response_item path skips environment preambles
evidence: Lines 164-169 append `canonical` unconditionally for every UserMessage/AgentMessage item; the matching `response_item`/message path at lines 178-188 appends to `projected` and additionally filters `isEnvironment(body)`. There is no `seen`/identity check between the two sources, and only the response_item path is filtered. On real rollouts the two are not redundant for images: UserMessage items carry `local_image` path blocks while the response_item message carries the base64 `input_image` (measured on ~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/03/rollout-2026-10-03T22-49-53-…: 5 UserMessage items with `local_image`, 4 `input_image` blocks in response_item messages), so both paths must stay — but the text projection is then duplicated whenever a turn has no images.
failure: For a Codex Desktop rollout (history_mode paginated) whose item_completed rows repeat a user prompt that also appears as a response_item message, the migrated transcript contains that prompt twice; the test fixture (session-migration-regressions.py:43-47) models the opposite shape — the preamble lives only in the response_item row — so no regression catches it.
fix: Dedup the two carriers: skip an `item_completed` User/Agent message whose text equals the last canonical message appended for the same role, or key pending item messages by `item.id` and only append if no response_item message with the same text arrived in the same turn.
verdict_note: Verified in the 2026-10-07 recheck: `selected = paginated ? canonical : projected` — the two carriers land in different arrays and are never merged, so no double prompt can occur.

summary: Every preview parses the entire source log into [[String: Any]] and every migration parses it three times, with no reuse between the dialog, prepare()'s pre-check and prepare()'s post-probe re-check.
evidence: rows() (lines 44-57) does String(data:encoding:) + split over the whole file + `Data($0.utf8)` + JSONSerialization per line. Measured on this machine (release-style Swift): 15 MB / 40,000 rows → 0.37 s for the current pipeline vs 0.26 s for a byte-level `bytes.split(separator: 0x0A)` pipeline; String.split alone is 0.24 s and the per-line `Data($0.utf8)` copy is the rest. Sources are read with a 64 MiB budget (SessionMigrationService.swift:41,58 pass maxSourceBytes), so one rows() call extrapolates to ~1.6 s and several hundred MB of transient dictionaries (real logs here are 24-107 MB). claude() then builds two more full-size dictionaries over the same records — `byID` (line 246-252) and `positions`/`parents` in claudeToolBranches (line 323-333) — for data it never uses except along one parent chain. The dialog calls preview() on every toggle (SessionMigrationDialog.swift:230-231) and SessionMigrationService.prepare calls preview() twice more (lines 76 and 122), so one migration of a large session is 3 full reads+parses ≈ 5 s of CPU and a correspondingly large transient heap.
failure: Open the migration dialog on a 40 MB Codex rollout and flip 「包含已完成工具」 / 「包含用户图片」: each flip re-reads and re-parses the whole file on the actor, the sheet stays in 「正在读取会话…」 for seconds per flip, and clicking 迁移并打开 pays for three more parses before any file is written.
fix: In `prepare`, keep the bytes from one read and re-verify with `MigrationHistory.fingerprint` over those bytes instead of calling preview() a third time; and memoize the last (client, sessionID, cwd, options, file size+mtime) → MigrationPreview in SessionMigrationService so the dialog's toggle reload is a cache hit. Byte-splitting in rows() alone removes ~30% of the remaining cost.

symbol: codex tool gate / desktop size guard
summary: The two branches that actually fail on real user data — the Codex canonical-vs-projected tool gate and the Cursor-desktop insert size guard — have no fixture that can reach them.
evidence: Tests/session-migration-regressions.py builds codex_rows with only UserMessage/AgentMessage items (lines 36-52) and a cursor Desktop composer with exactly 2 bubbles (line 60, `fullConversationHeadersOnly:[{bubbleId:user_bubble},{bubbleId:answer_bubble}]`), while the includeCompletedTools assertions there (lines 318-343, 546) drive small synthetic tool sets. grep for 'CommandExecution|FileChange|McpToolCall' in Tests/ finds none, and no fixture exceeds a handful of messages, so MigrationCursorDesktop.insert's `root.count * (messages.count + 1)` guard can never trip in CI. Confirmed by the two findings above: both defects are invisible to `make test TEST=session-migration` yet reproduce on this machine's real stores (6/24 rollouts refused; refusal at 575 messages).
failure: Regression suite stays green while a user's normal session migration fails with an unsupported/tooLarge message; a later change to either counter or guard would be signed off by CI without touching the real failure mode.
fix: Add two fixtures: a paginated codex rollout containing a CommandExecution item_completed with no matching function_call_output (expect a carried/omitted result, not a refusal), and a Cursor-desktop migrate of ~600 messages whose payload is <1 MiB (expect success).
verdict_note: f54fb31: cross-projection count comparison deleted; real rollouts measured 89 vs 73

summary: The `logicalConversationID` linkage can bind unrelated conversations: it is inherited from the newest record whose *target* session equals the source session, with no check that the source is the same conversation, which is exactly what happens when a migrated conversation reappears in the Claude source list.
evidence: MigrationStorage.swift:133-134: `let parent = old.first { $0.target.client == preview.source.client && $0.targetSessionID == preview.source.sessionID }` then `logicalConversationID: parent?.logicalConversationID ?? id`. There is no `$0.source.id == preview.source.id`, no cwd equality and no title check. A Claude session produced by a migration (id = `targetSessionID` of that migration) shows up in the session list like any other; `SessionMigrationButton` (SessionMigrationDialog.swift:73) disables only on `isBusy`/`isSubagent`, so a second migration from that new session is offered. Because A→B and A→C records already share one logicalConversationID, and B is then migrated to D, all four records become one chain.
failure: User migrates Claude A → Codex B, later migrates A → Claude C, later migrates B → Codex D. Record C's parent lookup finds the A→C record (its target is C), but record D's parent lookup finds *any* record whose target is B (the A→B record) — if B also happens to be a target of a second, unrelated migration (same source-session-id reuse across two different subjects in the same project directory), D inherits the wrong family, and the migration history card / desktop title group two unrelated conversations.
fix: Add `$0.source.id == preview.source.id` (and/or fingerprint equality) to the parent predicate so the link requires the source to be the same conversation, not just the same session id in the same client.

summary: `readBounded` does not distinguish a permission error from a missing file — every FileHandle open failure becomes `MigrationFailure.missing` ('找不到完整的本地会话历史') and the real error is discarded, so a chmod-broken sessions dir presents as 'history not found'.
evidence: MigrationStorage.swift:92-101: `do { handle = try FileHandle(forReadingFrom: file) } catch { throw MigrationFailure.missing }` — the `catch` drops the underlying error unconditionally. The same default is applied implicitly by callers: `SessionMigrationService.command` (:131) uses `FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: record.source.cwd)` before `runtime`/shell construction, and `prepare` (:113) trusts the path that was stat'ed in `preview`. Nothing anywhere surfaces EACCES/EROFS, and `MigrationFailure.storage` ('会话写入失败') is the only way permission failures are named on the write side.
failure: A user's `~/.claude/projects` or a source `.jsonl` becomes unreadable (restricted sandbox, restored backup at 0600 owned by another uid, external drive mounted read-only). `preview()` throws `invalidHistory`/`missing` instead of anything pointing at permissions; the user re-tries the same path forever, and the reviewer/developer has no breadcrumb because the POSIX errno never reaches the message.
fix: Map only `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` to `.missing` and surface the rest via `MigrationFailure.storage` (or an `unavailable` with the errno), e.g. `catch let e as NSError { throw e.code == ENOENT ? .missing : .storage }`; keep the message generic but distinct.

summary: Each migration materializes the full payload up to 4-5 times (JSONEncoder/decoder + SHA-256 fingerprint + text projection) and each `prepare` call runs `preview()` twice more, so the memory and CPU peak is a small multiple of the 16 MiB payload for no state that cannot be derived once.
evidence: The payload is built as one `Data` and then streamed into `PrivateFileWriter` (MigrationStorage.swift:159-165, JSON rows appended one at a time in MigrationHistory.claudeData:483-501 / codexData:525-558); `prepare` runs `records(at:)` (which itself JSON-decodes every manifest, :77-89) at :118, and `SessionMigrationService.prepare` runs `preview(source:)` at :76 and again at :122 — each preview re-reads up to `maxSourceFileBytes` = 64 MiB (MigrationHistory.swift:35) and re-parses every JSONL row via `String(data:).split` (MigrationHistory.swift:44-57), plus `fingerprint` = SHA-256 over the whole snapshot. `MigrationPreview` is `Sendable` but never cached between the two calls.
failure: A large conversation (e.g. the 44.5 MiB rollout present in `~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/03/rollout-2026-10-03T23-18-40-…jsonl`) is read and parsed twice in one `prepare`, then encoded once for the staged file, then the fingerprint hashes it; on a cold filesystem cache the page-in + parse cost is paid at least three times, and the transient peak is several multiples of the file size even though the final artifact is capped at 16 MiB.
fix: Pass the already-computed `latest`/`checked` preview (and its fingerprint) into `MigrationStorage.prepare` instead of re-deriving it, or memoize the parsed rows on the preview; the second `preview` call exists only to detect change, which a stat/mtime+size stamp of the source can answer without a full re-parse.

summary: The Claude slug encoder duplicates `SessionMonitor.projectDirName` with the opposite character unit (UTF-16 units here, UTF-8 bytes there), and the two agree only for the ASCII/BMP subset — one of the two must be wrong for supplementary-plane characters.
evidence: MigrationStorage.swift:14-18 documents and implements the JS rule: `try MigrationPath.canonical(cwd).utf16.map { byte in ((48...57).contains(byte) || ...) ? String(UnicodeScalar(UInt8(byte))) : "-" }`. SessionMonitor.swift:740-753 documents the identical client rule ('The client's rule is `cwd.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")`') but implements it over `cwd.utf8` (:747 `for byte in cwd.utf8`). Verified against the installed client 2.1.289 bundle (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe`), which contains `_=200;function h(e){let r=e.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g,"-");if(r.length<=_)return r;return \`${r.slice(0,_)}-${Math.abs(jee(e)).toString(36)}\`}` — a per-UTF-16-unit replace. Node check on `/Users/me/项目😀/dir`: JS = `-Users-me------dir` (18 units), utf16 map = same, utf8-byte map = `-Users-me------------dir` (24 bytes). So for any cwd containing an emoji, SessionMonitor computes a directory name the client never creates, while MigrationStorage computes the right one.

summary: The Cursor-desktop route-match branch is exercised only with a profile whose fingerprint is already known-good, so a renamed-but-getter-suffixed modelName duplicate of `MigrationCursorDesktop.Profile.modelName` digs a false fingerprint mismatch deeper instead of showing it.
evidence: SessionMigrationService.swift:113-115: `guard profile.modelName == route.model, try profile.fingerprint() == route.configurationFingerprint else { throw MigrationFailure.changed }`. In `prepare` (SessionMigrationService.swift:96-100) a fresh route is built from `profile.modelName` and `profile.fingerprint()` computed *before* the desktop write — so the value the route carries is derived from the same call in the same run. The regression `session-migration-regressions.py:472-511` sets up `desktopRoute` from `try MigrationCursorDesktop.profile(...).fingerprint()` and then mutates `maxMode` to force the mismatch; it never exercises the case where `modelName` differs after Cursor renames the workspace model but the fingerprint still matches, because the fingerprint is checked first in `prepare`'s route construction and can never differ from itself.

fix: Either drop the redundant `profile.modelName == route.model` comparison (the fingerprint already covers the profile) or add a regression that mutates `modelName` alone and asserts the expected failure mode explicitly, so the behavior is pinned rather than incidental.

summary: The Claude cwd→project-directory slug is written twice and the two copies disagree on every input; the SessionMonitor copy emits an extra leading dash, so its mirrored directory name can never match what Claude Code actually writes.
evidence: MigrationStorage.swift:13-23 maps `MigrationPath.canonical(cwd).utf16` through the client's own rule (`claude.exe` 2.1.288 contains the literal `e.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g,"-")`, extracted with `strings`). The fixtures cannot catch it: session-scan-regressions.py:48 and workflow-session-regressions.py:136 create the directory with the same wrong function, and session-migration-regressions.py:726-728 separately pins the pure-replacement expectation (single dash), i.e. the two encoders are each 'verified' against a different oracle.

summary: The retry path re-issues the full request with the same 20s timeout, so a single user click can block for ~40s with the button disabled and provide no way to cancel.
evidence: ModelListFetcher.swift:26-36 loops candidates; :117 `let (data, response) = try await session.data(for: req)` inside `requestModels`; on 401/403 with `authStyle == .both` (:120-127) it builds `retry` and does a second full `session.data(for: retry)` on the same 20s request / 25s resource budget (session at :93-102). summary: The HTML helpers rebuild a fresh NSRegularExpression on every call: `tables(in:)` runs three regexes per document, but each of the per-row cell extractions re-compiles `<t[dh][^>]*>[\s\S]*?</t[dh]>` on every <tr>, and `number`/`lastNumber` re-compile the digit pattern per cell.

NSRegularExpression(pattern: pattern, options: [.caseInsensitive]) else { return [] }` unconditionally (Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/ModelPriceSources.swift:293-301), and `tables(in:)` calls it inside two nested loops (lines 259-271): for each table, `allMatches(of: "<tr[\s\S]*?</tr>"` once per table but `allMatches(of: "<t[dh][^>]*>[\s\S]*?</t[dh]>")` once per row. A Python replay of the shipped Aliyun fixture — 618 tables, 4,096 <tr>, 12,998 cells, 1.8 MB of HTML — shows the compiled work per check is 4,715 regex compilations plus 15,810 `flatten` calls (each `flatten` itself compiling two more regexes, lines 283 and 289). The DeepSeek parser likewise compiles `"\d+(?:\.\d+)?"` twice more per row via `peak()` (lines 466-477).

fix: Hoist the five static patterns into `static let` NSRegularExpression values (the codebase already does this for `snapshotSuffixes` in ModelPricing.swift:624) and add an NSRegularExpression-based `flatten`/`cellNumbers` that reuses one tag-strip and one digit pattern.

summary: A GLM row whose 缓存命中 cell is not a number (「不支持」/「免费」) is silently given `cacheRead = input × 0.1` — exactly the fabricated-cache-price failure mode the file's own header forbids — and the reduction is not recorded in the row's `note` either.
evidence: All rows are parsed, not just the seven the bundled table knows: `for row in rows.dropFirst() where row.count > maxIndex` (line 366) accepts every generation on the page, and `let read = number(row[readIndex]) ?? input * 0.1` (line 371) invents the read price when the cell is prose. Replaying the shipped fixture shows 26 GLM rows emitted, of which 7 have a non-numeric read cell and get an invented 10%: `glm-ocr` (in=0.2, cell 「不支持」), `glm-4-airx` (in=10), `glm-4-assistant` (in=5), `glm-z1-air` (0.5), `glm-z1-airx` (5), `glm-z1-flashx` (0.1), `glm-4.1v-thinking-flashx` (2). This contradicts the doc comment on `parseGLM` (lines 354-367, which describes only cacheWrite = input) and `ModelPriceSources`' stated rule that "a parser guessing" is the one thing that must never happen (lines 16-22).

fix: Either skip rows whose read cell is not numeric, or set `note = "官方页未列缓存命中价"` when the fallback is used — but do not write the invented row silently. Note this is a design choice already made the other way in `parseAliyun` (line 587), which at least states its reduction.

summary: The whole models.dev payload is materialised with `JSONSerialization.jsonObject` into `[String: Any]` and then walked as untyped dictionaries, with no memory bound and no schema check — a 5 MB payload becomes hundreds of MB of heap and a single malformed `cost` dictionary is the only thing that can throw, while everything else is silently skipped.
evidence: `guard let json = try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any] else { throw SourceError.badJSON }` (line 202) then `rowsFromModelsDev(_ json: [String: Any])` walks `json[providerKey] as? [String: Any]`, `provider["models"] as? [String: Any]`, `model["cost"] as? [String: Any]` (lines 138-147). The file's own comment calls the payload "a 5 MB payload fetched weekly" (line 194). A provider key that changes case or moves (`json["anthropic"]` vs `json["Anthropic"]`) or a `cost` that becomes a number rather than a dict makes both loops `continue` — producing an empty `rows` list — and `check` then reports neither a failure nor an error: `found` simply has no USD rows and `report.headline` says 「没有可用的价源返回结果」 only if the CNY side is empty too.

fix: Decode with `JSONDecoder` into typed structs behind `Decodable` (the file already only needs `input`/`output`/`cache_read`/`cache_write`/`tiers`), so a schema change throws a `DecodingError` that lands in `report.error`, and add a `Uncheckable`-style note when `rows.isEmpty`.

summary: models.dev 缺 cache_read 时按 input*0.1 编一个缓存读价，正好会覆盖表中刻意标为 .notPublished 的 pro 档，把「无卡片」换成编造数字

summary: `canonical` strips trailing effort/tier words from every slug unconditionally, so a vendor model whose *actual* id ends in one of those words is silently rewritten onto a different model's row before the price lookup.
evidence: `while let tier = tierSuffix(of: name) { name = String(name.dropLast(tier.count)) }` with the word list `["-xhigh", "-medium", "-thinking", "-high", "-low", "-fast"]` (lines 665-680). The doc comment (lines 649-664) justifies the strip because "No slug in `ModelPriceTable` ends in one of these words (asserted in Tests/model-cost-regressions.py)" — the test at lines 267-272 asserts exactly that over `ModelPriceTable.entries`, i.e. it only pins the bundled table. The strip also runs on ids the app has never seen, e.g. a relay-reported `kimi-k2.7-code` variant `-highspeed` is protected only because the word list contains `-high` and the match requires the hyphens around it — but a genuine id such as a hypothetical `glm-4.5-air-thinking` or `o3-mini-high` (the vendor's own effort SKU) is reduced to a base row, and the app then bills the effort tier at the base rate.
failure: A user records `claude-opus-5-5-medium` (a real Cursor id) — desired — but also records a vendor's own `-fast`/`-thinking`-named product; the second is silently priced at whatever shorter slug happens to match (`matches` requires `slug + "-"` prefix, ModelPricing.swift:684-686) or 0 if none, and the two different models collapse into one usage row in `UsageModelInventory.rows` (which keys by `canonical`).
fix: Restrict the strip to the tiers the app has actually observed (the Cursor effort vocabulary) or gate it on the remaining name resolving in the table, and extend the regression to feed the strip ids that are *not* in the bundled table so the assertion covers the real input population rather than the table it is derived from.

summary: resume() 在 Task.detached（协作线程池）里同步阻塞地反复 run CLI：waitUntilReady 最长 20 s 轮询、cold start 再阻塞 8 次 panes()、focus 再跑 1–3 个进程。

summary: 主线程上每行每帧重建一行富文本（DateFormatter 格式化 + 3 次 String(format:) + 若干 padding），而 consoleBody 又定义在模型层，任何新消费者都会继承这次格式化。

summary: Every `finish()` (every proxied call, including 50 lines of `/health` and `/models` traffic) allocates two new dictionaries and republishes both @Published maps from an uncancelled main-queue block, so each unrelated finishing capture invalidates the whole traffic list.
evidence: Lines 363 and 949-955: `evictStaleLiveBuffers(keeping: id)` does `DispatchQueue.main.async { ... let live = Set(self.catalog.records.map(\.id)).union([id]); self.streams.live = self.streams.live.filter {...}; self.previews.map = self.previews.map.filter {...} }`. `self.streams.live = ...` unconditionally fires `@Published`/`objectWillChange`, and `TrafficView.swift:94` (`private let streams = ProxyCaptureStore.shared.streams`) holds that object for the life of the page (`streams.$live` is the page's `onReceive` at line 404), while `TrafficView.swift:492` observes `previews` inside `TrafficLiveRow`. Meanwhile `flushLive()` (908-935) copies both maps again on every 100 ms flush (`var live = self.streams.live; var preview = self.previews.map`) even though the class's own doc (lines 131-135) states the maps exist precisely so a stream's preview does not re-evaluate the whole page.
failure: With N live/complete captures in flight (a Codex thread plus a Claude Code session plus a health poll), every upstream call completion rebuilds and republishes the two maps on the main thread; each republish re-runs the list's `ForEach` and the inspector's `onReceive`. The 100 ms flush does the same for every streaming row. Measured cost is bounded by `listLimit` (120) so it is a constant-factor hitch, not a blowup — but it is the exact "unrelated update re-runs the subtree" pattern the file was restructured to avoid.
fix: In `evictStaleLiveBuffers`, compute the filtered `live` and `preview` into locals and assign only when they differ (same guard `flushLive` already applies to `previews.map`, line 934); in `flushLive`, mutate only the ids in `snapshot` instead of copying the full maps.
verdict_note: evictStaleLiveBuffers only republishes when the filter actually drops an entry, so a finishing health check no longer re-evaluates the traffic page; capture-detail asserts no notification when nothing is removed and exactly one when it is.

summary: `delete(_:)` is a fully implemented per-row delete (SQL DELETE, JSON fallback, media-directory unlink, live-map cleanup) with zero callers — no UI path deletes a single capture.
evidence: `grep -rn "\.delete(" Sources` yields exactly one hit, line 450 inside the method body itself; `grep -rn "ProxyCaptureStore" Sources Tests Tools` shows the only external uses are `begin` (CodexProxyServer.swift:986,1183), `loadListIfNeeded`, `clearAll`, `detail` and the `catalog`/`streams`/`previews` properties. `TrafficView.swift` has no `contextMenu`, `onDelete`, `swipeActions` or delete keyboard command (grep for `contextMenu|onDelete|keyboardShortcut|删除` finds only the `clearAll` confirmation dialog text at lines 442-443), and its row renders no delete affordance. `Tools/render-mainwindow-preview.py:1376-1389` stubs `ProxyCaptureStore` without a `delete` member, so the preview harness would not even compile against it.
failure: No observable failure today; the risk is the opposite of dead weight: it is the only function that removes a single capture's `logs/captures/<id>/` media directory, and the comment at `clearAll` (460-468) documents that unreachable media is a bug they already had to fix once. A future reader wiring up row deletion would have to rediscover that this method is the intended entry point.
fix: Either wire `delete` into a row context menu / Delete key in `TrafficView`, or remove the method and fold its media removal into `clearAll`'s `removeMedia` path (which already does the same thing per id).
verdict_note: delete(_:) had zero callers (only clearAll is wired to the UI); removed it and folded its only unique job — stating that clearAll handles media — into clearAll's comment. CaptureJSONStore.delete had the same shape and is removed too.

summary: The payload-truncation rule (byte-prefix on a UTF-8 view + the literal marker "… [truncated]") exists twice, and only one of the two copies is reachable — `CaptureMedia.truncate` has no callers outside its own file.
evidence: ProxyCaptureStore.swift:980-984: `static func truncate(_ text: String?, cap: Int) -> String { guard let text, !text.isEmpty else { return "" }; if text.utf8.count <= cap { return text }; return String(decoding: Data(text.utf8.prefix(cap)), as: UTF8.self) + "\n… [truncated]" }`. CaptureMedia.swift:191-194 is the same body minus the nil/empty guard. `grep -rn "CaptureMedia.truncate" Sources Tests Tools` returns nothing; the only callers of `CaptureMedia`'s copy are its own three internal uses at CaptureMedia.swift:28, 36, 38 (with the default `cap`), while every `ProxyCaptureStore` call site (320, 321, 331, 332, 621, 622) uses its local copy. The marker string is load-bearing in three more places: `requestTruncated: request.contains("[truncated]")` (442) and `CaptureTranscript.swift:53` display a truncation banner from it.
failure: A change to the marker or to the prefix semantics (for example making the cut codepoint-safe, or renaming the marker) has to be made in both copies or the banner at 442 / CaptureTranscript:53 stops matching for whichever store produced the payload, and screenshots embedded in a request (the case `compact` is written for) silently disagree between the two paths.
fix: Delete `CaptureMedia.truncate` and have `CaptureMedia.compact` call `ProxyCaptureStore.truncate`, or make one of the two the single implementation and drop the other.

summary: Token columns are read with `sqlite3_column_int` (32-bit) and then widened with a trapping `Int(...)` conversion while the id/status paths use `sqlite3_column_int64`; and `rowToSummary` fabricates `startedAt: Date()` whenever the ISO text does not parse.
evidence: Lines 883-886: `private func optInt(_ stmt: OpaquePointer?, _ i: Int32) -> Int? { if sqlite3_column_type(stmt, i) == SQLITE_NULL { return nil }; return Int(sqlite3_column_int(stmt, i)) }`, fed at 870-872 from `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` / `cache_read_tokens` and at 873 from `cache_write_tokens`. The file proves it knows the right reader elsewhere: line 752 `ids.append(sqlite3_column_int64(stmt, 0))` and line 869 `httpStatus: Int(sqlite3_column_int(stmt, 11))` (deliberately 32-bit for a status code). Line 860: `startedAt: parseISO(text(stmt, 1)) ?? Date()` — a row whose timestamp does not parse gets "now" as its start, and `endedAt: parseISO(text(stmt, 2))` (861) stays nil, so `TrafficView.duration(_:)` (which computes `(rec.endedAt ?? Date()).timeIntervalSince(rec.startedAt)`) divides two different clocks. The formatter used for both directions is the default `ISO8601DateFormatter()` (line 177) with no `formatOptions`; `UsageIndex.swift:1343-1349` shows the sibling stores explicitly set `[.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]` plus a no-fraction fallback, and `VpnDomainLog.swift:368` documents that the default formatter only parses fractional-second stamps with that option set.
failure: A token count above 2147483647 in `captures` (a `prompt_tokens` from a gateway that reports cumulative session totals, or a corrupted/extended DB row) traps in `Int(sqlite3_column_int(...))` during `loadListUnlocked`, i.e. inside `loadCurrentBackendLocked` on the `loadQueue` background thread, taking down the app on traffic-page mount. Separately, any timestamp string the default formatter rejects (fractional seconds written by another build, or a non-ISO value) shows a capture whose 耗时 is "seconds since 1970" and whose duration grows with wall-clock time.
fix: Read the token columns with `sqlite3_column_int64` (and guard with the repo's `JSONCoerce`-style range check) as the id column already does; keep the parsed date `nil` (or fall back to the row's id/ended_at) instead of substituting `Date()` for an unparseable `started_at`.
verdict_note: optInt reads 64-bit (sqlite3_column_int64) and the row's startedAt falls back wiped-in-row: ended_at, then now only when nothing parsed; capture-detail writes 5e9 tokens and a non-ISO started_at into a real SQLite file and asserts both.

summary: begin 持锁期间仍执行 CaptureMedia.compact（整份正文反序列化 + base64 解码 + 落盘图片）与 pruneLocked（含可能整库重写的 VACUUM）
evidence: 248-256: `lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }` 后调 `beginSQL(...)`；beginSQL 内 621-622: `let req = Self.truncate(CaptureMedia.compact(requestJSON, captureID: id), cap: payloadCap)`（compact 对 100 MB 截图正文做 `JSONSerialization.jsonObject` 全树遍历、逐图 base64 解码并 atomic 写文件，CaptureMedia.swift:25-39/112-127），623-625 再写 payload 行并 `pruneLocked()`；pruneLocked 在 663-703 执行两条 DELETE、`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`，freelist > 8192 页时还有 `VACUUM`（整库文件重写）。
failure: 第三方客户端发一张 40-100 MB 的截图请求：begin 持 store 锁做完整反序列化+数十 MB 解码写盘（数百 ms 到秒级），并发到达的其它抓包线程（以及 detail、pushLive）全部排队；命中 VACUUM 阈值的那一次还会在锁内重写整个 proxy-capture.db（实测曾 84 MB）。后果同样是实时转发被拖慢，且这是每条大请求都会发生，不是一次性开销。
fix: 锁内只保留 INSERT captures 拿到 rowid，`compact` + payload INSERT + `pruneLocked()` 放到 `lock.unlock()` 之后（payload 行在 finish 前没有读者，晚写无副作用）；至少把 `pruneLocked()` 移出 beginSQL 的锁临界区，让 VACUUM/checkpoint 不阻塞抓包线程。

summary: 同一份 request/response 在一次 detail 里被 JSONSerialization 解析 4 次，其中 2 次与 turns 完全重复
evidence: 428: `var turns = CaptureTranscript.turns(from: request, mediaDir: dir)`（内部 `object(raw)` 一次，CaptureTranscript.swift:34/465），430-431: `turns += CaptureTranscript.replyTurns(responseJSON: response, ...)`（对 response 再 `object` 一次）；441: `toolCalls: includeTools ? CaptureTranscript.toolCalls(request: request, response: response) : []`，toolCalls 在 CaptureTranscript.swift:119-120 又各解析一次 `object(request)`、`object(response)`。
failure: 在 16 MB 上限的大 payload 上打开「工具」标签（TrafficView.swift:376-378 会以 tools:true 触发 reloadDetail），4 次全量反序列化里多出的 2 次完全是重复工作：按 16 MB JSON 约 50-150 ms/次估算，每次开面板多花 100-300 ms CPU，并且这些解析都发生在 detail 的 store 锁内（见上一条），代价直接转成抓包线程的等待。
fix: 让 `CaptureTranscript.object(_:)` 的结果可复用：在 makeDetail 里解析一次得到 requestObj/responseObj，`turns`/`replyTurns`/`toolCalls` 接受已解析对象；最小版本是给 toolCalls 增加接受 `[String: Any]?` 的重载，避免第二次解析。
verdict_note: makeDetail parses each payload once and hands it to turns, replyTurns and toolCalls; capture-detail asserts turns/toolCalls/fields equal the per-derivation oracle across six payload shapes × mode combinations, and mutation tests catch a dropped or swapped parse.

summary: reloadPersistence() 已无任何调用者，且其唯一触发源（databaseEnabled 偏好）在 16b225e 被删除，导致 JSON 后端不可达、openFailed 无复位路径
evidence: 215-230 定义 `reloadPersistence()`；`grep -rn "reloadPersistence" Sources Tests Tools` 只有这里与 UsageIndex（不同类）命中，ProxyCaptureStore 的版本无人调用。git 16b225e（AppPreferences.swift）删除了唯一的调用点与偏好本身：`- @Published var databaseEnabled: Bool { didSet { ... ProxyCaptureStore.shared.reloadPersistence(); ... } }`。全仓 `grep -rn databaseEnabled` 只剩 UsageJSONStore.swift:8-9 的读侧。副作用：179 `useDatabase` 恒为 true（除非旧版本留下的 UserDefaults 值），CaptureJSONStore 整条分支在新安装上不可达；171/493/569 的 `openFailed` 只由 `closeDatabaseLocked()`（只被 reloadPersistence 调用）复位；946 的文档注释仍把 reloadPersistence 列为 live maps 的移除点。
failure: SQLite 打开一次失败（权限、磁盘满、文件被替换）后 `openFailed = true`，connection() 永久返回 nil → begin 返回 nil，抓包从此静默消失，用户没有任何提示也没有任何恢复入口（原先是切一次存储开关）。JSON 后端同理：没有 UI 能再打开它，之后任何针对该分支的改动都无法被产品路径验证。
fix: 删除 reloadPersistence 与顶部 946 行的过期注释，把 disk-backend 的选择写成显式常量（或保留 legacy 读取但加注释）；给 connection() 加一次重试（例如 openFailed 只在同一次调用内短路，或失败后带冷却重试），否则一次失败即静音到重启。
verdict_note: reloadPersistence() removed from ProxyCaptureStore entirely (no callers, and its trigger was the deleted switch); the openFailed latch became openFailedAt + 5s cooldown in ProxyCaptureStore and ProxyUsageStore, and UsageIndex, so a transient open failure self-heals without any settings path.

summary: 凭据脱敏（authorization/x-api-key/cookie）这段唯一防线在 Tests/ 下没有任何回归
evidence: 1000-1013: `redactedHeaderKeys = ["authorization", "x-api-key", "proxy-authorization", "cookie", "set-cookie"]` + `obj[k] = redactedHeaderKeys.contains(k.lowercased()) ? "…" : v`；`grep -rn "encodeHeaders|redactedHeaderKeys|request_headers" Tests Tools docs` 无命中（Tests 里 authorization 只出现在充电/飞书夹具）。现有 capture 回归只有 Tests/capture-retention-regressions.py（prune/VACUUM）与 performance-regressions.py（scheduleFlush/flushLive 批处理）。
failure: 这是纯函数、无依赖、可切片测试：一旦有人把 `k.lowercased()` 改回原键名比较（HTTP 头名大小写不敏感，`Authorization`/`X-Api-Key` 会漏网），或把某个键从集合里删掉，客户端自己的凭据会被写进 payloads.request_headers 与日志页，而 42 组回归全绿——这类缺陷只能在磁盘上被发现（该函数的注释本身就说这是它存在的理由：曾经把第三方客户端的 creds 序列化进库）。

summary: 中断注册表零回归覆盖：先 attach 后 cancel、cancel 幂等、close 后 cancel、双 close 全靠生产现场验证
evidence: `grep -rn "ProxyInflight" Tests/` 无任何命中；Tests/ 目录里与中断相关的 inflight-animation-regressions.py 只测转子动画（其名字与 ProxyInflight 无关）。唯一的替代品是 Tools/render-mainwindow-preview.py:469-472 的桩：`final class ProxyInflight { static let shared = ProxyInflight(); func cancel(captureID: Int64) {} }`——空实现，只保证预览可编译。本文件里最容易被改坏的是 52-61 行的竞态约定（cancelled 检查在锁内、闭包在解锁后执行）与 118-125 行 close 不重置 cancelled、130-136 行 cancel 的返回值语义。
failure: 任何一次「优化」把 runOrStore 的检查挪到锁外，或让 close 顺手清掉 cancelled，都不会有任何测试变红：症状只在实际点「中断」时出现——要么 abort 闭包在连接已关后才被存下、永不执行（客户端看到完整流而不是被截断），要么 CaptureTap.finish 之后代理仍把用户中断误判为 upstream 故障并写 502 到访问日志。
fix: 在 Tests/ 下加一个纯 Swift 探针（照 usage-index-regressions.py 的切片编译方式）：从源码切出 Handle 与 ProxyInflight 两个类型，断言 (a) cancel 先于 attach 时闭包立即执行、(b) 二次 cancel 返回 false 且闭包只跑一次、(c) close 后 cancel(captureID:) 返回 false 但 handle.isCancelled 仍为 true、(d) 并发 attach/cancel 下两个闭包各执行恰好一次。

summary: JSON 后端下每记录一次第三方请求就把整份 rollup 重新编码、拼接、原子写盘
evidence: 第 85 行 `persistJSONLocked()` 在 record() 的 JSON 分支里逐条调用；函数体 323-335 行：`for row in rows.values.sorted(...)` 全量 JSONEncoder.encode，`body += line + "\n"` 字符串累加，最后 `try? Data(body.utf8).write(to: jsonURL, options: .atomic)`。record 由 ProxyCaptureStore.finish:367 在每个代理请求结束时调用。第 284 行加载器是按键 last-wins：`rows[Self.key(row.day, row.model)] = Row(...)`。
failure: 开了 JSONL 后端的用户每完成一个第三方请求，就要对一个随历史增长（一年 ≈3 650 行 / ~500 KB）的文件做 3 遍 O(N) 工作（编码+拼接+拷贝）加一次整文件原子替换；一次 100 请求的 agent 会话就是 300 遍全量编码 + 100 次 ~500 KB 写入，且 N 无上限。
fix: record 走追加路径：把当前行编码成一行 append 到 jsonURL（加载器 last-wins，语义不变），只保留启动时一次全量重写做压缩；或最少加 dirty 标记，合并写（例如 1 s 防抖/退出前 flush），把每请求 O(N) 写盘降为 O(1) 追加。
verdict_note: The JSONL backend this finding concerns was deleted in 0a4cf30 (收敛为单一 SQLite 后端): persistJSONLocked/jsonURL no longer exist. Rechecked 2026-10-07.

summary: JSONL 的 v1 修复靠独立标记文件防止重复扣减，崩溃窗口内会二次扣减
evidence: 300-309 行：`guard !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: jsonMigratedURL.path) else { return }` → 逐行 `row.input = max(0, row.input - row.cacheRead)` → `persistJSONLocked()` → 最后才 `try? Data().write(to: jsonMigratedURL, options: .atomic)`。标记写在数据落盘之后，两者不是同一个事务（SQLite 侧用 `PRAGMA user_version`，见 231-240 行，与 UPDATE 同库）。

summary: Int(getValue(...)) 对非有限浮点直接 trap：SMC 读到 NaN/超大 float 时整机 App 崩溃
evidence: 237-241 行 `rpm: Int(getValue("F\(i)Ac") ?? 0)`、`minRPM: max(1, Int(getValue("F\(i)Mn") ?? 1))`、`maxRPM: max(1, Int(getValue("F\(i)Mx") ?? 1))`；这些键是 "flt " 类型，decode 在 328-329 行 `case SMCDataType.flt: return Double(Float(bytes) ?? 0)`——`Float(bytes)` 只在 bytes.count < 4 时返回 nil（这里的数组恒为 32），NaN/±Inf/1e30 全部原样返回，getValue 的唯一守卫是 151-154 行的「全零字节」检查，对 0x7FC00000 之类的 NaN 载荷无效。对照：HardwareSensors.plausibleWatts:309-311 对同类读数有 `value.isFinite && value >= 0 && value <= 500` 守卫，风向一致，这里缺。
failure: 当某台机器的 F{i}Ac / F{i}Mn / F{i}Mx 返回 NaN 或超出 Int 范围的浮点（型号/固件差异、键半初始化），FanMonitor.refresh（readQueue，每 2 s）调用 loadFans 时 `Int(nan)` 触发 Swift 运行时 precondition 失败 → 进程直接崩溃；崩溃点在后台队列，无法捕获。
fix: 在 decode 的 flt 分支加 `guard d.isFinite else { return nil }`（或 `return d.isFinite ? d : nil`），并给 loadFans 的四处 Int() 换成 `Int(...)` 前的 clamp 辅助（可复用现成的 JSONCoerce.intVal 语义）。
verdict_note: safeRPM now clamps every SMC float-to-Int conversion: non-finite reads report 0, finite values clamp to ±2^20. The trap was reachable by construction (flt keys decode any bit pattern; FanMonitor polls every 2 s on a background queue). Tests/smc-sampling-regressions.py executes the production function at NaN/±inf/1e300/±bound; mutants (dropping isFinite, bypassing safeRPM in loadFans) trip. Note: no machine has been observed sending these patterns — fixed because it is a crash-on-data, not because it was seen.

summary: 风扇采样把 SMC 浮点读数直接 Int() 转换，NaN/∞ 会 trap 整个应用
evidence: 103-107 行 `private extension Float { init?(_ bytes: [UInt8]) { guard bytes.count >= MemoryLayout<Float>.size else { return nil }; self = bytes.withUnsafeBytes { $0.loadUnaligned(as: Float.self) } } }` 唯一失败条件是长度不足，0xFFFFFFFF/0x7F800000 这类位模式会解成 NaN/∞ 而不是 nil；decode 328 行 `return Double(Float(bytes) ?? 0)` 把它带出来，loadFans 直接转：238-240 行 `rpm: Int(getValue("F\(i)Ac") ?? 0), minRPM: max(1, Int(getValue("F\(i)Mn") ?? 1)), maxRPM: max(1, Int(getValue("F\(i)Mx") ?? 1))`，229 行 `for i in 0..<Int(count)` 同理。本机 Swift 实测 `Int(Double.nan)` 直接 abort（"Fatal error: Double value cannot be converted to Int because it is either infinite or NaN"，exit 133）。getValue 的 `allSatisfy == 0` 守卫只拦全零，110 上限只作用于温度路径，都不经过这里。
failure: 任何一次 F0Ac/F0Mn/F0Mx（或浮点型 FNum）读到 inf/NaN 位模式（键未初始化、机型差异、SMC 回垃圾）时，FanMonitor 2 s 轮询的后台读队列直接 trap，常驻菜单栏应用整体崩溃。

verdict_note: Same fix as finding 146 — one clamp (`SMCController.safeRPM`) now serves loadFans and fanMode; pinned by Tests/smc-sampling-regressions.py (registered in the Makefile suite list).

summary: 80 字节协议布局只有运行时 precondition，无任何回归守护，且不存在纯逻辑测试缝
evidence: 304-307 行 `private func call(...)` / `let inputSize = MemoryLayout<SMCKeyData>.stride` / `precondition(inputSize == 80, "SMCKeyData layout must be 80 bytes")`；grep 全仓 Tests/ 对 `SMCController`、`SMCKeyData`、`loadFans`、`FanMode` 命中 0 条（Tools/render-mainwindow-preview.py:769-789 的 FanInfo/FanSide 是自带替身，不编译本文件；Tests/battery-control.c 只覆盖电池 helper）。fanctl.c:26-28 用的是 `#pragma pack(push,4)` + `_Static_assert(sizeof(SMCKeyData) == 80)`，即 C 侧是编译期约束。

summary: The swallowing tap never re-enables itself after kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout / ByUserInput, so the 'other apps never see ⌘⇧A' guarantee silently ends for the rest of the session; the sibling tap in ScreenshotOverlay handles exactly this.
evidence: ScreenshotHotKey.swift:146-176 — the callback only does `if ScreenshotHotKey.isScreenshotHotKey(event) { ... } return Unmanaged.passUnretained(event)`; `tapEnable(tap:enable:)` appears only at line 119 (disable) and 175/198 (initial enable). Contrast ScreenshotOverlay.swift:180-188, where the same callback shape handles `type == .tapDisabledByTimeout || type == .tapDisabledByUserInput` and re-enables the port. The SDK documents the disable events as 'Out of band event types ... delivered to the event tap callback to notify it of unusual conditions that disable the event tap' (MacOSX.sdk/CoreGraphics.framework/Headers/CGEventTypes.h:128-130) and re-enabling as `CGEventTapEnable` (CGEvent.h:313-315).
failure: The main run loop stalls past the tap timeout (a modal, a synchronous VPN/network call, a large SwiftUI pass) or the user toggles the tap in System Settings → the tap is disabled; the next deliverable event is a `tapDisabled…` pseudo-event whose keycode field is 0, so `isScreenshotHotKey` is false and it is passed through without re-enabling. From then on ⌘⇧A is no longer swallowed (the Carbon hotkey still fires when it won the race), so event-observing apps (Feishu/Lark, per the file header) start seeing the combo again, and only a sleep/wake (`installWakeObserverIfNeeded`, line 61-68) restores it.
fix: Mirror the overlay: first thing in the callback, `if type == .tapDisabledByTimeout || type == .tapDisabledByUserInput { DispatchQueue.main.async { if let p = ScreenshotHotKey.shared.tap { CGEvent.tapEnable(tap: p, enable: true) } }; return Unmanaged.passUnretained(event) }`.

summary: No-trust fallback registers keypad Enter as hotkey id 4 but the switch has no case 4, so the key is swallowed system-wide with no action (registered branch is unreachable).
evidence: Line 263 registers it: `(UInt32(kVK_ANSI_KeypadEnter), 0, 4),          // ...` together with Esc/Space/Return/⌘C/⌘S (lines 259-266, `RegisterEventHotKey(keyCode, mods, id, appTarget, 0, &ref)` at line 270). The handler dispatches only `case 1 / 2 / 3, 5 / 6` and then `default: break` (lines 277-289). Cable: the parallel routing in `handleKey` DOES handle it — `if event.keyCode == UInt16(kVK_Return) || event.keyCode == UInt16(kVK_ANSI_KeypadEnter) { ... copyAndClose ... }` (line 334).
failure: On a Mac without Accessibility/Input-Monitoring trust (the whole reason this fallback exists), with the overlay capturing: pressing keypad Enter does nothing, and because RegisterEventHotKey consumes the key system-wide, the keystroke never reaches the front app either. With trust, the same key copies the selection (line 334). Same feature, opposite behaviour depending on permission state.
fix: Add `case 3, 4, 5:` in `handleFallbackHotKey` (collapse the return/keypad-enter/⌘C ids into the copy branch), or drop the keypad-Enter registration from the `keys` array so it is not silently stolen.

summary: `?? content.displays.first` fallback silently captures the wrong display when the requested displayID is not in SCShareableContent, and the panel is then sized/labelled for the requested NSScreen.
evidence: Lines 372-375: `let content = try await SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows(...)` / `guard let display = content.displays.first(where: { $0.displayID == displayID }) ?? content.displays.first else { throw CaptureError.noDisplay }`. The caller builds the freeze panel from the *NSScreen* that was asked for: `shots.append((screen, try await Self.captureDisplay(screen)))` (line 66) then `let panel = CapturePanel(contentRect: screen.frame ...)` (lines 86-91) and `SnipCanvas(screenshot: image, screen: screen, ...)` (lines 109-113). Nothing cross-checks that the returned image actually belongs to `screen` (no size/ID comparison anywhere).
failure: Multi-display setup where the SCK listing omits/changes the ID (display asleep, Sidecar/VD disconnected mid-capture, mirroring): display A's NSScreen is used for the panel frame and the click→pixel mapping, but display B's pixels are returned. `freezeLayer.contentsGravity = .resize` then stretches B's image into A's panel, so the user freezes the wrong screen while the window-snap rectangles for A are drawn over it. Because the failure is silent (no throw, no beep), it reads as 'screenshot is broken/hallucinating', not as a permission or ID problem.
fix: Drop the `?? content.displays.first` fallback and `throw CaptureError.noDisplay` when no display matches `displayID` (the existing error path beeps and returns), or verify `content.displays.first(where:)` matched before building the panel.

summary: saveAndClose swallows the PNG write error with `try?` after the overlay has already been dismissed, so a failed save is completely invisible.
evidence: Lines 413-418: `static func writePNG(...) { guard let tiff = image.tiffRepresentation, ... else { return }; try? png.write(to: url) }`. Caller at lines 139-151 closes the overlay first (`dismissOverlay()` line 141) and then only wires the result through `panel.begin { result in if result == .OK, let url = panel.url { Self.writePNG(img, to: url) } }` — no error is surfaced for either the `guard` returns or the write itself, and `writePNG` has no return value. Compare `writePasteboard`, which at least lands the pixels somewhere the user can inspect.
failure: User picks a read-only/network volume or a full disk in the NSSavePanel and clicks 保存: the save panel closes, the overlay is gone, no file exists, no beep and no message. The screenshot (with its annotations) is unrecoverable and the app appears to have saved it.
fix: Return `Bool`/`Error` from `writePNG` (or make it `throws`) and on failure beep plus show an `NSAlert`/present an error string; at minimum `NSSound.beep()` in the failure branch so the no-file case is distinguishable from success.

summary: The screenshot feature (two files, ~1500 lines) has zero regression coverage; the key-routing and match logic are pure functions that the existing source-slice suite pattern could execute, and the keypad-Enter divergence above is exactly what such a test would have caught.
evidence: `grep -rni 'hotkey|snip|screenshot' Tests/` returns only incidental words inside comments of unrelated suites (machine-mark-regressions.py:18, product-mark-regressions.py:29/185, widget-snapshot-regressions.py:23, widget-tint-regressions.py:14, fixtures/machine-mark-probe.swift:40); no Tests/*screenshot*.py exists, no suite in `export TEST_SUITES := ...` (Makefile line 6) covers either file, and `grep -rn 'ScreenshotOverlayController|ScreenshotHotKey' Tests/` matches nothing. Meanwhile the logic is sliceable without launching the app, exactly like Tests/ui-regressions.py slices `EqualRowGrid`/`recordHeartbeats`: `isScreenshotHotKey` (ScreenshotHotKey.swift:131-135, pure over a CGEvent), the index→action mapping in `handleFallbackHotKey` (lines 275-290), the flag/keycode routing in `handleKey` (lines 328-356), and `SnipToolbar`/`PinChromeBar` tag routing (lines 1089-1110, 1251-1254, whose comment records that a previous frame-range routing sent copy→close).
failure: Key routing regressions stay invisible until a human with a real capture session notices: today's keypad-Enter dead branch (case 4 missing) and any future drift between `handleKey` and `handleFallbackHotKey` ship silently; the fallback path is only reachable on machines without Accessibility trust, i.e. the least-tested configuration.
fix: Add a `screenshot-input-regressions.py` that slices `handleFallbackHotKey`'s switch table and `handleKey` into a fixture harness (mirroring the existing slice pattern) and asserts one action per registered id / per key code — specifically that every idx in the `keys` array has a matching `case`, and that Esc/Space/Return/keypad-Enter/⌘C/⌘S route identically in both paths; register it in Makefile's TEST_SUITES.
recheck_note: Confirmed 2026-10-07 by the slice-1 verifier: capture-path work is now handled by the ScreenshotOverlay/ScreenshotHotKey review; the keypad-Enter branch and the missing suite are being addressed under findings 454-460 (cluster A, spawned).

summary: Each display capture re-enumerates SCShareableContent, and a display that is absent from the result is silently replaced by a different display instead of failing.
evidence: ScreenshotOverlay.swift:63-72 loops `for screen in screens { shots.append((screen, try await Self.captureDisplay(screen))) }`, and captureDisplay starts with `let content = try await SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows(false, onScreenWindowsOnly: true)` (line 372) — one full shareable-content enumeration per display. Lines 373-375: `guard let display = content.displays.first(where: { $0.displayID == displayID }) ?? content.displays.first else { throw CaptureError.noDisplay }`. `displayID` is `(deviceDescription["NSScreenNumber"] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0` (1276-1278).
failure: Displays are unplugged/asleep (or the NSScreenNumber key is missing → displayID 0) between the `NSScreen.screens` snapshot (line 60) and this call → the guard falls back to `content.displays.first` and the *wrong* display's pixels are captured. `present()` still builds the canvas against the original `screen.frame`/`backingScaleFactor` (87-118) and `freezeLayer.contentsGravity = .resize` (597) stretches them, so the user gets a frozen image of another monitor, offset and blurry, with no error. Secondary cost: N displays means N enumerations of every on-screen window before anything is captured.
fix: Enumerate once in `run()` (`let content = try await SCShareableContent...`), pass the matching `SCDisplay` into `captureDisplay`, and `throw CaptureError.noDisplay` when it is missing instead of substituting `content.displays.first`.

summary: Neither screenshot file has any regression, and the two sign-flip conversions (CG window list → Cocoa, view rect → image pixel rect) are exactly the pure functions the suite's slice fixtures exist for.
evidence: `grep -rl 'Screenshot|Snip|CGEvent|Carbon|ScreenCaptureKit|SCShareableContent' Tests/` returns only Tests/e2e-codex-tree.py (an unrelated build of a helper), and no suite in `TEST_SUITES` (Makefile:6) names screenshots. The untested pure logic: the y-flip at ScreenshotOverlay.swift:462 `let cocoa = CGRect(x: x, y: originY - y - h, width: w, height: h)` plus the cross-screen clip at 470-476, and the crop flip at 754-760 `let scaleX = CGFloat(cgImage.width) / bounds.width ... y: (bounds.height - sel.maxY) * scaleY ... .integral` with `cgImage.cropping(to: pixel)`. Both files were touched by the recent review rounds (git log 6048ec0, 199181e), and every other Utils file of this size has a slice fixture (core-regressions.py, access-log-tail-regressions.py, capture-retention-regressions.py).

summary: The committed table holds Hong Kong Observatory (UTC+8) civil dates, but lookup compares the observer's local (month, day), so for observers west of UTC+8 every term and season boundary flips one day late.
evidence: Header, lines 8-12: dates come from HKO conversion tables and 'agree with the apparent-solar-longitude crossings'. Lines 102-108 build a Gregorian calendar from the caller's `calendar.timeZone` (default `.current`) and 114/126 compare `(month, day)` against the HKO rows; nothing carries the table's own zone. I solved the crossings with an independent low-precision NOAA-style solver, first checking it reproduces all 120 committed rows in Asia/Shanghai. Shift counts per 120 term-days: America/Los_Angeles 73 (season openers 12/20), Europe/London 28 (5/20), Pacific/Auckland 25 (2/20), Asia/Tokyo 5. Example, 2026 (HKT -> local): springBegins 2026-02-04 04:03 -> 2026-02-03 12:03 PST; autumnBegins 2026-08-07 19:50 -> 2026-08-07 04:50 PST. The 'Outside the table the nearest year is reused: a one-day drift cannot move a season' note (line 14) only covers the year clamp, not this zone shift.
failure: A user in Seattle on 2026-02-03 after 12:00 local: `season(on:)` still returns .winter because the table says 立春 is (2, 4), so GreetingPhrase.forDate (GreetingPhrase.swift:146-152) serves winter verse pools for the rest of that day — and the same one-day lag hits 73/120 term days, including 12 of the 20 season openers across 2026-2030.
fix: Resolve the date in the table's own zone: interpret the committed entries as UTC+8 civil dates and compare against `Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)` with `TimeZone(identifier: "Asia/Hong_Kong")` in `components(_:calendar:)`, leaving every caller's `calendar` irrelevant to the term lookup. Keep the committed table as is.
verdict_note: The HKO series was fetched through 2036 and the table extended to match (2026–2036, 2027–2030 verified identical to the rows already committed); `schedule` clamps to the new edge. `solar-term-regressions.py` now checks all 24 terms × 11 years against the HKO transcription, and pins 2033-02-03 as 立春 — the day the 2030 row's reuse got wrong.

summary: `schedule()` cancels the previous DispatchWorkItem but the item never checks `isCancelled`, so a cancelled item still runs `handler()`; after `stop()` a late item still fires a full `refreshUsage(rescan: true)` while no window is visible.
evidence: UsageFSWatcher.swift:83-87 `debounceWork?.cancel(); let work = DispatchWorkItem { handler() }; debounceWork = work; lock.unlock(); queue.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 0.4, execute: work)`. `DispatchWorkItem.cancel()` does not dequeue an already-enqueued item and the closure has no `isCancelled` guard (contrast ProxyCaptureStore.swift:898-903, whose comment is exactly this rule: "must not enqueue a cancelled main-queue item for every token"). `stop()` (:53-59) cancels the pending item and nils `handler`, but the item's captured closure still runs at T+0.4 → ProviderStore.swift:1233-1234 `DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.refreshUsage(rescan: true) }`. `refreshUsage` is not visibility-gated; only the stream is (ProviderStore.swift:650-660: "With no window on screen the re-index is pure background cost; stop the stream and let the next visible poll rescan").
failure: Close the popup / hide the window within 0.4 s of any transcript event (routine when a session is live) → the cancelled item still runs and executes a full `UsageIndex.updateIndex()` corpus pass off the visibility gate: directory enumeration of ~2,500 transcripts, re-parse of changed files, and — with the UsageClaims defect above — a 32 MB claims rewrite, all while the app is supposed to be idle.
fix: Have the item re-check state under the lock before calling through, e.g. `let work = DispatchWorkItem { lock.lock(); let handler = Self.handler; lock.unlock(); handler?() }` — `stop()` clears `handler`, so a stopped watcher's late item becomes a no-op while a rescheduled one (same handler) still debounces correctly.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: the DispatchWorkItem is created per schedule() call and cancelled items are never re-scheduled by stop(); a late fire after cancel cannot happen because schedule() always cancels and replaces the previous item first.

summary: Codex session-family parent links are read from only the first 64 KiB of the rollout, while the sibling parser of the same record deliberately reads up to 2 MiB — a large session_meta line silently drops the parent link.
evidence: Line 403: `let data = try? handle.read(upToCount: 65_536)` then line 405 `data?.split(separator: 10).first` must parse as one JSON object; anything larger arrives truncated and the `try? JSONSerialization` fails, so `header` stays nil and line 415 caches `nil` for that path (re-read on every mtime/size change, still nil). The first record is `session_meta` whose `base_instructions` carries the whole system prompt: measured on this machine, `~/.codex/sessions/2026/10/04/*.jsonl` first lines are 22,895–22,913 bytes (likely to grow past 64 KiB with larger instructions).
