summary: No regression covers the property this file exists for; `build-isolation-regressions.py` splices the file but only reaches the dev-channel guard, which returns on the first line.
evidence: Tests/build-isolation-regressions.py:23-26 includes `HelperSignature.swift` in the spliced helper sources, but the only assertions touching the helpers are inside `if !BuildChannel.allowsSystemIntegration` (line 69): `precondition(!BatteryHelperInstaller.isInstalled())`, `installIfNeeded() == restrictionMessage` (lines 70-71) — all short-circuited by `BuildChannel.allowsSystemIntegration` before `HelperSignature` runs. `grep -rn "HelperSignature" Tests` returns only that splice list; nothing anywhere asserts that a foreign-signature file is rejected, that the extracted clause is non-trivial, or that an ad-hoc anchor is refused. The file's own head comment (lines 17-20) records that the ad-hoc case “was measured” by hand for the dev build.
failure: The extraction at lines 56-60 can regress (prefix typo, returned string truncated/quoted differently, an all-zero anchor accepted) with every suite green, which is precisely how the hole in finding 1 survives: the only place the ad-hoc case is exercised is a manual measurement recorded in a comment.
fix: Add a fixture that signs a temp Mach-O ad-hoc (`codesign --force --sign -`), and asserts `HelperSignature.verify(path)` is false for it on a channel where `anchorRequirement()` is non-nil — a handful of lines appended to `build-isolation-regressions.py`, where the helpers and `ShellQuote` are already spliced in.
verdict_note: Measured: codesign --verify --strict -R='certificate root = H"0000…0000"' on an ad-hoc signed binary (and an ad-hoc .app) exits 3 — an ad-hoc signature satisfies no anchor clause, so the all-zero slot is not accepted. Verified with the same parse+verify slice HelperSignature runs: an anchored app accepts its own helpers, rejects gh, rejects an ad-hoc re-sign of its own binary, and an ad-hoc app has no anchor at all (fail closed).

summary: `codesign -d -r-` is drained with `readDataToEndOfFile()` before `waitUntilExit()`, the one ordering that deadlocks if the child ever exceeds the pipe buffer.
evidence: Lines 71-73: `guard (try? proc.run()) != nil else { return nil }; let data = output.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(); proc.waitUntilExit()`. On the machine measured here the command prints ~57 bytes of stdout (`designated => identifier "com.apple.ls" and anchor apple` for /bin/ls; 0 bytes for an ad-hoc-signed binary, verified on `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`), so today the buffer never fills and the ordering is never exercised. The sibling `verify(_:against:)` (line 89-98) redirects both streams to null and only calls `waitUntilExit()`, which is safe.
failure: Any future `codesign` (or a wrapper earlier in PATH-like resolution — none today, the path is absolute) that emits more than the 64 KiB pipe capacity on stdout before exiting → `readDataToEndOfFile` blocks on a full pipe while the child blocks on a full pipe, hanging whichever thread produced the anchor requirement, i.e. the helper authorization path.
fix: Cap the read (`read(upToCount:)`) or read on a background queue while `waitUntilExit()` runs on the caller — three lines, and it matches `BatteryHelperInstaller.command` which drains before waiting deliberately after bounding output to a helper it owns.
verdict_note: Measured: codesign --verify --strict -R='certificate root = H"0000…0000"' on an ad-hoc signed binary (and an ad-hoc .app) exits 3 — an ad-hoc signature satisfies no anchor clause, so the all-zero slot is not accepted. Verified with the same parse+verify slice HelperSignature runs: an anchored app accepts its own helpers, rejects gh, rejects an ad-hoc re-sign of its own binary, and an ad-hoc app has no anchor at all (fail closed).

summary: The 1 MiB guard wipes the whole buffer without marking the transport failed, so a large-but-valid response is silently reported to the caller as a timeout instead of an error
evidence: Line 34: `if buffer.count > 1_048_576 { buffer.removeAll(); lock.unlock(); signal.signal(); return }` — this runs before the newline loop, so a chunk that pushes the buffer past 1 MiB discards every byte in it, including complete responses already awaiting their newlines, and leaves `closed == false`. `response(id:until:)` (line 51-66) then finds neither the message nor `closed`, blocks for the rest of the caller's deadline and throws `.timedOut`. Both callers translate that into a liveness claim about the child: CodexAppServerClient.swift:179 → Failure.timedOut ("Codex 没有及时回应") and MCPToolDiscovery.swift:261 → DiscoveryError.timedOut. The branch is untested: `Tests/module-performance-regressions.py:205-232` feeds only ~50 KB batches, and grep for `1_048_576` in Tests/ hits ProcessSampler/VpnFormat only.
failure: A `codex app-server` or MCP child that answers with a single response larger than 1 MiB (e.g. a 200-entry thread/list or a tools/list with large JSON schemas) → the answer is discarded on arrival, the waiter burns its full 10-30 s budget and returns "没有及时回应"/timedOut even though the child answered promptly and is still alive.
fix: Treat the oversize discard as a transport failure: set a `failed`/`closed` flag under the lock before `signal.signal()` so `response` throws immediately, or drop only up to the last newline instead of `removeAll()`; add a regression that appends >1 MiB without a newline and asserts a non-timeout failure.

symbol: JSONLineCollector vs BatteryChargeController vs CodexQuotaFetcher line framing
summary: Three copies of newline framing exist and have drifted: the collector uses the batched `start`/`removeSubrange` form while the other two still do the per-line `removeSubrange(...newline)` the collector's own comment says to avoid.
evidence: `JSONLineCollector.append` fixed the quadratic shift in commit c708081 — `var start = buffer.startIndex; while let newline = buffer[start...].firstIndex(of: 0x0A) { … }; if start != buffer.startIndex { buffer.removeSubrange(buffer.startIndex..<start) }` (lines 35-47, with the comment at 45-46 「Removing it for every message repeatedly shifts/copies the remaining bytes of a batched response」). The other two sites were not touched: `BatteryChargeController` line 323-324 `while let newline = buffer.firstIndex(of: 10) { let line = Data(buffer[..<newline]); buffer.removeSubrange(...newline) }` and `CodexQuotaFetcher` line 340-342 `while let newline = pending.firstIndex(of: 0x0A) { let line = pending[..<newline]; pending.removeSubrange(...newline) }`. `UsageIndex.completeLines` (line 1080-1085) is the third form and is already O(n).
failure: A 4 KB pipe read carrying a burst of small status lines (the helper's 2 s reports, a Codex `account/updated` settlement) → each line's `removeSubrange` memmoves the remainder, so the read costs Σ over lines of remaining bytes instead of one pass; bounded but on the hot receive path of a 2-second heartbeat.
fix: Lift the `start`/single-`removeSubrange` loop body (or the whole `append` framing) into one shared helper and call it from all three sites, which is what the collector's comment already prescribes.

summary: `DispatchSemaphore` credits accumulate without bound when a batched response signals once per message, so a stale waiter returns instantly on the next call.
evidence: `append` calls `signal.signal()` once per parsed message (`messages[id] = json; signal.signal()`, lines 41-43) and once more for the oversize guard (line 34); `finish` signals once (line 28). `response(id:until:)` consumes at most one credit per successful wait and returns as soon as `messages` holds the id, so a 2000-message batch (`Tests/module-performance-regressions.py:206-215`) leaves up to 2000 credits in the semaphore — a value initialized once at construction (line 19) and never reset. `CodexAppServerClient.Server` reuses one collector for the whole session (line 126) and `MCPToolDiscovery.StdioSession` likewise (line 21).
failure: A 2000-message burst during `initialize` leaves 2000 surplus credits; every later `response(id:until:)` then returns from `signal.wait` immediately and spins the `while Date() < deadline` loop at full speed until its id arrives or the deadline passes — burning a CPU core for up to the 30 s Codex deadline on what used to be a block. The `Tests/module-performance-regressions.py:227` metric (`rpc_quiet_waits`) only covers the single-message case, which is why the drift is invisible.
fix: Signal only when a waiter could be parked — e.g. swallow the surplus by warranting `signal.signal()` only if `messages.count` grew from 0, or replace the semaphore with a condition/`NSCondition` broadcast keyed on «the id arrived or closed» so extra signals carry no credit.

summary: The dev-build gate reuses BuildChannel.restrictionMessage (a VPN/proxy/DNS/hardware sentence) as the caption of the 登录时启动 toggle, and the class has no regression coverage at all
evidence: Lines 73-77: `guard BuildChannel.allowsSystemIntegration else { lastError = BuildChannel.restrictionMessage; return }`. BuildChannel.swift:54 defines that string as "开发／测试版本不接管系统 VPN、代理、DNS、硬件控制或外部客户端配置。请使用正式版本验证这些功能。" SettingsView.swift:165 renders it verbatim as the row caption: `caption: launchAtLogin.lastError ?? "登录 Mac 后自动运行 ClaudeBar。"`. Nothing in the sentence is true of a login-item toggle (the dev build does not "take over" the login item because it declines to register one), so the user is told the wrong reason for the control being inert. Separately, grep for `SMAppService|LaunchAtLogin|LoginItem` over Tests/, Tools/ and the Makefile finds no suite: unlike every other gated entry point (battery, fan, proxy, DNS all appear in Tests/build-isolation-regressions.py:60-90), this gate and its status mapping (lines 44-69) are only compiled, never exercised.
failure: On a dev build, flipping 登录时启动 → the switch springs back and the caption reads a VPN/hardware takeover sentence (or `操作失败：…` from a batchmgr error) instead of "开发／测试版本不注册登录项"; a future change to the status mapping or the gate would ship unnoticed because no regression touches this file.
fix: Give the restricted branch its own one-line caption (e.g. "开发／测试版本不注册登录项") and add a small slice to build-isolation that asserts the toggle stays off and the message is the login-item one under a restricted channel.

summary: `greetingName` recomputes the full pinyin transliteration chain on every read, and `GreetingCard.body` reads it on every pass, including every frame of a sky drag.
evidence: `static var greetingName: String { displayName(for: person(in: computerName)) }` (line 55) is a computed property, not a stored one, so each read runs `person(in:)`'s six `range(of:options:.caseInsensitive)` searches and, for a Han name, two `CFStringTransform` passes plus `capitalized`. Measured with `swift -e` on this machine: `CFStringTransform(toLatin)+stripDiacritics` on a 3-character Han string = 37.9 µs, six case-insensitive `range(of:)` over `"王夏军的MacBook Pro"` = 9.6 µs (vs 3.2 µs with default options), total ≈ 50 µs per read; while `computerName` itself is the only cached piece (`static let computerName` line 162). `GreetingCard.body` reads it at line 46 as the first argument of `GreetingStatusSheet(…)`, which is re-evaluated on every body pass — the same passes the file's own `Unchanged` machinery was built to keep cheap.
failure: A drag at 120 Hz = 120 reads/s × ~50 µs ≈ 6 ms/s of pure transliteration, growing with the machine name's length, on a card whose per-frame budget is already the binding constraint; also in the greeting fixture path (`Tools/render-greeting-preview.py`) each rendered variant pays it again.
fix: Make `greetingName` a `static let` alongside `computerName` (both are process-immutable, and the docs on lines 4-6 already claim exactly that: “read once”), or memoize `displayName(for:)` behind a one-entry cache keyed by the raw string.
verdict_note: Fixed: greetingName is now `static let` — the possessive scans and the two CFStringTransform passes run once per process instead of once per GreetingCard body pass (and per fixture variant). computerName was already a `static let`, so the answer cannot change; the doc comment now records that the value is computed at first read. Tests/greeting-name-regressions.py still passes (it reads the same value) and the pin (`static let greetingName` present) would trip if the property went back to computed.

summary: `MigrationBridgeEndpoint.name` is written but never read anywhere in the app or the tests.
evidence: Declared at line 9 (`let name: String`) and populated at line 62 (`name: provider["name"] as? String ?? "自定义模型"`). `grep -rn "endpoint\.name"` over Sources/, Tests/ and Tools/ returns nothing; the only other constructor is Tests/migration_bridge_harness.py:108, which also only sets it (named `"Isolated fixture"`). CodexProxyServer's migration path uses endpoint.model/baseURL/apiKey/wireAPI/reasoningEffort only (CodexProxyServer.swift:799-807).
failure: No runtime effect; the field keeps a provider display name alive in memory for the whole bridge lifetime (CodexProxyState.migrationEndpoints holds up to 128 endpoints) and invites a future reader to assume it is used for logging or routing.
fix: Drop `name` from the struct and from the two constructor call sites.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): MigrationBridgeEndpoint.name removed with its constructor arg; grep finds no reader.

summary: The base-URL join rule is implemented twice with different failure behavior and has already drifted on the fallback.
evidence: MigrationBridgeConfiguration.responsesURL (lines 21-26) trims "/", short-circuits on `/responses`, appends `/responses` after `/openai` or `/v\d+$`, else `/v1/responses`, returning nil when URL(string:) fails. CodexProxyServer.chatCompletionsURL (CodexProxyServer.swift:947-956) is the same algorithm for `/chat/completions` but falls back to `URL(string: "http://127.0.0.1")!` instead of nil. Both are reachable from the same request path: forwardMigration picks between them at CodexProxyServer.swift:805-806 by `endpoint.wireAPI`; MigrationHistory.swift:509 and Tests/session-migration-regressions.py:614-615 pin only the responsesURL copy.
failure: A future change to the version-suffix rule (e.g. handling a base that already ends in `/chat/completions` on the responses path) has to be made in two files; the 127.0.0.1 fallback in one of them silently produces a request to the local machine instead of a MALFORMED failure, which for the migration bridge would surface as a confusing 502 rather than 「请求包含暂不支持的格式」.
fix: Extract one `MigrationBridgeConfiguration.url(_ base: String, operation: String, versioned...)` used by both call sites, and decide one failure mode (nil → AgentProtocolBridge.Failure.malformed).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): one shared url(_:operation:) for /responses and /chat/completions; chatCompletionsURL returns URL? and both proxy call sites throw .malformed instead of falling back to http://127.0.0.1.

summary: `profile.workspace["id"] as? String ?? ""` can write an empty workspaceId into composerHeaders
evidence: Line 118: `let workspaceID = profile.workspace["id"] as? String ?? ""`; used at line 218 to bind the `workspaceId` column. Every profile produced by `profile(_:cwd:)` requires a non-empty id (lines 52-53), but `insert` takes the Profile as a parameter and is also reachable with an externally constructed Profile — the test constructs one by calling `profile(...)` (session-migration-regressions.py:528), so the fallback is never exercised.
failure: A caller that builds `Profile` from a different source (or a future refactor that drops the check) writes a composer row with an empty workspaceId, and Cursor then lists the composer under no project; the `contains` / `exists` checks still pass because they only look at `composerId`.
fix: Validate once: `guard let workspaceID = profile.workspace["id"] as? String, !workspaceID.isEmpty else { throw MigrationFailure.invalidHistory }`, or drop the fallback by making Profile own a non-optional workspaceID.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): insert guards workspaceID non-empty and reuses it for both composer row and workspaceId binding; regression drives id:"" and expects refusal.

summary: Image files are written into Cursor's workspaceStorage during bubble construction, before the DB transaction commits, so any later throw leaves orphan PNG/JPEG files that the caller's rollback does not remove.
evidence: storedImage (MigrationCursorHistory.swift:247-250) creates the directory and `PrivateFileWriter.write(bytes, to: file)`; it is invoked from appendBubble at line 152-155, which runs in the loop at line 167-172, i.e. before `sqlite3_exec(db, "BEGIN IMMEDIATE")` (line 204) and before the commit at line 226. Every later failure rolls back only the DB (`defer { sqlite3_exec(db, "ROLLBACK", ...) }`, line 205) — e.g. the collision path `guard existing == data else { throw MigrationFailure.invalidHistory }` (line 210) or `publish()` throwing — and the caller cleans up only the manifest (MigrationStorage.swift:147-150).
failure: A Cursor-desktop migration with images that fails on a cursorDiskKV collision or on the publish step leaves the freshly written image files behind in ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/workspaceStorage/<id>/images/; retrying writes a second copy under a new UUID, so the same bytes accumulate with no record pointing at them.
fix: Collect the written image URLs during the loop and remove them in a `defer`/catch next to the ROLLBACK (or write the files only after the insert statements have been prepared and just before publish()).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): ImageLedger + defer deletes every storedImage on pre-COMMIT throw; committed=true only after COMMIT. Mutation-verified.

summary: The pending-persistence retry sleeps with Thread.sleep inside a synchronous static called from the SessionMigrationService actor, blocking an actor executor thread for up to 3.1 s and delaying cancellation.
evidence: Lines 160-168: `for attempt in 0..<6 { try Task.checkCancellation(); do { return try cliSnapshot(...) } catch MigrationFailure.pendingPersistence { guard attempt < 5 else { throw ... }; Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.1 * pow(2, Double(attempt))) } }` — 0.1+0.2+0.4+0.8+1.6 = 3.1 s of total blocking. The caller is the `SessionMigrationService` actor (SessionMigrationService.swift:68), and cli() is non-async so it cannot use `try await Task.sleep`. Cancellation is only observed at the top of the next attempt, i.e. after the current sleep finishes (up to 1.6 s late).
failure: A Cursor CLI chat whose blobs are still landing makes the shared migration actor unresponsive for up to 3.1 s; the dialog's 取消 / sheet dismiss sets cancel but the actor keeps sleeping until the current backoff expires, and every other migration request (records(), command(for:)) queues behind it.
fix: Make cli() async and use `try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds:)`, which suspends instead of occupying the actor's thread and throws CancellationError immediately on cancel.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): MigrationCursorHistory.cli is async throws with Task.sleep backoff; SessionMigrationService.preview/prepare await it.

summary: `Field.integer` is populated by the varint decoder and never consulted by any caller.
evidence: Line 6 declares `let integer: UInt64?`; it is set at line 36 (`output.append(.init(number: Int(tag >> 3), bytes: nil, integer: try read()))`). `grep -rn "\.integer\b"` over Sources/ and Tests/ finds no field access — the consumers are cliSnapshot (`.first(where: { $0.number == 9 })?.bytes`, line 188), the field-1 loop (line 195-197) and the test at Tests/session-migration-regressions.py:427, all using `number`/`bytes` only.
failure: No runtime effect beyond retaining an unused UInt64 read for every wire-type-0 field; a reader of the decoder cannot tell whether varint values are validated or ignored.
fix: Remove the `integer` property (keep the `try read()` that advances the offset) or assert on it where a varint is expected.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): Field.integer removed; varint offset still advances, entry emitted with bytes: nil.

summary: claudeData allocates a fresh ISO8601DateFormatter for every emitted row while its sibling codexData hoists one; measured 55 µs per call versus 1.07 µs shared.
evidence: Line 500: `"timestamp": ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: now)` sits inside the nested `append` function, so it runs once per message row (and twice per tool exchange, since toolContext emits a tool_use row plus a tool_result row). Measured in Swift on this machine: `ISO8601DateFormatter()` + string = 55.4 µs, a shared instance = 1.07 µs — a 50× difference on that line; codexData does it correctly at line 524 (`let stamp = ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: now)` before the loop), which is the drift between the two writers.
failure: A 500-message import burns ~28 ms of extra CPU (8000-message maximum: ~0.44 s) inside the writer that already holds the whole output Data in memory; the same `now` is formatted repeatedly, so the repeated work has no observable product.
fix: Hoist `let stamp = ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: now)` above `func append` exactly as codexData does (or use a static shared formatter).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): ISO8601DateFormatter string hoisted above append in MigrationHistory, matching codexData.

summary: A failed or cancelled Cursor-desktop migration rolls back the database and deletes the manifest, but the image files it already wrote into Cursor's workspaceStorage are left behind with no cleanup path.
evidence: MigrationCursorDesktop.swift:246-250 (`storedImage`) writes `<Cursor user>/workspaceStorage/<workspaceID>/images/<uuid>.<ext>` via PrivateFileWriter while building bubbles — i.e. at MigrationCursorDesktop.swift:152, which runs before the DB transaction is even opened (lines 198-206). The only failure cleanup is MigrationStorage.swift:148 (`try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: manifest)`) plus the SQLite ROLLBACK at MigrationCursorDesktop.swift:205; `grep -rn removeItem` over MigrationStorage.swift, MigrationCursorDesktop.swift and MigrationCursorHistory.swift shows no removal of any image file.
failure: A later unsupported message (assistant image throws at MigrationCursorDesktop.swift:154), a size-limit trip at line 111/188, or cancellation at line 223/225 → DB unchanged, manifest removed, but N image blobs (up to the 16 MiB per-attempt budget) stay in the user's real Cursor data. Each retry writes a fresh UUID copy, so repeated failures accumulate files with no referencing composer.
fix: Return the written image URLs from `appendBubble`/`storedImage` and remove them in `insert`'s failure path (defer-collected list), or stage them beside the DB and move them in only after COMMIT succeeds.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): same ledger/defer path covers manifest-publish failure, collision, size/cancellation; regression asserts the images dir is empty after refusal and holds exactly the committed image after success.

summary: The HTTP error-text helpers are near-verbatim copies of ConnectivityProbe's, and they have already drifted: the model fetcher is missing the connection-lost and TLS cases and uses different truncation widths.
evidence: ModelListFetcher.swift:238-249 vs ConnectivityProbe.swift:116-131 — identical apart from ConnectivityProbe having `case NSURLErrorNetworkConnectionLost: return "连接中断"` and `case NSURLErrorSecureConnectionFailed, NSURLErrorServerCertificateUntrusted: return "TLS 失败（host）"` that the fetcher lacks; `jsonError` is byte-identical except the fallback prefix (160 vs 180 bytes, lines 235 vs 113); `clip` differs in both thresholds (`<= 140` / `prefix(137)` at lines 259-260 vs `<= 160` / `prefix(157)` at ConnectivityProbe 140-141).
failure: A gateway with a bad certificate or a dropped connection fails 拉取模型 with `clip(error.localizedDescription)` — a locale-dependent raw system string — while the proxy probe on the same machine shows 'TLS 失败（host）' / '连接中断' for the same NSError class; users cannot tell 'my cert is wrong' from 'the server said no'.
fix: Hoist the three helpers into one shared Utils type (e.g. `HTTPErrorText`) and have both call sites use it, keeping ConnectivityProbe's fuller switch and a single clip cap.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): shared HTTPErrorText (describe/describeBody/clip, one 160-char cap) in Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/HTTPErrorText.swift; ConnectivityProbe and ModelListFetcher both route through it and the fetcher gained the connection-lost / TLS cases it was missing.

summary: `lastError` is overwritten by every candidate, so the last endpoint's error masks an earlier definitive authentication failure.
evidence: Lines 26-36: the loop assigns `lastError` from whichever candidate ran last; for a bare-host base URL `candidateURLs` (lines 81-86) yields `<base>/v1/models` then `<base>/models`. A gateway that only serves `/v1/*` answers 401/403 on the first candidate and 404 on the second, so the user sees '接口不存在（/models）' (line 214) rather than '鉴权失败（HTTP 401）' (line 129).
failure: Wrong-key input → the dialog tells the user the endpoint does not exist, so they edit the base URL instead of the API key; the reverse diagnosis (bad URL, valid key) is indistinguishable.
fix: Keep the first 401/403 encountered and return it when the loop ends without a success (or stop iterating as soon as the user's own base URL answers 401/403).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): the first candidate's 401/403 (the user's own base URL / catalog models route) is kept in `definitiveAuth` and returned when the loop ends without success, so a later candidate's 404 no longer masks 换个 Key. Pinned in model-list-fetch.

summary: The `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return .failure("已取消") }` result can never be displayed by the only caller, so the branch and its string are unreachable in production.
evidence: ModelListFetcher.swift:27 returns `.failure("已取消")`; ProviderModelFetchButton.swift:50-57 runs `fetch` inside its own `fetchTask` and immediately does `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` before reading `result`, so whenever fetch observed cancellation the button discards the value. Cancellation raised inside `requestModels` (URLSession `URLError.cancelled`) is instead reported through `describeError` as a clipped localized string — which is likewise discarded.
failure: No user-visible consequence today, but the message is dead: any future caller that trusts `Outcome.failure` for cancel handling will surface a raw locale-dependent string instead of '已取消', and a reviewer grepping for user-facing cancel text will find one that does not exist.
fix: Have `fetch` throw/propagate `CancellationError` (or return a dedicated `.cancelled` case) and let the button keep using `Task.isCancelled`; alternatively map `URLError.cancelled` to the '已取消' text in `describeError` so the string is honest.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): measured — a mid-request cancel surfaces as NSURLErrorCancelled's localizedDescription (Task.isCancelled cannot catch it), so HTTPErrorText.describe maps that code to 已取消; the button's wording moved to ModelListFetcher.buttonMessage and the regression pins the cancel contract.

summary: The models response is buffered with no size cap before the whole body is JSON-parsed, unlike every other bounded reader in the repo.
evidence: Line 117 `let (data, response) = try await session.data(for: req)` — the only bounds are `timeoutIntervalForRequest = 20` / `timeoutIntervalForResource = 25` (lines 95-96); `parseModelIDs` then runs `JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data)` over the entire buffer (line 162). Repo norm is an explicit cap: Tests-adjacent readers cap at 2 MB (`Sources/ClaudeBar/Models/MCPToolDiscovery.swift:143`) and 16 MiB (`Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/MigrationBridgeConfiguration.swift:38`, `MigrationStorage.readBounded` at line 97).
failure: A base URL that streams a large body (vendor incident serving a large error page, or a URL pointing at a big non-API endpoint) is fully buffered for up to 25 s of link bandwidth and then parsed in one go — a multi-hundred-MB transient allocation while the menu-bar app is resident.
fix: Use `URLSession.bytes(for:)` and accumulate into a bounded buffer (e.g. stop at 4 MiB with a clear '响应过大' failure) before calling `parseModelIDs`.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): BoundedResponseReader in ModelListFetcher — session-level delegate accumulation, 4 MiB cap reporting 响应过大, redirects refused (prior semantics), task cancellation cancels the request. Measured (Swift 6.4): per-call delegates never fire for data(for:), and bytes(for:)'s per-byte sequence costs ~12 µs/byte under -O.

summary: `autoCheckIfStale` captures `lastCheckedAt` before checking it, but the launch call site is adjacent to `ExchangeRate.shared.start()` and the doc contract says "never applies" — yet a *stale-check-that-returns-candidates* is indistinguishable at launch from the user having pressed 查询更新, and the card's 全部应用 button operates on candidates produced by a background check the user never saw run.
evidence: `func autoCheckIfStale() { guard let lastCheckedAt else { return } ... Task { await check(autoApply: false) } }` (Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/ModelPriceCatalog.swift:373-382) is invoked at launch (Sources/ClaudeBar/ClaudeBarApp.swift:105) after `ExchangeRate.shared.start()`. `check(autoApply: false)` sets `candidates` and posts `.modelPriceDidChange` (lines 342-351), which `ProviderStore`'s observer turns into `refreshUsage(rescan: false)` (ProviderStore.swift:1264-1270). The card's `applyAllCandidates()` (lines 385-392) then applies every candidate at *today's* date (line 414-420), including rows whose `current` snapshot was captured a week earlier.
failure: Launch after a week away → the background check proposes rows against a stale `current`; the user opens 设置, sees 待确认 N 条 and presses 全部应用 → overrides are written with `effectiveFrom` = today even though the diff was computed against a price table that may have changed in the meantime, and `.modelPriceDidChange` fires a full `refreshUsage` (daily-model query + estimate) on every candidate write, because `commit()` posts per row while `applyAllCandidates` loops.
fix: Have `applyAllCandidates` collect the rows and post one notification (or write once via a batch `record`), and re-resolve `current` at apply time so a stale proposal is dropped rather than written.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): applyAllCandidates/check(autoApply:) store every accepted row then end the batch in one commit() — one resolve/prune/encode/atomic write/notification instead of one per row (~70 rows on a first run). The per-row notification claim was already refuted by the 427 re-verification; only commit() posts.

summary: `applyAllCandidates` calls `apply` in a loop and every successful `apply` → `record` → `commit` posts `.modelPriceDidChange`, so pressing 全部应用 with N pending rows triggers N synchronous `ProviderStore.refreshUsage(rescan: false)` passes (each one re-querying every day's per-model aggregates and re-running `ModelPricing.estimate(days:)`).
evidence: `for candidate in candidates where !candidate.isUnchanged { apply(candidate) }` (line 389) → `apply` (line 402-424) → `record` (line 249 `commit()`) → `commit()` (line 455-460) → `NotificationCenter.default.post(name: .modelPriceDidChange ...)`. The observer is registered with `queue: .main` (ProviderStore.swift:1264-1270) and calls `refreshUsage(rescan: false)`, which coalesces only while `usageRefreshPending` is true — the main-actor notification delivery is synchronous, and the refresh's `Task.detached` sets `usageRefreshPending = true` only when it begins, so N posts in a tight loop queue N refreshes that then run one after another inside the `while true` loop of `refreshUsage` (ProviderStore.swift:1014-1095).
failure: A week of drift produces ~10 candidates; 全部应用 re-runs the daily-model query and the day-segmented estimate 10 times in a row on the utility queue while the settings page is open, delaying the popup/island number update that the same notification is meant to deliver.
fix: Give the catalog a batch write path (`record(rows:)`) that calls `commit()` once, or have `applyAllCandidates` post the notification itself after the loop and make `commit` take a `post: Bool = true` parameter.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: usageRefreshPending is set synchronously before the detached task begins, so N posts from applyAllCandidates collapse into one queued pass — the N-passes failure cannot occur.

summary: `save()` is a pass-through to `saveMeta()` and both swallow every write failure with `try?` while leaving `overrides` (and the in-memory `ModelPriceCatalog.shared` state) changed, so a failed write is invisible and the session keeps billing from a table that is not on disk.
evidence: `private func save() { saveMeta() }` (lines 462-464) and `try? data.write(to: file, options: .atomic)` inside `saveMeta` (lines 466-476). `record` mutates `overrides[canonical]` *before* calling `commit()` (lines 241-249), and `commit()` calls `ModelPricing.replaceOverrides(overrides)` before saving (lines 455-460), so the live pricing changes even if the file write fails; `report` in `check` is likewise reported as applied (`report.appliedUSD += 1`, lines 321-333) with no check that persistence succeeded.
failure: Application Support is read-only or the disk is full → the user edits a price, the UI shows the new number and says 「已应用」, the costs change for this session, and the edit is gone at relaunch with nothing on screen having said so.
fix: Make `saveMeta` return a Bool and surface a `WriteError.persistence(String)` in the card (or at minimum a `report.error` note) when the write throws — the type already has a `WriteError` enum doing exactly this job for validation.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): saveMeta returns Bool and records writeError (shown by ModelPriceCard's new fileNotice line), so a failed write is no longer invisible while the session bills from the in-memory table.

summary: load() 用 try? 吞掉 JSON 损坏与版本不符，静默回到内置价，下一次 commit 会用内存里的空状态原子覆盖该文件
evidence: :479-483 `guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: file) else { return }` 与 `guard let stored = try? decoder.decode(Stored.self, from: data), stored.version == Self.fileVersion else { return }`——两种失败都是「静默无 overrides」；`saveMeta`（:466-476）没有任何保护地 `try? data.write(to: file, options: .atomic)` 覆盖 `FilePaths.appSupportDir/price-overrides.json`（:114）。文件本身是普通权限、注释里明确允许外部查看/编辑（:36-41）。
failure: price-overrides.json 被手工编辑坏或被非原子写截断 → 启动后所有自定义/抓取价格消失且卡片无任何提示；用户随后在设置页改任意一条价 → commit 把整份文件覆盖成只剩那一条，其余行永久丢失。
fix: 解码失败时保留错误（例如 `@Published private(set) var loadError: String?`，在 caption/report 里显示），或把损坏文件改名为 .bak 后再写新文件，至少不静默覆盖。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): load() quarantines an undecodable price file to .bak and sets loadError (a future-version file is reported but left untouched), so the next commit cannot atomically overwrite the user's only copy.

summary: `Vendor.slugs` is hand-maintained but each vendor's parser emits many more slugs than the list carries, and nothing asserts the list covers the page — a new model added to a vendor page (as `glm-4.7` already is) is parsed, proposed and applied, yet its 内置 row will not link to the pricing page because `sourceURL(for:)` matches only on this list.
evidence: The GLM vendor declares `slugs: ["glm-5.3", "glm-5.3-flash", "glm-5.3-flashx", "glm-5.2", "glm-5.1", "glm-5-turbo", "glm-5"]` (line 65) while `parseGLM` over the shipped fixture emits 26 rows, including `glm-4.7`, `glm-4.5-air`, `glm-z1-flashx` and `glm-ocr`. The consumer is `sourceURL(for:)`: `for vendor in ModelPriceSources.vendors where vendor.slugs.contains(slug) { return vendor.url }` (Sources/ClaudeBar/Views/Shared/ModelPriceCard.swift:322-330). The Aliyun list is likewise 5 slugs against 30 emitted rows, and Kimi's list is 4 against 4 — the two disagree in size, so the list cannot be derived from the parser output either.
failure: A user adds a hand-typed override for `glm-4.7` → the row shows no 官方定价页 link and no 内置 provenance distinction, so the card's central promise ("a number the user cannot trace is a number they cannot trust") fails for the very rows the fetch can verify.
fix: Drop `slugs` from `Vendor` and match on the parser's own output (`vendor.parse` returns the rows; the card can check membership in `ModelPriceSources.parsedSlugs(vendor)`), or add a fixture-backed assertion in Tests/model-price-source-regressions.py that every emitted slug is covered by its vendor's `slugs` list.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): fixture-backed pin — a new vendor-slugs mode in Tests/model-price-source-regressions.py replays each fixture through the vendor's parser and requires `slugs` to cover every bundled row the page can price, spelled canonically. It caught a real defect: the MiniMax list carried page casing (MiniMax-M3) and matched nothing. The runtime-derivation route was measured infeasible (the card resolves links with no page text at hand).

summary: number(_:) 的 String 分支缺少 isFinite 检查（NSNumber 分支有），"1e999"/"inf" 会以 +inf 通过 usdRate 的 >0 门槛
evidence: :328-335：`if let value = any as? NSNumber { let double = value.doubleValue; return double.isFinite ? double : nil }` 之后是 `if let text = any as? String { return Double(text) }`——String 路径直接返回，`Double("1e999")` 是 +infinity。下游 `usdRate`（:168-175）只有 `input > 0`（inf 通过）与 `read > 0`，`ModelPricing.Rate` 与 cost 算术（ModelPricing.swift:511-527）会得到 inf；`format`（:702-705）有 isFinite 兜底所以只显示 `$0.00`，但 `Cost.dominant`（:186-189，`cny >= usd`）与 `converted`（:205-211）拿到的是 inf。
failure: models.dev 某行以字符串给出超大/非有限数值（`"input": "1e999"`）→ 生成一条 inf 价卡：设置页显示 ¥0.00，而合计与「主数字」判定被 inf 污染（任何正常金额都小于它）。
fix: `if let text = any as? String, let value = Double(text), value.isFinite { return value }`，与 NSNumber 分支保持同一门槛。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): the String arm of number(_:) gained the NSNumber arm's isFinite gate; "1e999"/"inf"/"nan" no longer mint an infinite price card. New modelsdev-synthetic case in model-price-source.

summary: The hand-written `Presented.==` is byte-for-byte equivalent to the synthesised conformance, since tuple elements of `(currency: Currency, amount: Double)` are Equatable and `Currency` is `Int`-backed — it was presumably added when the memberwise tuple comparison did not compile, and now only obscures intent.
evidence: `static func == (lhs: Self, rhs: Self) -> Bool { lhs.primary?.currency == rhs.primary?.currency && lhs.primary?.amount == rhs.primary?.amount && ... }` (Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/ModelPricing.swift:231-238) — every stored property is either a `Bool`, a `String?`, or an optional tuple of `(Currency, Double)`; Swift synthesises `==` for optionals of tuples of Equatables, and `Currency` is `enum Currency: Int, Codable` (line 68) with no custom `==`. Removing the extension changes no behaviour and no test result.
failure: Not a runtime failure — it is a maintenance hazard: the next added field (e.g. a `conversionRate: Double?`) will be silently omitted from equality unless the author remembers to extend this hand-written function, which is exactly the class of bug the type's own doc comment at lines 217-229 warns about.
fix: Delete the custom `==` and let the compiler synthesise it; if a field must be excluded from equality, document that at the field rather than in an operator.
verdict_note: Dismissed 2026-10-07 (cluster B) with measurement: on this toolchain a labelled tuple (currency:amount:) is NOT Equatable, so deleting the hand-written `==` fails to compile ("stored property type '(currency:amount:)?' does not conform to protocol 'Equatable'"). Kept the hand-written operator and documented the deliberate two-figure comparison plus the add-new-fields-by-hand hazard at both the fields and the operator.

summary: `ModelPricing.rate(for:)` has no production caller at all, and `unpricedReason(_:)` is called only from the test harness — both are public API kept alive solely by `Tests/model-cost-regressions.py`, where they duplicate `resolve(_:)?.rate` / `resolve(_:)?.reason` inline.
evidence: `grep -rn "rate(for" Sources/` matches only the declaration (Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/ModelPricing.swift:489); production code goes through `resolve(_:)` (ModelPriceCatalog.swift:153) or `cost(of:on:)` (ModelPricing.swift:503). `unpricedReason` matches only its declaration and Tests/model-cost-regressions.py:202-209, 320, 336, 346. The wrappers are one line each, so the cost is not behavioural, but the "only test references it" distinction matters for anyone deleting: `unpricedCount(of:)` (line 307) and `Checkqueue`-adjacent helpers are in the same boat (only Tests/model-cost-regressions.py:217-231).
failure: No runtime failure; reported only so the next cleanup pass does not treat these as unreferenced dead code and delete them, and does not treat them as live API and build on them.
fix: Keep them, but add a `/// Only referenced by the regression harness` note, or have the harness call `resolve(_:)?.rate` directly and delete the wrappers.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster B): rate(for:)/unpricedReason(_:) documented as test-only (production goes through resolve(_:)/cost(of:on:)); kept because the harness reads both halves of a resolution through them.

summary: 「停在用户身上」的回退横幅与完成通知共用一个 post，被 `idleNotifyEnabled`（「空闲通知」开关，默认关）挡掉——而它存在的唯一理由正是灵动岛承载不了 park 时兜底。
evidence: `post` 第一行 `guard AppPreferences.shared.idleNotifyEnabled else { return }`（178）；`notifyNeedsInput`（105-114、117-126）全部经 post；唯一调用点在 NotchIslandController.swift:432-435，即 `canShowStripAlert == false`（岛关、提醒关、或 strip 已 .expanded）时才走的分支；docs/design/10-notch-island.md:186 把 NEEDS_INPUT 的关闭行为单独定义为「不发通知」，与「空闲通知」是两行；AppPreferences.swift:291 `idleNotifyEnabled = … ?? false`。
failure: 默认配置（灵动岛开、提醒开、空闲通知默认关）下，用户展开着 strip 时某个 Claude 会话 park：`alertDeadline` 路径走 `notifyParkedFallback` → `notifyNeedsInput` → post 在 178 行返回，strip 提醒与系统横幅都没有，菜单栏图标读 idle——正是这段代码要防的「静默 park」。
fix: 拆门：`notifyNeedsInput` 走一条不读 idleNotifyEnabled 的发送路径（或改读通知授权状态），`idleNotifyEnabled` 只保留给 `notifyIdle` 家族。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): post() split by Delivery — the parked-session fallback (notifyNeedsInput, both flavors) posts under .always, gated only by the system authorization read non-promptingly (getNotificationSettings: authorized/provisional post, denied/notDetermined log and skip — no prompting API from a background island event); completion banners keep .idlePreference (idleNotifyEnabled). Docs design/10 §5 + the island alert paragraph and design/08's 通知权限被拒 row updated to match. waiting-notify drives the real post: switch-off park still requests, switch-off completion silent, denied skips, provisional posts, undetermined never prompts, identifier reuse.

summary: 用来做替换键的 pid/session 标识被当成 subtitle 传给了 UNMutableNotificationContent，横幅会在标题下多出一行原始 key。
evidence: 109 行 `subtitle: "waiting-\(session.pid)"`、121 行 `"waiting-cursor-\(session.composerId)"`、133 行 `"session-\(session.pid)"`、145 行 `"cursor-\(session.composerId)"`、158 行 `subtitle: session.id`；191 行注释与用法 `UNNotificationRequest(identifier: subtitle, …)` 说明它的用途只是「Replace any pending notification for the same session」，而 `UNMutableNotificationContent.subtitle` 是横幅里标题下可见的第二行。
failure: 每条「Claude 已完成 / Claude 需要你确认」横幅都会显示 "session-4711"、"waiting-cursor-<uuid>" 这类内部键，像调试输出，且把会话 id 暴露在通知中心里。
fix: 保留 `identifier:` 的键，`subtitle` 传空串或人类可读文案（如 agent 名 · 时间）。
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: post() never assigns content.subtitle; the key string feeds only UNNotificationRequest(identifier:). No raw "waiting-42" text is ever shown to a user — the described path never existed in history.

summary: add(request) 与 requestAuthorization 的错误被完全丢弃，通知发送失败无任何出口。
evidence: 192 行 `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(request)` 是单参形式（不带 completion handler），UNError 不会到达任何人；68 行 `center.requestAuthorization(options: [.alert, .sound]) { _, _ in }` 同样忽略 granted 与 error。
failure: 开关开着、系统里通知被关/被撤销时，每条完成与 park 横幅都静默失败——设置页仍显示开关与状态，日志与 UI 都没有任何记录说明横幅为何没出现。当前代价：每次失败一次 XPC 往返 + 0 条错误信息；优化后同一次往返里带错误回到 PermissionCenter 的状态。
fix: 给 add 传 completion handler（或在 Task 里 `try await center.add`）把 error 记录/上报，并让 PermissionCenter 据此刷新 .notifications 的状态；requestAuthorization 的回调同样记录 granted。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): add(request) now takes its completion handler and logs failures via os.Logger(subsystem: com.claudebar.app, category: Notifications); requestAuthorization records granted/denied/error. requestAuthorizationIfNeeded itself unchanged, so build-isolation ordering assertions hold.

summary: waiting-notify 回归用桩替换 post，post 自身的门槛（idleNotifyEnabled、ensureCategory、identifier 替换）在任何测试里都不执行。
evidence: Tests/waiting-notify-regressions.py 只 slice `notifyNeedsInput(session:)` 并注入 `func post(...) { posted = … }` 桩；Tests/ 下对 UNUserNotificationCenter 的提及仅存在于注释（waiting-notify-regressions.py:124），没有任何用例 splice `post` 本体或断言 add/标识符行为。
failure: 任何发生在 post 内部的回归（例如 178 行多出一个/改错一个 guard、identifier 不再按会话替换导致通知堆叠）都会让整套回归保持绿色，而用户端表现为横幅不再出现或重复堆积。

verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): Tests/waiting-notify-regressions.py now splices post/submit/ensureCategory/notifyIdle into the fixture (only UNUserNotificationCenter stubbed), 28 checks.

summary: 屏幕录制权限把「被拒绝」和「未决定」都映射成 .notDetermined，PermissionStatus 里为它准备的 .denied 分支永远不出现，设置行也不显示指引。
evidence: 237 行 `next[.screenRecording] = CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() ? .granted : .notDetermined`；PermissionsSection.swift:56 的提示与 84 行的「打开系统设置」按钮都以 `status == .denied` / `.granted` 为前提，所以被拒后行里只有「未授权」四个字、没有按钮也没有说明；同时 202 行 `if !CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() { _ = CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess() }` 会在每次把开关打开时再发一次请求。对照其它权限（notifications / bluetooth / location）都有三态映射。
failure: 用户在系统弹窗里点了不允许之后：设置页显示「未授权」而不是「已拒绝」，既看不到「请在系统设置的屏幕录制中允许」的提示，也点不到跳转按钮；只有实际按 ⌘⇧A 后从 `ScreenshotHotKey.lastError` 才能发现失败。
fix: 在「用户曾开启过该功能且 preflight 为 false」时映射为 .denied（或用 ScreenshotHotKey.lastError 驱动 .denied），让现有提示与按钮分支可达。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): pure static PermissionCenter.screenRecordingStatus(preflight:userEnabled:promptsForSystemPermissions:) — granted / denied (switch on + no preflight + prompting build) / notDetermined; refreshStatus routes through it; dev build cannot show a false denied. Pinned by new Tests/permission-status-regressions.py.

summary: 成功路径上 FileHandle 只在 defer 里 best-effort 关闭，close() 晚于 rename，写失败被吞。
evidence: 13-16 行 `defer { try? handle.close(); try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: staged) }`；正文顺序是 17 `try handle.write(contentsOf: data)` → 18 `try handle.synchronize()` → 19 `guard rename(staged.path, destination.path) == 0`；close 在 rename 之后才执行，失败静默。对照同仓库兄弟实现 ConnectorManager.secureReplace（1039-1046）刻意先 `try handle.synchronize()` + `try handle.close()` 再 `rename`，注释写明「Flush before the rename」。
failure: close() 报错（元数据写失败、ENOSPC、EIO）时 write 仍返回成功：settings.json / providers.json / 迁移清单这些带凭据的文件被告知已落盘，实际字节可能只停在 page cache 甚至未完整提交——调用方据此继续写下一步状态。当前代价：一次 close 的系统调用；优化后代价相同，只是失败可见。
fix: 在 18 行后、rename 之前插入 `try handle.close()`（defer 里的 `try?` 对已关闭句柄自然变成 no-op）。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): `try handle.close()` before rename in PrivateFileWriter.write; the defer's try? on an already-closed handle is a measured no-op.

summary: The `request_headers` migration runs an `ALTER TABLE` on every connection open, and its error is discarded; the payloads CREATE TABLE does not carry the column, so the ALTER always runs and always fails on an existing database.
evidence: Lines 522-529 create `payloads` with only `capture_id, request_json, rewritten_json, response_json, raw_sse`, and line 531 issues `sqlite3_exec(db, "ALTER TABLE payloads ADD COLUMN request_headers TEXT DEFAULT ''", nil, nil, nil)` with no callback and no return-code check. On any database where the column already exists (every database this build creates, since the CREATE never includes it and the ALTER supplies it on first open) the statement is a guaranteed "duplicate column name" failure executed once per process; note that the sibling migration on line 536 (`ALTER TABLE captures ADD COLUMN cache_write_tokens INTEGER`) has the same shape but at least has the column in its CREATE path only on the legacy side. Conversely, if the ALTER ever fails for a reason that matters (a read-only or locked database), `requestHeaders` silently reads as "" through `COALESCE(p.request_headers, '')` (398/407) and the inspector's 请求头 section disappears with no signal.
failure: Routine case: one failed prepare per `connection()` open, invisible. Real case: on a DB that predates the column and cannot be altered, the capture inspector loses the request headers for every row and nothing reports it (the `[truncated]` marker bug fixed by adding an explicit `requestTruncated` flag is the same class).
fix: Add `request_headers TEXT DEFAULT ''` to the `payloads` CREATE TABLE and keep the ALTER only as a best-effort legacy step, or gate the ALTER on `PRAGMA table_info(payloads)` so the common case issues no statement and the failure case can be logged.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): payloads CREATE TABLE carries request_headers; both legacy ALTERs gated on sqlite3_table_column_metadata (hasColumn) and their return codes logged.

summary: delete(_:) 没有任何调用者（UI 只有 clearAll），连同它引用的 media 清理路径都不可达
evidence: 446-458 定义 `func delete(_ id: Int64)`；`grep -rn "ProxyCaptureStore.shared" Sources Tests Tools` 只命中 begin/detail/clearAll/loadListIfNeeded/previews/catalog/streams，TrafficView 里唯一的删除操作是 433-444 的 `clearAll()`（`grep -rn "store.delete|shared.delete" .` 无命中，git log -S 也从未存在过调用点）。该函数还在主线程同步 `try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: CaptureMedia.mediaDir(captureID: id))`，而 `mediaDir` 会先 createDirectory（CaptureMedia.swift:17-22），即先建目录再删。
failure: 无运行时后果，但 460-482 的 clearAll 注释（"media directories ... are only removed by `delete(_:)`"）与实际不符，读者会以为存在单条删除路径；任何只测单条删除的行为验证都跑不到这段代码。

verdict_note: Same method, same removal — delete(_:) deleted with 132; the clearAll comment no longer claims media removal lives in delete.

summary: token 列以 Int64 写入却以 sqlite3_column_int（32 位）读回，超过 2^31 的值会被静默截断/变负
evidence: 写入侧 841: `case .int(let n): sqlite3_bind_int64(stmt, Int32(i + 1), n)`，值来自 `Int64($0)`（310-313），而上游 token 数经 `TokenTotals.intValue` 的 NSNumber.intValue（StreamAssembler.swift:211-215）本身就是 64 位；读取侧 883-886: `if sqlite3_column_type(stmt, i) == SQLITE_NULL { return nil }; return Int(sqlite3_column_int(stmt, i))`。rowToSummary 的 prompt/completion/cache 四列全走它。
failure: 上游/中转网关上报一个越界的 token 数（例如把累计量或错误字段放进 usage.prompt_tokens，> 2_147_483_647）：写库正常，读回时 SQLite 按低 32 位截断，面板与「输入/输出」统计显示负数或荒谬的小值；UI 与库内不一致，且没有任何日志。conf 标 medium 是因为实际 API 上报超过 21 亿 token 的请求罕见，但代码路径确实存在。
fix: `return Int(sqlite3_column_int64(stmt, i))`（httpStatus 那种小整数可保持不变）。
verdict_note: Already fixed in 44138c4: optInt is now Int(sqlite3_column_int64(stmt, i)) with an explicit comment; the 32-bit truncation is gone.

summary: 所有抓包状态写入都丢弃 sqlite3_step 的返回码，写入失败静默、库与 UI 分叉
evidence: 832-846: `guard sqlite3_prepare_v2(...) == SQLITE_OK else { return }` 之后 845 直接 `sqlite3_step(stmt)`，返回值与 sqlite3_errmsg 都不看；同一个文件 691-692 的注释已经承认这类丢弃的代价（"execRaw discards the return code, so leaving the pragma inside its own defer scope made every one of these a silent no-op"），但只修了 VACUUM 那一处。exec 承载的是 finish 的状态/用量 UPDATE、DELETE、recoverOrphans 等全部状态机写入。
failure: 磁盘满、SQLite 文件被替换为只读、或 2 秒 busy_timeout 用尽（500 行有 2000ms 超时）时，一次 `UPDATE captures SET state=...` 失败：内存里的 catalog.records 已经是 done，库里仍是 pending/streaming，用户看到行永远「实时」且中断按钮无效；下次启动 recoverOrphans 才把它改成 aborted/interrupted，用量与错误信息丢失。
fix: `let rc = sqlite3_step(stmt); if rc != SQLITE_DONE { /* os_log + 可选：把该 id 标为持久化失败 */ }`，至少把返回值用于诊断；不必在此改状态机。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): finish/clearAll/update now read exec()'s Bool and log via os.Logger(category: Capture).

summary: cancel/attach 竞态是文件里唯一被文档强调的不变量，但没有任何回归
evidence: 44-61 行注释写明「the cancelled check happens *inside* the lock — read outside it, an attach that lost the race by nanoseconds would store a hook on a handle whose cancel() already copied the two hooks and unlocked, leaving the abort client alive」，随后才是 `private func runOrStore(_ immediate: @escaping () -> Void, store: () -> Void)` 的锁内判断。grep 全仓 Tests/ 对 `ProxyInflight`、`CaptureTap`、`attachAbort`、`attachUpstreamAbort` 命中 0 条（Tools/render-mainwindow-preview.py:469-471 只有 `final class ProxyInflight { static let shared = ...; func cancel(captureID: Int64) {} }` 空壳替身）。
failure: 把 cancelled 判断挪到锁外（或把 immediate() 收进锁内）不会有任何测试失败，而真实时序下表现为：中断按钮把 capture 标成已中断、`isInterrupted` 变 true，但客户端连接从未被断开（abort 被存进了已经 cancel 过的 handle），Claude Code/Codex 那侧继续等一个永远不会结束的流。
fix: 加一个不启应用的 Swift 切片回归，直接用 Handle 跑两种顺序并断言：cancel→attachAbort 时 abort 恰被立刻调用一次；attachAbort→cancel 时 abort 恰被调用一次且 `cancel()` 第二次返回 false；混入 detach 后 attach 的 hook 不再被执行。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster C): new Tests/proxy-inflight-regressions.py (216 checks) — cancel/attach order, idempotence, double-cancel, late attach, detach, re-opened id, and a 200-iteration threaded race asserting abort runs exactly once. Test-gap only; ProxyInflight.swift unchanged.

summary: SQL 写入失败被静默吞掉，但 didChange 通知照发，触发一次必然空转的全量用量刷新
evidence: 256 行 `guard sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, sql, -1, &stmt, nil) == SQLITE_OK else { return }`，sqlite3_step 的返回值也未检查；返回后 record() 继续执行 89-91 行 `DispatchQueue.main.async { NotificationCenter.default.post(name: Self.didChange, object: nil) }` → ProviderStore.swift:1255-1260 的观察者调 `refreshUsage(rescan: false)`。

summary: 同一 SMC 键在一轮判断里被读两次（各 2 次内核 struct 调用）
evidence: 248-254 行：`if let md = getValue(fanModeKey(id)), let parsed = FanMode(rawValue: Int(md)) { return parsed.isAutomatic ? .automatic : parsed }` 之后 arm64 分支又 `let modeValue = Int(getValue(fanModeKey(id)) ?? 0)` —— 完全相同的一次 getValue；getValue→read 每次是 2 次 IOConnectCallStructMethod（keyInfo + readBytes，见 read:269-302）。触发条件是第一读成功但 `FanMode(rawValue:)` 失败（模式值不是 0/1/3，例如 SMC 报 2）。
failure: 每台有非标准模式值的风扇、每 2 s 轮询（FanMonitor.syncPolling 的 2.0 s 定时器）就多 2 次跨内核调用，且这些调用与 ProcessSampler 的温度扫描共用 ioLock（call:308-310）互斥——纯重复工作换来的锁争用。

verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): fanMode reads the mode key once, into a local, instead of twice on the parse-failure path (worst case per 2 s per fan: two extra IOConnectCallStructMethod calls).

summary: #if arch(arm64) 恒为真：Intel 的 FS! 分支与 fanModeKey 的 #else 从未被编译
evidence: SMCController.swift:210-224（fanModeKey 的 `#else return "F\(id)Md"`）与 252-263（fanMode 的 `#else` 读 `FS! ` 并按 (fansMode, id) 分派）；`grep -rn '#if arch' Sources/ClaudeBar` 只有这两处。构建侧：Sources/build.sh:24 `MACOS_TARGET="arm64-apple-macos${MACOS_MIN}"`，274/385 行两次 swiftc 都传 `-target "$MACOS_TARGET"`，仓库没有第二个构建入口（Makefile→build.sh），也不存在 x86_64 目标。连带 152 行 getValue 的全零豁免表里的 `"FS! verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): The unreachable `#else return "F\(id)Md"` branch is deleted (build.sh builds arm64 only), and the "FS! " entry from the all-zero-exempt table went with its only reader.

summary: ui8 的 16 位小端拼装在 Swift 里被 UInt8 位移吞掉，与 fanctl.c 的同款实现漂移
evidence: 316-317 行 `if dataSize == 1 { return Double(bytes[0]) }` / `return Double(bytes[0] | (bytes[1] << 8)) // " 8iu"-style LE 16-bit`，两侧都是 UInt8。本机 Swift 实测：`UInt8(0x35) << 8 == 0`、`func g(_ b: UInt8,_ n: UInt8) -> UInt8 { b << n }; g(0x35, 8) == 0`，即高字节部分恒为 0，结果只剩 bytes[0]。C 版同一惯用法 Sources/fanctl/fanctl.c:98-99 `if (type == fourcc(" 8iu") || type == fourcc("ui8 ")) { return size == 1 ? bytes[0] : (double)(bytes[0] | (bytes[1] << 8)); }` 在 int 提升下是正确的——同一条公式两份实现已经漂移。
failure: 任何 ` 8iu`/` 8ui` 类型、数值 ≥256 的 16 位小端键，Swift 侧只拿到低字节，而 helper 拿到完整值，两边对同一物理键给出不同数字；当前风扇数 <256 掩蔽了后果，但 FNum 之外任何走 getValue 的 ` 8iu` 键都会低估。
fix: 改成 `return Double(UInt16(bytes[0]) | (UInt16(bytes[1]) << 8))`（与 ui16 分支互为字节序），并在 fan-rotor 或新 suite 里加一条对 ` 8iu` 的切片回归。
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): The ui8 16-bit fallback is now `Double(UInt16(bytes[0]) | (UInt16(bytes[1]) << 8))`, matching fanctl.c's int-promotion expression; a mirror mutant reverting it is caught by the 309 assertion.

summary: fds 名称固定取 bytes[4...15]，但文件内没有任何地方跳过 4 字节头部，无法自证正确

summary: The listen-only fallback asks for the same keyDown mask at the same tap point whose defaultTap just failed, and the SDK says that mask is emptied (→ NULL) for the same missing permission — the branch is likely unreachable.
evidence: ScreenshotHotKey.swift:146-170: when `CGEvent.tapCreate(... options: .defaultTap, eventsOfInterest: mask ...)` returns nil the code calls `installPassiveTap(mask)` (168) with the same `mask` (keyDown|keyUp|flagsChanged, line 147) and the same `.cgSessionEventTap`, only switching to `.listenOnly` (183-199). CoreGraphics' header states the rule without distinguishing tap options: 'Taps placed at ... kCGSessionEventTap ... may only receive key up and down events if access for assistive devices is enabled ... If the tap is not permitted to monitor these events when the tap is created, then the appropriate bits in the mask are cleared. If that results in an empty mask, then NULL is returned.' (MacOSX.sdk/.../CoreGraphics.framework/Headers/CGEvent.h:272-279). The file header (lines 11-12) and the comment at 166-167 claim the fallback exists precisely for the untrusted case.
failure: On a machine where Accessibility/Input Monitoring is not granted (the case this branch was written for) the fallback also returns nil, so the function does nothing and the comment/doc promise is false; the only trigger left is `RegisterEventHotKey`. Uncertain because modern macOS routes this through the Input Monitoring TCC category rather than the legacy assistive-devices flag, and some trust states (granted-but-changed identity, ticked-in-settings) may behave differently — I could not verify on-device under the read-only constraint.
fix: Either delete the fallback path and its comment (documenting the Carbon path as the only untrusted fallback), or log/`lastError` when both creations return nil so the dead branch is visible instead of implied to work.

summary: The pasteboard write encodes the full-resolution image to TIFF twice; the second encode is discarded work on the main thread.
evidence: Lines 401-409: `if let tiff = image.tiffRepresentation, let rep = NSBitmapImageRep(data: tiff), let png = rep.representation(using: .png, properties: [:]) { item.setData(png, forType: .png) }` immediately followed by `if let tiff = image.tiffRepresentation { item.setData(tiff, forType: .tiff) }` — the first TIFF is consumed into a local `let` (line 402) and the second call re-derives the same NSData. `writePasteboard` runs on the main thread from `copyAndClose` (line 135) and `copyPin` (line 1201).
failure: Copying a 3024x1964 crop (~8 MB of pixels, ~24 MB uncompressed TIFF) pays two full TIFF encodes plus one TIFF decode plus one PNG encode before ⌘C returns; the extra encode is a straight main-thread stall (tens of ms at full-screen selections) with zero behavioural benefit and a second peak allocation of the encoded buffer.
fix: Bind once: `if let tiff = image.tiffRepresentation { if let rep = NSBitmapImageRep(data: tiff), let png = rep.representation(using: .png, properties: [:]) { item.setData(png, forType: .png) }; item.setData(tiff, forType: .tiff) }` — halves the encode work and one large allocation.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): writePasteboard encodes the TIFF once and reuses it for both the PNG and TIFF representations — the second full-resolution encode is gone.

summary: SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows is re-fetched once per screen inside the capture loop, serialising one extra full window/display enumeration plus XPC round trip before the first frame appears.
evidence: `run()` loops `for screen in screens { shots.append((screen, try await Self.captureDisplay(screen))) }` (lines 64-72), and every `captureDisplay` call starts with `let content = try await SCShareableContent.excludingDesktopWindows(false, onScreenWindowsOnly: true)` (line 372). Only `content.displays` is used (line 373); the window list is never touched here (window snapping uses the synchronous `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` instead, line 440).
failure: On a 2- or 3-display Mac the hotkey pays 2-3 shareable-content enumerations (each a replayd round trip that walks every on-screen window) serially before the first freeze panel is shown; every entry after the first returns the identical `displays` array. Latency of the ⌘⇧A → freeze path grows with display count for zero information gain.
fix: Fetch `SCShareableContent` once in `run()` (or on first use) and pass `content.displays` into `captureDisplay(_:display:)`; keep the per-screen `SCContentFilter`/`SCStreamConfiguration` construction where it is.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): run() fetches SCShareableContent once (failure beeps and clears capturing identically) and passes it into captureDisplay, so a multi-display capture no longer re-enumerates replayd per screen.

summary: The pin's hover chrome bar is positioned 8pt above the top edge of its own window, so the top of the bar (and of every button in it) is clipped by the window frame.
evidence: Lines 1175-1181: `let photo = frame.size  // includes padding` then `chromeBar.frame = NSRect(x: photo.width - chromeBar.frame.width - 2, y: photo.height - chromeBar.frame.height + 8, ...)`. With `chromeBar` height 24 (`setFrameSize(NSSize(width: x + 4, height: 24))`, line 1246) the bar spans window y = H-16 … H+8; its NSButtons are 20pt tall at bar-local y=2 (line 1242), i.e. window y = H-14 … H+6. The host view is the window's `contentView` (line 1170) and the window is `NSSize(width: size.width + padding, height: size.height + padding)` (line 1133), so H is the window height and a window clips its content at its own frame.
failure: Every pinned screenshot shows the close/copy/zoom chrome with its top ~6-8pt cut off — the SF Symbols in those four buttons are shaved at the top edge. The accompanying comment ('extra window padding hides it until the cursor enters', lines 1120-1121) also does not match the implementation: there is no mouseEntered/tracking-area or hover-hide path anywhere in ScreenshotPinPanel (grep for mouseEntered in the file returns only the SnipCanvas tracking area at line 621).
fix: Position the bar inside the frame, aligned to the photo's top edge: `y: photo.height - chromeBar.frame.height - padding / 2 - 1` (and either implement the documented hover-hide with `NSView.addTrackingArea` on the host, or delete the stale comment).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): The chrome bar is positioned from the photo height and padding (padding/2-1), so its four buttons land inside the window (measured: window 334×234, bar 236,192,96,24, all buttons inside); the stale hover-hide comment is gone. Tests/screenshot-overlay-regressions.py pins it.

summary: SnipToolbar's `intrinsicContentSize` override is never read, and the `sizeToFit()` called on every toolbar reposition recomputes a size that cannot have changed — both are no-ops inside the drag path.
evidence: Line 1081: `override var intrinsicContentSize: NSSize { frame.size }`. Nothing constrains the toolbar: it is a plain subview of SnipCanvas (`addSubview(toolbar)`, line 620) positioned by frame math, and the canvas has no Auto Layout constraints on it, so the intrinsic-content machinery is never queried. Line 1083-1087: `func sizeToFit() { var w: CGFloat = 8; for v in subviews { w = max(w, v.frame.maxX) }; setFrameSize(NSSize(width: w + 8, height: 36)) }` is called from `positionToolbar()` line 945, which runs on every `mouseDragged` resize frame (line 842) and every lock/full-screen selection (lines 744, 875, 899). The buttons/divider/undo are created once in `init` and never removed or resized inside `positionToolbar`, and `sizeToFit`'s own header sets the same 36pt height (line 1066), so the recomputed width always equals the current width.
failure: No functional failure — a wasted O(subviews) walk plus a redundant `setFrameSize` per drag event (up to 120/s on ProMotion while resizing a selection), and an override that misleads the next reader into thinking the toolbar participates in Auto Layout sizing.
fix: Delete the `intrinsicContentSize` override and drop the `toolbar.sizeToFit()` call from `positionToolbar()` (or convert it to a `static let toolbarSize` computed once in `init`), keeping the explicit `setFrameSize` at line 1066 as the single source of the toolbar's size.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): SnipToolbar's intrinsicContentSize override and custom sizeToFit are deleted; positionToolbar uses the frame fixed at init.

summary: The overlay's fallback hot keys reuse ScreenshotHotKey's Carbon signature 'CBSH' with id 1 for Esc, so the app's own ⌘⇧A registration (also id 1, same signature) is dispatched as Esc while a capture is up.
evidence: ScreenshotOverlay.swift:259-266 registers `(kVK_Escape, 0, 1), (kVK_Space, 0, 2), (kVK_Return, 0, 3), (kVK_ANSI_KeypadEnter, 0, 4), (8, cmdKey, 5), (1, cmdKey, 6)` with `EventHotKeyID(signature: 0x43425348, id: idx)` (269), and 277-278 `switch idx { case 1: cancel() ... }`. ScreenshotHotKey.swift:93 registers `EventHotKeyID(signature: Self.signature, id: 1)` with `signature: OSType = 0x43425348` (235), and its handler at 208-223 filters only on the signature — `if id.signature == ScreenshotHotKey.signature { DispatchQueue.main.async { ScreenshotOverlayController.shared.begin() } }` — never on `id.id`. Both handlers are installed on `GetApplicationEventTarget()` for `kEventHotKeyPressed`, so both receive every 'CBSH' press.
failure: In the no-Accessibility path (the only one that installs fallback keys), pressing ⌘⇧A while the freeze overlay is up delivers a 'CBSH'/id-1 event to the overlay's fallback handler → `case 1: cancel()` dismisses the capture the user was trying to restart, while ScreenshotHotKey's handler simultaneously calls `begin()`, which the `capturing` guard drops — the opposite of the 'double delivery is harmless' contract in the file header. Symmetrically, every Space/Return/⌘C/⌘S the fallback registers also calls `begin()` through the app handler (harmless only because of that same guard).
fix: Give the fallback keys their own signature (e.g. `0x43425302`) and have ScreenshotHotKey's handler check `id.id == 1` before dispatching.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): The fallback hot key uses its own signature (CBOV, 0x43424F56) instead of sharing 0x43425348 with the screenshot hot key, and ScreenshotHotKey's handler verifies id.id == triggerID; a signature mismatch no longer cancels a live capture.

summary: mouseMoved rebuilds and reassigns a full-screen even-odd CAShapeLayer path on every move event even when the hovered window did not change.
evidence: ScreenshotOverlay.swift:796-802: `cursor = convert(...); if !locked, !dragging { hoverWindow = WindowSnapper.frontmostWindow(contains: cursor, in: windowRects); refreshMask() }` — no comparison against the previous value. `refreshMask` (902-926) builds `let path = CGMutablePath(); path.addRect(bounds); if let r = highlight ... path.addRect(r)` and assigns `dimLayer.path = path` and `strokeLayer.path`, where `bounds` is the full `NSScreen.frame` at 1:1 (line 591) and dimLayer is a sublayer of the screen-sized root layer. `windowRects` is a flat array, so `frontmostWindow` also rescans it per event.
failure: Moving the pointer across the freeze (up to the display's event rate, 120 Hz on ProMotion, plus an extra event for each sub-pixel move) re-tessellates and re-uploads a display-sized shape layer for an unchanged highlight; on a 6K display the dim overlay is ~6000×3400 and this is the only work done per event in that state.
fix: Compute the candidate first and bail when it is unchanged: `let next = WindowSnapper.frontmostWindow(...); if next != hoverWindow { hoverWindow = next; refreshMask() }`.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): mouseMoved computes the candidate window first and only assigns hoverWindow + refreshMask when it differs — no more full-screen even-odd path rebuild per mouse move.

summary: Committed annotation layers are rasterized at the main screen's backing scale instead of the canvas's, so marks drawn on a display with a different scale are resampled relative to the live draft.
evidence: ScreenshotOverlay.swift:703-716: `private static func markShape(_ mark: SnipMark, in sel: CGRect) -> CAShapeLayer { ... l.contentsScale = NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor ?? 2; ... }` — `markShape` is a static helper that never receives the canvas, and `refreshMask` gives no `contentsScale` to `marksLayer` either (906-907 only sets anchorPoint/frame). The canvas knows its own display (`screen` stored at 556, `layer?.contentsScale = screen.backingScaleFactor` at 594).
failure: Capture on a 1x external display while the built-in Retina is `NSScreen.main` (or the reverse) → a committed rect/arrow/pen stroke is rasterized at 2x and drawn into a 1x layer (or vice versa), so it renders softer/thicker than the draft the user was just dragging, and differs from the same mark burned into the exported PNG by `croppedImage()` (786-789), which strokes at native crop resolution.
fix: Pass the scale in: `Self.markShape(draft, in: sel, scale: screen.backingScaleFactor)` (or read `window?.backingScaleFactor`), and apply the same value to `marksLayer` once in `refreshMask`.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster A worker, committed eced4a9): markShape takes the capturing screen's backingScaleFactor (draft and commit paths) and refreshMask sets the same contentsScale on marksLayer; the NSScreen.main dependency is gone.

summary: The only regression on this function pins the inner escape fragment, not the enclosing quotes, so a mutation that drops the quotes still passes while the security property is gone.
evidence: Tests/session-migration-regressions.py:455 asserts `precondition(ShellQuote.single("a'$(touch NEVER)").contains("'\\''"))`. A hypothetical `single` that returns `value.replacingOccurrences(of: "'", with: "'\\''")` (no outer quotes) still contains `'\''` and passes, yet every path handed to the installers' `sh -c` scripts becomes word-split and `$`/backtick live again. The same test does build the real `MigrationCommand.shell` (line 456) and the installers are compiled for real in Tests/build-isolation-regressions.py:25, but neither round-trips a quote-bearing value through a shell.
failure: A refactor that removes or narrows the enclosing quoting passes the suite, and the two privileged installers (BatteryHelperInstaller.swift:89-100, FanHelperInstaller.swift:91-103) would then execute a path such as `/Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/$(...)` with administrator privileges.

verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster E): session-migration pins ShellQuote.single for a hostile value plus a real /bin/sh round trip; mutation (dropping quotes) fails the suite.

summary: Each of the ~288 scan samples computes the full sun+moon snapshot to read only the sun's altitude, roughly doubling the transcendental work of the one uncached path in this file.
evidence: Line 51: `snapshot(date: instant, ...).sun.altitude + 0.833`; `snapshot` (84-105) computes lunarMean/lunarAnomaly/lunarDistance, the lunar longitude and latitude, a second `position(...)` (and thereby a second `horizon()`), plus the phase, all discarded by the caller. Per sample that is about 6 extra transcendental calls over a sun-only evaluation; the 300 s grid plus a bisection per crossing means roughly 300 full snapshots per call. Amortization is real: the key includes the day start, so the path runs once per (day, zone, latitude, longitude) — first render of a day, a location/zone change, or the day boundary while the canvas is up — and `GreetingCard.trackColors` rebuilds 25 scenes on its own key change (GreetingCard.swift:1063-1078) without touching solarEvents. So the current cost is a one-off main-actor spike on those events, not per-frame work; it is the largest single computation in this otherwise cached file.
failure: No user-visible failure today — the observable effect is a ~2x longer main-actor stall on the first sun-path render after a coordinate or zone change and at local midnight, on the same thread that rebuilds the greeting card body.
fix: Factor a sun-only helper (`sunAltitude(date:latitude:longitude:)` using lines 85-88 and one `horizon()` call) and use it inside the `altitude` closure; `snapshot` keeps its current shape for the renderer.
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 (cluster D): the solar-events scan now calls a sun-only `sunAltitude(date:latitude:longitude:)` (sun terms + one `horizon()` call) instead of building the full sun+moon `Snapshot` per sample; `snapshot` unchanged. Differential vs HEAD over 5,000 instants: max altitude delta 0.0; 60 day/zone solarEvents combos identical.
