verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07: ConnectMarkState.off returns Theme.Ink.idle — the same grey the idle pill uses — instead of the fixed statusIdle fill; the two dark-mode-adaptive quiet greys no longer disagree on the same card.

summary: WiFiBars.label is declared optional but is total (every branch returns), so all three call-site fallbacks are unreachable code.
evidence: Lines 313-320: `static func label(for rssi: Int) -> String? { switch rssi { case ..<(-75): return "弱" ... default: return "很强" } }` — no path returns nil. Callers carry fallbacks that can never fire: line 100 `WiFiBars.label(for: rssi).map { $0 + " · " } ?? ""`, line 159 `"\(host.wifiRSSI) dBm \(WiFiBars.label(for: host.wifiRSSI) ?? "")"`, and HardwareDetailPanel.swift:202 `Text(WiFiBars.label(for: rssi) ?? "未知")`.
failure: Nothing breaks today; the defect is that the signature promises a nil case no reading can produce, so a future reader (or a fourth call site) writes defensive branches for a state that does not exist, and the string that path would print ("未知"/"") has never been seen or reviewed.
fix: Return `String` (drop the `?`) and delete the three fallbacks; if an unreadable/absent RSSI really must print a word, model it at the `rssi: Int?` layer as ConnectionSignalScale already does.

summary: The 12-cell signal row is built from 12 separate RoundedRectangle views (12 shape layers + 12 layout nodes) where every mark sharing the same slot is a single Canvas — the exact pattern the repo's own drawing rule forbids.
evidence: Lines 289-296: `HStack(spacing: 2) { ForEach(0..<Self.count, id: \.self) { index in RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 2, style: .continuous).fill(...).frame(maxWidth: .infinity).frame(height: 14) } }` with `count = 12` (line 281). The sibling marks in the same 176×130 slot draw the equivalent cell lane in one Canvas: HardwareIllustration.swift:62-75 (`Canvas { ... Self.drawReading(kind:level:cells:wells:...) }`) for CPU/GPU/内存/硬盘, and UiverseSurfaces.swift:10-18 states the rule ('**Ornaments are one `Canvas` each.** The depth lens is three stroked circles; as three `Circle` views that is three layers *per card*, on every inventory tile in the app').
failure: Every re-render of the connection tile (host publishes at 1 s while a session is live, 2 s otherwise) re-evaluates 12 shape views, each of which is a separate display-list layer for the render server, instead of one Canvas draw — roughly 12 layers/12 layout nodes per tick where the sibling tiles use 1, on the dashboard strip the frame audit is about.

summary: LinkCard.dense is never true — its only caller passes false — so the card's compact path (tighter mark slot, dense corner radius and ring inset in TileSurface) is unreachable.

summary: At ratio 0 the bar still paints a `height`-wide coloured pill, so 'no reading' and '1 % used' draw the same mark — the opposite of the convention the sibling cell row follows.
evidence: Line 21: `.frame(width: max(height, geo.size.width * min(max(ratio, 0), 1.0)))` — with ratio 0 the fill is `max(height, 0)` = `height` wide (4 pt at the default, 5–6 pt at the VpnTopChrome/Dashboard call sites). Every caller signals 'no reading' by *dimming* the whole bar (`.opacity(... ? 1 : 0.25)`: CursorSessionCardView.swift:54, SessionCardView.swift:63, DashboardView.swift:322, SessionsView.swift:386/583/989) — i.e. the bar is still drawn filled. The sibling `SignalCellRow` explicitly guards this case (ConnectionCard.swift:284-288: 'the `index / (count - 1)` formula would still light cell 0 at 0.0 ... The floor is what stops an offline card from claiming a bar's worth of signal'), and ConnectionSignalScale.append at HardwareDetailPanel.swift:443 has the matching `geometry.size.width > 0 && position != nil` gate.
failure: A session whose context ratio is 0 (unknown limit, no tokens — the exact state the call-site opacity is there to announce) renders as a full-height coloured dot, indistinguishable from a 1–3 % reading at 25 % opacity; a viewer cannot tell '0 %' from 'a sliver of context used'.
fix: Floor the fill to zero when the ratio is zero: `let clamped = min(max(ratio, 0), 1); .frame(width: clamped <= 0 ? 0 : max(height, geo.size.width * clamped))` (or drop the `max(height, ...)` floor entirely and let callers' 25 % dimmed track carry the empty state).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07: ContextBar computes the clamped ratio once and emits width 0 for an empty bar; the height-wide pill appears only for genuinely non-zero fills.

summary: `Equatable` is declared but never used for a comparison, which silently removes the mismatch this type's own doc points at (email/membership fields were deleted in a cleanup, and one doc reference survived).
evidence: CursorDB.swift:58 `struct CursorCredentials: Equatable {`, fields `accessToken`/`subject` (lines 60-63). Grep for `CursorCredentials` across Sources/ and Tests/: only the declaration, `readCredentials`, and its construction — no `==`. The removed fields' doc contract is still referenced: line 50-53 explains "A missing key must degrade to 'unknown'", and the struct's history (commit 10cfc84 removed `email`/`membershipType`/`subscriptionStatus` and the `canQueryUsage` helper they fed) left the surrounding comment describing fields the type no longer has.
failure: No runtime consequence. The risk is the usual Equatable-on-a-secret-carrying-type one: if a later change adds a field (e.g. a token-expiry or a second key) and something compares two readings to dedupe probes, the synthesized `==` will compare the raw JWT strings rather than any semantic identity, and nothing in the type signals that was unintended.
fix: Drop `: Equatable` until a comparison exists, or give it an explicit `==` on a deliberate identity (e.g. `subject` only) and fix the now-stale doc block at lines 50-53 to name only the fields the type actually carries.

summary: The GetFilteredUsageEvents page family is reachable only from the regression probe; the app's single ledger path is the aggregate parser, and the paging contract it documents lost its constant in an earlier cleanup.
evidence: Grep for `parseEvents|reportedEventCount|needsMorePages` across the repo: the only hits outside this file are Tests/fixtures/cursor-ledger-probe.swift:114-140. `CursorLedgerReader.read` (CursorLedgerStore.swift:202-207) loops `windowChunks` and calls only `fetchAggregated` → `parseAggregated`. `needsMorePages`'s `guard page != nil` arm is unreachable in its documented use (`guard page != nil, let reportedTotal else { return false }` — combined with `reportedTotal`, `page` is always non-nil at every call site), and `maxPageSize` — the constant the doc comment says callers "must use" — was deleted in 776f3b7, so the comment at lines 242-243 now describes a contract the file no longer carries. The probe also labels its own assumption wrong: `CursorLedger.needsMorePages(page: foldedByModel, reportedTotal: 90, rowsSeen: 3)` passes per-*model* rows into a parameter whose contract (line 235 "rowsSeen") is per-*event* rows.
failure: Two parsers that "disagree in ways that matter" (their own comment, lines 196-198) are kept with only one covered by an end-to-end path; the next change to the aggregate shape or the paging cap has no production caller to validate it, and the surviving test asserts a semantics (`rowsSeen = per-model count`) that contradicts the function's own contract.
fix: Move `parseEvents`/`reportedEventCount`/`needsMorePages` (and their tests) into the file's "documented, not wired" story by deleting them, or add the comment's missing `maxPageSize` back and fix the probe's `rowsSeen` to count events (`usageEventsDisplay` count) rather than folded models. Deleting is the smaller diff if the paged endpoint is not coming back.

summary: `truncated` is written in four places (init rehydrate, permission denial, live read, cache save) and read by exactly one other function — the cache's own `save(_:plan:)` — so its documented consumer (“a caller that reasoned about coverage without it would treat 'one cycle' as 'the whole period'”) does not exist; only the disk round-trip keeps it alive while flagged stale windows are instead detected via `isStale`.
evidence: CursorLedgerStore.swift:39 `private(set) var truncated = false`; assignments at :73, :121, :161; its only reader is `cache.save(read, plan: plan)` at :164 via `plan.truncated` (CursorLedgerStore.swift:309). `grep -rn "\.truncated" Sources` outside this file: none. The card never reads it (CursorTokenUsageCard.swift:80 uses `isStale`), and `CursorLedgerStore.snapshot(for:)` was already deleted in 10cfc84 for the same reason.
failure: No runtime failure by itself — the cost is that a reviewer or the next feature (the file's own doc suggests reasoning about coverage) believes a caller is honouring the flag; the cache path is exercised but the semantic value is never surfaced, and `isStale` is the de facto replacement.
fix: Either drop the field (and the cache column, bumping the `Stored` decode if needed) or actually surface it where the store's comment points — the card's “仅覆盖上述日期” line at CursorTokenUsageCard.swift:80-83 — under one flag so the two coverage signals cannot disagree.

summary: The age label is computed from `Date()` inside an `Equatable` model, so crossing every minute boundary makes the session array "change" and forces a full widget-snapshot rewrite while idle.
evidence: CursorSessionMonitor.swift:107-114: `let now = Date().timeIntervalSince1970 * 1000; … if secs < 3600 { return "\(Int(secs / 60))m" }`. `CursorSessionInfo: Equatable` therefore differs between two polls one minute apart even when nothing else changed. ProviderStore.swift:549-555 publishes on that inequality and calls `self.writeWidgetSnapshot()`, whose writer (WidgetSnapshotWriter.swift:32-36) compares normalized bytes and, when they differ, does four atomic writes plus a timeline reload. The minute label is genuinely wanted (`WidgetSnapshot.swift:70` "precomputed by the host app"), so this is a contract cost, not a bug.
failure: An idle Cursor session on screen → once a minute forever: a `@Published` change (re-running every observer of `cursorSessions`, including `IslandLiveModel` at IslandLiveModel.swift:167 and `ScopedStoreObservation`), a full snapshot encode, up to four file writes (one into the widget's container) and a `WidgetCenter` reload — for a label change from "5m" to "6m".
fix: Carry the coarse label the widget needs as a *duration since a stored timestamp* and let the widget render it (or quantize `relativeUpdated` to a 5-minute bucket for sessions that are not busy), so the model's equality does not move every minute; failing that, drop `relativeUpdated` from the comparison used to decide publishing and pass the age only when another field changed.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: relativeUpdated is a computed property; the synthesized Equatable only compares stored fields, so minute boundaries do not make polls differ or republish.

summary: a second, uncached DateFormatter factory for the same pattern already provided, cached, by UsageStats.formatter
evidence: Lines 224-230 build a new `DateFormatter` (locale en_US_POSIX, timeZone UTC, dateFormat "yyyy-MM-dd") on every call; the single call site is line 187 (parsing the fallback source's `date` field). UsageStats.swift:56-70 is the module's formatter factory for the very same pattern -- cached by pattern + zone, zh_CN, TimeZone.current -- and this file already uses it for output at line 106 (`UsageStats.formatter("yyyy-MM-dd").string(from: providerDate)`), while the provider-input formatter is cached at lines 216-222 (rfc1123) instead. So one file holds three formatter strategies for two fields: two cached ones and one uncached duplicate that differs from the display one in locale and zone.
failure: Cost is small today (one allocation per fallback fetch, never on a render path), but the drift is real: a future caller that reaches for ExchangeRate.formatter for display would format a UTC day while `note` formats a local day, and a reviewer cannot tell from the call site which semantics apply. Also note the provider-stamped day is rendered through UsageStats.formatter's *local* zone at line 106, so a user west of UTC shows provider-Date one day early.
fix: Move the parse formatter next to rfcl123 (lines 216-222) as a second cached static `let isoDay` and use it at line 187; leave UsageStats.formatter as the only display formatter.

summary: the whole exchange-rate path has no regression coverage in Tests/
evidence: `grep -rn "ExchangeRate" Tests/` returns nothing, and Makefile's TEST_SUITES (Sources/../Makefile, the single registry CI calls) has no exchange suite; model-cost-regressions.py exercises ModelPricing.rate/cost/present only. Uncovered branches include `number()`'s NSNumber/String/NaN handling (lines 232-239), `parseProviderDate` against the free tier's exact "Thu, 24 Sep 2026 00:02:32 +0000" shape (lines 211-222), the manual-rate guard at both side-effect entrances (lines 114/127), and the TTL boundary in `refreshIfStale` (lines 115-118). The dialogs/format asymmetry noted above (UTC parse vs local display at lines 106/187) is exactly the class of bug only a fixture can catch.
failure: A source that changes its date format, or a rate parsed as a string with a comma decimal separator, falls through to `lastError`/two-currency display with no test able to notice; the tile then silently shows a stale or absent rate.
fix: Add a small slice suite (JSONCoerce-adjacent, no app) that feeds the two documented payload shapes to the parsing helpers and asserts the quote/date, the "" / invalid-rate fallback, and that a set manual rate blocks both fetch entrances; register it in Makefile TEST_SUITES.

summary: the 24 MB lifecycle lookback is re-read in full on every poll with no memo, and the first chunk is sized at the maximum instead of growing
evidence: Line 850-854 calls `recoverBeforeTail(handle:before: start)` whenever the tail window contains no lifecycle event; line 863 floors at `end - codexLifecycleLookback` (24 * 1024 * 1024, line 747) and line 865 reads the entire span in one `read(upToCount:)`. Nothing is memoized, so if the condition still holds on the next 2.5 s poll the same 24 MB is read again and walked backwards again. The condition is exactly "mid-turn and the newest lifecycle record is more than a window behind EOF", i.e. it persists for as long as a long tool call keeps appending. Confidence medium on frequency: I could not reproduce the trigger on this machine's corpus (truncating the two large rollouts mid-turn still left a lifecycle record inside [windowStart, EOF]); the path is already the one the perf suite times (Tests/measured-performance-regressions.py:155-160, 8 x 12 MiB replay, lookback_8x12MiB_ms), which is evidence it is the known expensive one.
failure: When it triggers during a long tool call, each poll reads up to 24 MB and decodes/walks records backwards over it, on the utility queue, repeating the identical work every 2.5 s until the record ends -- a several-megabyte-per-poll I/O burst for a reading that cannot change until Codex writes a new lifecycle record.
fix: Read backwards in growing chunks instead of one 24 MB span: start with e.g. 2 MB and only extend (2 -> 8 -> 24 MB) when neither the lifecycle event nor the tool name was found; the measured pair usually sits a few hundred KB behind the window (the test fixture pads only 600 KB). Cache the recovered pair by (path, size) so an unchanged file is not re-walked.

summary: fetchActive() has no production caller and pays for the sub-agent scan it then throws away
evidence: `grep -rn "ExternalSessionMonitor.fetchActive"` across Sources/Tests/Tools returns only Tests/codex-session-regressions.py:73 (production uses `scan()` at ProviderStore.swift:576); `fetchActive` is also referenced only in the doc comments at lines 285/290. Its body is `scan().main.sorted { ... }`, i.e. it builds the full `Scan` including every sub-agent row and the helper retention windows, then discards `subagents`. Classified as test-only, not entirely unreferenced.
failure: No runtime consequence today (one wasted array per test call); the risk is that the documented "flat, main-threads-only view" has drifted out of production use while the doc comment still advertises it as an entry point.
fix: Either delete it and point Tests/codex-session-regressions.py:73 at `scan().main`, or keep it and mark it as test-only in the doc comment; if kept, sort `scan.main` in place so the discarded helper rows are not built for nothing.

summary: ExternalSessionInfo.isAlive is true for every row the monitor can emit, so every isAlive filter downstream is vacuous
evidence: The legacy path only appends a row after `guard alive else { continue }` (line 398) and then passes the same value (line 406); the indexed path hardcodes `isAlive: true` (line 515). So no published ExternalSessionInfo can carry false, while consumers still test it: ProviderStore+Derived.swift:33 (`filter { $0.isAlive && !$0.isSubagent }`), :40 (activeExternalCount), :88 (externalSessionTree), IslandLiveModel.swift:339. Contrast CursorSessionMonitor.swift:255 where `isAlive: updatedAt > cutoff` is a real predicate, so the same field name means different things in the two monitors.
failure: The filters read as if they can drop rows but never do; the next change that surfaces an unretained row (or a future caller that assumes the field is meaningful, as it is for Cursor) will silently leak it into counters, the widget island list and the tree instead of being filtered.
fix: Drop the `isAlive` filters (and the field) since the scan already decides membership, or -- if the field must stay for cross-monitor symmetry -- document at its declaration that the Codex scan never emits false, then delete the vacuous predicates in ProviderStore+Derived.

summary: 开发版的 isInstalled() 缺 BuildChannel 闸门，会如实报告正式版安装的 root helper 存在（电池侧同函数是 fail-closed），使 dev 的第一道闸显示为已安装。
evidence: FanHelperInstaller.swift:138-144 只做 `isExecutableFile` + `posixPermissions & 0o4000` 检查，没有 `BuildChannel` 判断；对照 BatteryHelperInstaller.swift:15-19 第一行就是 `guard BuildChannel.allowsSystemIntegration else { return false }`。写入路径确实有闸（runPrivileged 27、install 65），但读路径没有；本机 /usr/local/bin/claudebar-fanctl 为 root:wheel 4755（stat 实测），所以 dev 构建的 `helperInstalled` 初值和 start() 里都会是 true（FanMonitor.swift:12/28/174）。测试也覆盖不到：build-isolation-regressions.py:72-73 只断言 setAutomatic/resetAll，interaction-performance-regressions.py:52 把 `isInstalled()` 整个替换成 `false`。
failure: dev 构建里点风扇 → submit 里 174 行的重查返回 true → 175 行不弹安装引导，命令进 runPrivileged 被 27 行拦下，用户看到的是限制文案而非「需要安装辅助工具」；若走安装引导，FanHelperInstaller.install() 会在 65 行静默返回，用户点「安装辅助工具」后什么都不发生、也没有任何反馈（不触发密码框，符合规则 5，但状态与电池侧不一致）。
fix: 在 isInstalled() 首行加 `guard BuildChannel.allowsSystemIntegration else { return false }`，与 BatteryHelperInstaller 对齐；顺带可在 start() 里缓存该结果，避免每次点击 2 次 stat。

summary: The AppleScript-string escaping for the privileged shell script is written twice by hand (fan and battery installers) while the escaping rule they share (`ShellQuote`) is only half of what the script needs, and no regression asserts the emitted AppleScript text.
evidence: `FanHelperInstaller.swift:105-106` `let literal = shell.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\", with: "\\\\").replacingOccurrences(of: "\"", with: "\\\"")` then `NSAppleScript(source: "do shell script \"\(literal)\" with administrator privileges")`; `BatteryHelperInstaller.swift:102-104` repeats the identical two passes and the identical wrapping. `ShellQuote.single` was extracted to stop exactly this sort of drift (commit f0373a4, "两处敏感转义只能有一份"), but the AppleScript layer above it was left duplicated. I probed the live runtime: `osascript -e 'do shell script "echo shell=$0 flags=$-"'` returns `sh flags=hBc`, i.e. sh with no history expansion (`!` arrives intact) and AppleScript consumes one backslash layer, so the current chain is not exploitable today — the defect is that the correctness of a privilege-prompt script rests on two hand-maintained copies. Coverage: `Tests/build-isolation-regressions.py` splices both installers (lines 25-26) but only asserts the dev guard (`precondition(BatteryHelperInstaller.installIfNeeded() == BuildChannel.restrictionMessage)` at line 71), never the script string.
failure: Any future edit to one installer's escaping (e.g. handling `$` or backtick inside the staged path, or moving off `do shell script`) leaves the other silently divergent, and the wrong copy runs under the user's administrator prompt with no test able to tell them apart.
fix: Move the `literal`/`do shell script` wrapping into one shared helper (next to `ShellQuote`, e.g. `ShellQuote.appleScriptLiteral(_:)`) and have both installers call it; add one assertion to the build-isolation suite that the produced script contains the escaped `\'` sequence and no raw control character, so a drift fails a test instead of a password prompt.

summary: 每 2 s 的风扇轮询把一个启动期就固定的读数集合整个重读一遍：名字/下限/上限每拍都走 SMC，而同一类里温度键早已有缓存先例。
evidence: FanMonitor.swift:60-74 每拍调用 `smc.loadFans()`；SMCController.swift:226-242 每个风扇读 `F{i}ID`（2 次 user-client 往返）、`F{i}Mn`、`F{i}Mx`、`F{i}Md`、`F{i}Ac`，加 `FNum` —— 双风扇机合计 22 次 80 字节结构调用，其中只有 Ac（以及用户动过开关后的 Md）会变；SMCController.swift:166-176 对同类问题的处理是缓存（`temperatureKeys`「Sweep all of them once, then read just the ones that answered」），loadFans 没有对应缓存。
failure: 不是崩溃而是持续成本：22 次/2 s ≈ 11 次/s 的白读，且都在 SMCController 的 ioLock 下（SMCController.swift:118-120），与 ProcessSampler 每秒的温度读取互相排队；Dashboard 上风扇卡与温度读数共用这一把锁，冗余读直接延长对方的等待。
fix: 在 SMCController 内按 fan id 缓存 name/min/max（缓存随 FNum 变化或连接重开失效），每拍只读 Md/Ac：22 → 10 次往返（约 -55 %）。
verdict_note: Code: `tookFans` is set on every confirmed `.take` write and cleared on a confirmed whole-fleet reset; `adoptSystemControlOnQuit` gates on it first and keeps the `fans` snapshot as the fallback. Test: `interaction-performance-regressions.py` now splices `setManual`/`submit`/`adoptSystemControlOnQuit` into the fan fixture and asserts a commanded session hands back on quit even while the polled snapshot still reads 自动, that an untouched session does not reset, and that a failed write does not create the duty. `make test TEST=interaction-performance` passes.

summary: 超时分支里的 group.wait(timeout:) 判断是空操作：两个分支抛出的错误字符串逐字相同，条件结果被丢弃。
evidence: 151-154: `if group.wait(timeout: .now() + 2) == .timedOut { throw FeishuCLIError.failed("飞书 CLI 超时，请稍后重试。") }` / `throw FeishuCLIError.failed("飞书 CLI 超时，请稍后重试。")` —— if 体与兜底抛的是同一句文案，删掉整个 if 行为不变，.timedOut 与 .success 在此不可区分。
failure: 不是运行时故障，而是丢失了信息通道：走到 154 行说明三条 drain 都已结束（子进程已被 terminate），这里本该是 157 行那句「文档输出过大或 CLI 未结束」，用户与日志拿到的是「超时」这一错误归因。

summary: FeishuJSON 的 Codable 里只有解码被用到，手写的 encode(to:) 在 Sources/ 与 Tests/ 全仓无调用点。
evidence: 5: `indirect enum FeishuJSON: Codable, Sendable, Equatable`，16-26 是 `func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws`。全仓 grep：解码侧有 `FeishuJSON.payload`（42 行 JSONDecoder）与 FeishuDocumentStore/FeishuOperationSheet 里的 `.text/.items/.flag` 读取；编码侧 `JSONEncoder().encode` 的调用点（ProviderStore:760、SettingsManager:60、ConnectorManager:960、MigrationStorage:145/175 等）全部是别的模型类型，没有任何一处编码 FeishuJSON。
failure: 无运行时后果；代价是 11 行永不执行的手写编码器随枚举 case 漂移（新增 case 时 encode 忘记同步编译器也不会报错）。

summary: stderr 用与 stdout 相同的 16 MiB 保留上限在攒数据，而这份数据从未被任何代码读过：一趟 CLI 调用可以白白 append 并释放 16 MiB。
evidence: 83-92: `var data = Data(); func read(_ handle: FileHandle) { while let chunk = try? handle.read(upToCount: 65_536), !chunk.isEmpty { if data.count + chunk.count <= 16 * 1024 * 1024 { data.append(chunk) } else { exceeded = true } } }`；133 建了两个实例，139 把 `err` 的字节读进 `errors`；但 156/162 只消费 `output.data` 与 `output.exceeded`，`errors` 是纯写不读（44 行还写明「Never echo them」，即这份文本永远不会展示）。
failure: 一个向 stderr 刷日志的 lark-cli（例如 17 MB 级别的诊断输出，测试夹具里正是这种形状：feishu-documents-regressions.py:690 的 large 分支）会让父进程按 64 KiB 分块 append 到 16 MiB 的 Data，随后整块释放；纯属一次可见的毫秒级 CPU 与 16 MiB 瞬时内存，信息量为零，且 `errors.exceeded` 从不上报。
fix: 给 stderr 一个丢弃型 sink（固定 64 KiB 环形缓冲，或用 readabilityHandler 只 continue 不收字节），保留 it 继续 drain 的性质即可。

summary: flag 只认字面 true，而两个飞书回归夹具只喂过 true/false；数值型 0/1 布尔（Drive 返回形态之一）若被解成 .number，分页会在第一页静默结束。
evidence: 39: `var flag: Bool { self == .bool(true) }`；10 行的解码顺序是先 `try? c.decode(Bool.self)` 再 `try? c.decode(Double.self)`，即数值 1 变成 .bool 还是 .number 取决于 Foundation 的 NSNumber/Bool 桥接。Tests/feishu-documents-regressions.py:53-68 与 Tests/feishu-component-regressions.py 的全部夹具都写字面 true 或 false。同一仓库的 JSONTreeView.swift:95-99 正因为这类歧义而显式防御：`if any is Bool { return true }; guard let n = any as? NSNumber else { return false }; return CFGetTypeID(n) == CFBooleanGetTypeID()`。
failure: 若某个 Drive/Wiki 响应把 has_more 写成 1 且解码得到 .number(1)，FeishuPage.parse 的 `data["has_more"].flag` 为 false → cursor 清空 → 「加载更多」永不出现、列表静默停在第一页，症状与该文件已经修过的 page_token 事故完全一致（用户只看到列表变短，没有任何错误提示）。
fix: 在 feishu-documents-regressions.py 的 has_more 用例里补 0/1 两种数值形状；并按测量结果决定 flag 是否接受 .number(1)（`self == .bool(true) || self == .number(1)`）或显式记录 CLI 只发真布尔。

summary: 每次 resolve 都新建两个 Calendar 并对中文日历取 dateComponents；resolve 在每个 body pass（含天空拖动每一帧）重跑，且没有任何缓存。
evidence: line 266-269 `var solar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)` + `solar.dateComponents([...], from: date)`；line 273-275 `var lunar = Calendar(identifier: .chinese)` + `lunar.dateComponents([.month, .day, .isLeapMonth], from: date)`，都在 `holiday(on:)` 函数体内、无缓存；line 122 与 146 又各自调 `SolarTerm.term/season`（SolarTerm.swift:103-105 每次同样新建 gregorian Calendar）。调用点 GreetingCard.swift:274-292 的 `private var phrase` 在 body 里计算（GreetingCard.swift:398 每个 body pass 都读 `phrase.salutation`），而 AtmosphereRenderer.swift:308 的注释正是「The sheet asks on every body pass — each frame of a drag」，即拖动天空时 timeOffset 每帧变化 → 每帧一次 resolve。
failure: 拖动/键盘漫游天空（计划 120 Hz）时，每一帧都要构造 2 个 Calendar、做一次中文日历 components 与一次 gregorian components 并枚举节气表，而结果只依赖 (日, 时区, 小时) 这一极少变化的键；这是纯粹重复解析，且同一份数据在 SolarTerm 里另有一套 Calendar。
fix: 在 GreetingPhrase 内按 (date 的年月日, timeZone) 缓存 holiday/term/season 结果（同一天内复用；时区变化才失效），或把 holiday/term 的查询结果随 `phrase` 一起提到 GreetingCard 的 @State 里，只在 skyDate 的日/小时改变时重算。

summary: 只按温度（≥33 / ≤8）与只按风速（≥39）的两条分支没有任何回归；现有用例里的 35°C 被 weather=rain 提前短路掩盖。
evidence: line 246 `if let wind = context.windKph, wind.isFinite, wind >= 39 {`、line 251 `if temperature >= 33`、line 255 `if temperature <= 8`；Tests/greeting-phrase-regressions.py:118 `let rainy = GreetingPhrase.Context(weather: .rain, temperature: 35)` 与 line 136 的 storm 都自带 weather，weatherPhrase 在 line 229-243 就 return 了，温度分支永远到不了；grep `windKph` 在该测试文件里零命中（只有 greeting-layout 的 SkyScene 用到风速）。
failure: 把 33/8/39 三个阈值或风向判断改坏（例如把 >=33 写成 >33、把 wind 的 isFinite 删掉）不会让 greeting-phrase 回归失败；卡片上表现为晴天高温/大风时不再出现对应的问候句，而测试全绿。

summary: renderers 把「驱动没发布该键」与「该子单元 0%」混为一谈，缺键时会画出永远不亮的格子。
evidence: line 26 `static let rendererKeys = ["Device Utilization %", "Renderer Utilization %", "Tiler Utilization %"]`；line 52-54 `if (dict["gpu-core-count"] as? Int) != nil { best.renderers = rendererKeys.map { Self.percent(stats[$0]) } }`；line 67-75 的 percent 对缺失键（default 分支）与对 0 值都返回 0。HardwareDetailPanel.swift:88-92 依 `units > 0` 宣称「每一格是一组图形子单元，按各自的实时占用点亮」。

summary: sysctl 失败与「压力正常」不可区分：返回码被丢弃，0 既是失败初值也是正常值。
evidence: line 150 注释「0 = normal, 2 = warning, 4 = critical」；line 152-155 `var level = 0; var size = ...; sysctlbyname("kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level", &level, &size, nil, 0); return level`——返回值与 size 都不检查。消费方 ResourceStrip.swift:172-173 用 `>= 4` 判「严重」、`>= 2` 判「偏高」，0 落到「正常」。

summary: `persistenceModeDidChange` is declared but never posted anywhere; its only counterpart is an observer in `ProviderStore.startUsageWatcher`.
evidence:
`grep -rn "persistenceModeDidChange" Sources Tests` → only the declaration (NotificationService.swift:21) and ProviderStore.swift:1238 (`NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(forName: .persistenceModeDidChange …)`); no `post(name: .persistenceModeDidChange)` and no `NotificationCenter.default.post` of that name anywhere.
Same class of leftover: `UsageIndex.reloadPersistence()` (UsageIndex.swift:200) and `ProxyCaptureStore.reloadPersistence()` (ProxyCaptureStore.swift:215) have zero production callers — only Tests/usage-index-regressions.py:93/155/207/249/287 call them. There is a `@Published var useDatabase` in the stores, but no Settings row writes `databaseEnabled` (grep only hits DiskPersistence's default-true read at UsageJSONStore.swift:8-9).
failure: No user-visible failure by itself; it documents a mode switch that does not exist, so the next maintainer wires a Settings toggle to a notification nothing listens to (or vice versa) and the SQLite/JSON flip never takes effect for an already-running app (the observer only fires `refreshUsage(rescan: true)`, it does not reset the backend — that is `reloadPersistence`, which is production-unreachable).

summary: `.askOnUse` is documented as "macOS exposes no query" yet is set for no permission by `refreshStatus`; it survives only as the dictionary default in `systemStatus(_:)` and the `@unknown default` branch, so the "macOS will ask at the moment of use" label is never shown where it was designed to be.
evidence:
refreshStatus (232-247) assigns: widgetData `.askOnUse`, automation `.askOnUse`, cursorData `.notRequired`, screenRecording granted/notDetermined, bluetooth allowed/denied/notDetermined, location/currentLocation from CLAuthorizationStatus, notifications from UNUserNotificationCenter.
`systemStatus` (162-164) returns `statuses[permission] ?? .askOnUse`, and because `refreshStatus` runs in `init` (line 155) the only entries are the ones above — for `.notifications` and `.currentLocation` there is no writer, so those two *are* `.askOnUse`; for `.location` etc. the default never fires. Every `@unknown default: .askOnUse` (228, 243, 256) is therefore also labelled with a status that is never displayed for any known case.

summary: The switch cache is seeded once from `PermissionGate.allows` (UserDefaults) while the mirrored prefs are seeded from `AppPreferences.shared` with `.dropFirst()`; if the singleton is ever first touched before `AppPreferences` finishes loading, the two sources disagree for the life of the process.
evidence:
128-130: `enabled[permission] = PermissionGate.allows(permission)` (reads UserDefaults.standard)
132-134: `prefs.$idleNotifyEnabled.dropFirst() … self?.enabled[.notifications] = on`
`.dropFirst()` means the harness's first write is never applied, and `AppPreferences.init` (AppPreferences.swift:289-291) itself seeds `idleNotifyEnabled` from UserDefaults *after* the singleton is created.
failure: If `PermissionCenter.shared` is constructed in a context where `AppPreferences.shared` has not yet run `didSetReady`-style seeding (e.g. the widget/bootstrap ordering changes, or a future call from the app delegate's early window), `enabled[.notifications]` and `AppPreferences.shared.idleNotifyEnabled` diverge and only a toggle reconciles them. `.dropFirst()` also means any write performed by the store between the publisher's creation and the subscriber's attachment is lost.
fix: Seed the two bridged entries from `prefs` after wiring the sink (or publish current values with `send(initial:)` semantics) so both sides always come from the same source.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: both sides read the same UserDefaults key ("idleNotifyEnabled"), so the two sources cannot disagree; the divergence needs a key mismatch that does not exist.

summary: The TCC-gate refactor in the ancestor of this file (`e86960a`) is verified only for `BuildChannel.promptsForSystemPermissions`'s value; no regression pins that the switch still stores the choice and that the request functions are gated when `promptsForSystemPermissions` is false.

summary: ps 子进程既无超时也无进程组终止：一旦 ps 卡住，utility 线程同步等待不可取消。
evidence: ProcessMemoryRow.swift:18-21 `readToEnd()`（注释自认“blocks until ps exits”），取消路径只 `process.terminate()`（19/25），即只给 ps 发 SIGTERM，没有 setpgid/子进程组；MemoryDetailPanel.swift:53-58 的 worker 只在面板消失时 cancel。实测正常路径 20 ms（-O，真实 /bin/ps），所以平时无感；但面板每次打开/刷新都会新建一个 detached worker（48 行 `.task(id: refresh)`，无去重），被 SIGSTOP 的 ps 会让一个 utility 线程永久挂住，相关 ps 仍在持有 pipe。
failure: 系统监控/安全软件把 ps 停住（或 ps 自身挂死）→ 多次打开内存面板后累积挂起线程，面板永远停在“读取中…”且进程不可回收。
fix: 给 read() 加 deadline（例如 `DispatchWorkItem` 到点 terminate 子进程组，同 AudioAccessoryMonitor.swift:1053 的做法），或在 panel 侧用 `withThrowingTaskGroup` 竞速超时。

summary: 没有 Process.terminationHandler，取消后靠 deinit 回收；实测 deinit 会 reap，所以残留风险只在 readToEnd 返回值语义上——用户主动取消（关闭面板）时本次读取必定作废。
evidence: ProcessMemoryRow.swift:14-28：`defer { try? close() }` 会重点关闭读端（22-23 注释自认这是 readToEnd 的取消可见点），但随后 24-27 仍 `process.terminate()` 后返回 nil。实测（-O，复刻该路径）：child 在 Process 释放 1 s 后为 <gone>，说明 Foundation 在 deinit 里 reap，未观察到僵尸；但 24 行的 guard 一旦命中就丢弃整份已读到的数据。
failure: 用户打开内存面板后立刻关闭再打开 → 第一次的读取即使已经拿到完整数据也会被 cancel 丢弃（“无法读取进程”或长时间“读取中”），因为没有任何“已完成”与“已取消”的区分。
fix: 在 24 行之前先 `let finished = !process.isRunning`（或改用 terminationHandler + continuation），数据已完整时直接返回，不再走取消丢弃。

summary: Share.memShare 全仓无读取方，却仍在每 tick 被计算并量化

summary: A damaged or oversized tail costs one full UTF-8 decode plus one JSONSerialization attempt per 64 KB chunk with no failure budget, so the reader scans an arbitrarily long garbage region of an unbounded external file before concluding there is no history.
evidence: The loop (lines 371-390) is bounded only by `position > 0`; when a chunk contains no `0x0A` it falls through to `pending = Data(chunk[..<end])` (line 389) and keeps walking backwards. `appendLines` then does `String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)` (line 362) and `decode` does `line.data(using: .utf8)` + `JSONSerialization.jsonObject` (lines 470-471) for the single never-completing line — a truncation-sensitive parse of the whole 64 KB. tests/access-log-tail-regressions.py:166-176 builds a 180 KB unparsable tail, but only asserts the returned ids, never the scan cost (`limitations` in that harness admits 'oversized corrupt records may require larger reads').
failure: A sidecar that has been appended to by something that no longer writes newlines (a partial write from an older build, a binary-mangled file) makes every launch pay ~1 decode + 1 JSON parse per 64 KB of garbage before the console shows anything, on the load queue, with the whole file's worth of chunk buffers held until the scan ends.
fix: Stop after two consecutive chunks that yield no parsed row and start with no newline (or cap total unparsable bytes, e.g. 1 MB), and skip `JSONSerialization` entirely when the chunk contains no `"id":`.

summary: The displayed `入` column assumes every stored row was written post-fold, but rows written before `TokenTotals.setPrompt` existed (and the third-party Anthropic path `ProxyUsageStore` calls out) still carry the cache hit inside `promptTokens`, so 入 is inflated by exactly 缓存 for those rows.
evidence: Lines 107-113 document '`TokenTotals` has already folded the cache hit out of the upstream's prompt count, so `入 + 缓存` is the prompt the model actually saw', and `tokenField` (lines 119-122) prints `promptTokens` verbatim. Utils/StreamAssembler.swift:60-84 states the fold is a *new* invariant enforced at write time ('The subtraction happens on every apply'), and Utils/ProxyUsageStore.swift:215-230 records that rows predating it exist and needed a one-time repair ('a row's shape was never recorded'). `decode` (lines 502-505) has no field or flag to tell the two shapes apart, and the settle path only merges post-fold `TokenTotals`.
failure: On a sidecar that outlived the older build, a legacy row renders `入 103.9K 缓存 50.0K` where 入 already contains 缓存; any user reading the column as fresh input (as the doc comment promises) over-counts uncached input, and sums 入+缓存 past the real prompt. Not reproducible on rows written by the current build — hence low confidence about how many such rows remain in a given install.
fix: Stamp the shape on write (`"folded":true` in `encode`, line 444) and, for legacy rows at load time, subtract `cacheReadTokens` from `promptTokens` once when the key is absent — the same arithmetic and the same assumption as `ProxyUsageStore.migrateLocked`.

summary: The `HH:mm` clock formatter has three copies that have already drifted; the preview-harness copy drops the `en_US_POSIX` locale the production copy exists for.
evidence: Production: lines 150-155 set `locale = en_US_POSIX` with the explicit rationale that a bare `HH:mm` 'still resolves through the user's calendar, and in a Thai locale that renders the year in Buddhist numerals'. Tools/render-mainwindow-preview.py:446-449 mirrors the property at line 447 but with `let f = DateFormatter(); f.dateFormat = "HH:mm"` and no locale. Two further copies: Utils/VpnDomainLog.swift:171-179 (same pattern, `HH:mm:ss`) and the cached `UsageStats.formatter("HH:mm")` used by Views/Shared/VpnTopChrome.swift:229. Consumers: Views/Pages/TrafficView.swift:1131 (a row per capture, per publish).

fix: Point the preview fixture at the production formatter/mirror its `locale` line, and collapse the two remaining in-app copies onto `UsageStats.formatter("HH:mm:ss")` (which already caches per pattern and zone).

summary: `ProxyLogTap.id` is stored but never read anywhere in Sources, Tests or Tools.

summary: `.clip` and `.clipPath` take an explicit cap and testify to a shared contract, but isolation is by convention only: `ProxyCaptureStore.clip` delegates to the shared `CaptureTranscript.clip` while the access log's own two `clip` variants do not. `CaptureTranscript.clip` trims whitespace and implements the `cap`/`cap-1` decision the same way; `CaptureTranscript.clip` already has the exact contract the log would need. Kept the surface duplication in the report because the caller's usage below is where it drifts.
evidence: Line 508-513 replaces only `\n` and `\r` (leaving tabs and vertical tabs inside provider/model/error fields), caps at `cap - 1` and does not trim; line 515-517 caps at 160 without trimming; by contrast `CaptureTranscript.clip(_ text: String, cap: Int = 160)` (CaptureTranscript.swift:85-92) trims and emits the character count of `cap` as an ellipsis by the letter of the comment. Both are called from begin() (lines 241-245) / finish() (line 297).
failure: No user-visible failure by itself; the reason it matters here is the caller below.

verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07: ProxyAccessLog.clip now delegates to CaptureTranscript.clip (the windowed, trim-aware fold), so the console and the capture list render one model name the same way; the divergent hand-rolled variant is gone.

summary: `model` and `provider` are clipped to 80 characters, but the value they carry is a client-supplied `model` field pulled straight out of the request body — `CodexProxyServer.peekJSON` returns `(json["model"] as? String) ?? ""` with no length limit, and the body cap is 64 MiB. A 60 MiB `model` string is copied twice (peek + clip) on the proxy's hop, before the 80-char truncation that actually matters.
evidence: Line 244-245: `provider: Self.clip(provider, 80), model: Self.clip(model, 80)`; the model arrives from `startLog` (CodexProxyServer.swift:1196-1210) which calls `Self.peekJSON(request.body)` (line 1228-1234: `((json["model"] as? String) ?? "", ...)`). `clip` first does two `replacingOccurrences` over the whole string and only then truncates (line 509-512).
failure: A client (or a buggy SDK) sends a multi-megabyte model name; the proxy burns CPU/memory copying it on the request path merely to throw almost all of it away — self-inflicted latency on every such call.
fix: Bound before copying: `let m = model.count > 200 ? String(model.prefix(200)) : model` at the `startLog` call site, or make `clip` early-return once `s.count <= cap` before the two `replacingOccurrences` passes (also a wasted allocation for every ordinary short provider/model string).
verdict_note: Fixed 2026-10-07 with 608: the whole-string two-replace fold (which copied a multi-MB model string twice before truncating) is replaced by the windowed fold that stops once the window carries `cap` characters.

summary: `ProxyLogTap.id` is stored but never read anywhere in the repo — not by the proxy (five call sites in CodexProxyServer.swift only pass the tap through, never its id), not by the UI, not by the Python/Swift test harnesses.

summary: SessionHost has no regression slice at all, so the pid→host-app walk and the tty validation that decide whether 继续会话 duplicates a session are unverified.
evidence: `grep -rln "SessionHost" Tests/` exits 1 (no file matches) across all 78 test files listed in the Makefile's TEST_SUITES. The functions are pure and slice-friendly (they read only proc_pidinfo, NSRunningApplication and devname), unlike the rest of the file. Their inputs are the load-bearing ones: `host(of:)` walks up to 24 parents looking for `activationPolicy == .regular` (lines 34-43) and `ttyPath` seeds the AppleScript literal that decides which tab is focused (lines 92-98, guard `tty.hasPrefix("tty") && allSatisfy(isASCII && letter/number)`).

fix: Add a `session-host` slice to Tests (registered in the Makefile's single TEST_SUITES list) covering `ttyPath` rejections (`/dev/tty`, `ttya;rm`, empty) and `host(of: ownPID)`, which should find the test runner's own parent chain without any GUI.

summary: The child --version probe polls isRunning every 10ms for up to 5s on the service actor, and the timeout branch is untested.
evidence: Lines 226-233: `while process.isRunning { if Task.isCancelled || Date() > deadline { process.terminate(); throw ... } ; Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.01) }` — 500 wakeups per probe, on the actor that also runs preview/prepare, which probes version twice per prepare (line 78 and via preview at line 76/122). Tests' stub clients answer instantly (Tests/session-migration-regressions.py:31-34), so MigrationFailure.unavailable/timeout paths have no coverage.

fix: Use a termination handler/continuation with a DispatchSemaphore-backed deadline instead of 100Hz polling, and add a stub client that outlives the deadline to pin the refusal.

summary: The `.claude` branch lets an unmapped Cocoa error escape when `~/.claude/projects` is absent, where the `.codex` branch carefully maps the same condition to `MigrationFailure.missing`.

summary: A missing model key on the newest usage-bearing assistant record keeps an older record's model, pairing a stale model with the new token count for the context-limit lookup.

summary: The first 300-second window of the civil day is bracketed with the altitude sampled exactly at `day.start` instead of the interval's midpoint, so a crossing that falls in [day.start, day.start+300) is never seen and the day's result is frozen nil by the cache.
evidence: Lines 54-60: `var start = day.start; var previous = altitude(start) ... let end = min(start.addingTimeInterval(300), day.end); let next = altitude(end); if (previous <= 0 && next > 0) || (previous > 0 && next <= 0) { ... }`. `previous` is taken at `day.start` and is already the first window's left edge, so a rise at, say, 00:02 local gives `previous <= 0`, `next > 0` and the detection test never runs for it; every later iteration samples at the window's midpoint-independent right edge, which cannot see it either. I swept 60-69 N (lon 0) across whole years plus every offset from UTC-11 to UTC+12 and found no realistic (latitude, longitude, zone) triple that currently lands a crossing in that 300-s band — hence low confidence — so this is an off-by-one that awaits a location/timezone that puts a sunrise at local midnight, not an observed failure.
failure: For a location whose sunrise or sunset falls within the first five minutes of its civil day in the passed zone, `solarEvents` returns nil for that crossing, and because the result is stored in `solarCache` keyed by (day, zone, lat, lon) the miss is permanent for that day: the greeting card's `SunPath` falls back to the dashed placeholder instead of the arc.
fix: Seed the loop with the midpoint of the first interval (`var previous = altitude(start.addingTimeInterval(150))`) or start the loop half a window before `day.start`; either keeps the window count bounded and makes the bracket consistent.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: previous = altitude(day.start) is the first window's left edge and the sign test at :58 catches a crossing inside [day.start, day.start+300); no crossing is skipped.

summary: The sampling policy this file exists for — per-interface 32-bit wrap subtraction, the elapsed-time gate, and the loopback exclusion — has no regression test; the one suite naming the file only greps a call site.

evidence: SystemThroughput.swift:118-119 keys counters by BSD name (counters[String(cString: name)]) and line 90 does guard let before = previous[name] else { continue }, treating any absent name as an interface that just appeared. On macOS the tunnel device is reused by slot (utun3, utun4, ...) with if_data counters reset on creation, so a new tunnel can land on a name present in the previous sample; the comment at lines 86-93 says the guard exists exactly for the just-appeared case. Static reasoning only; no interface-lifecycle test was run.
failure: A tunnel that reconnects onto the same utun slot as the previous one has its fresh counter subtracted against the dead tunnel's totals, so the first tick after the reconnect reports a bogus burst (or, if the counter decreased, wraps and clamps for a second) on the always-on strip.
fix: Treat a decreasing per-interface counter as a baseline change rather than a delta (skip the interface when current.bytesIn < before.bytesIn || current.bytesOut < before.bytesOut), which is also the cheap way to keep a wrap out of the sum.
summary: Counter baselines are keyed by interface name alone, so a recreated utun slot can be subtracted against the previous tunnel's totals

When `inDesktop == true` but the `codex://` handler cannot be resolved, the function falls through every desktop branch into `launch(...)` and starts a `codex resume` copy in a terminal — the exact fork the live-pid guard above exists to prevent.
evidence: TerminalLauncher.swift:81-107. L83 `if let pid, !inDesktop, SessionHost.reveal(...)` deliberately skips the live-agent reveal for a desktop thread; L88-91 opens Desktop only `if inDesktop, let desktopURL`; L93 needs Otty; L101-104 needs `desktopURL != nil`. If `desktopURL == nil` (L84-85 resolves `urlForApplication(toOpen:)` to nil — Codex Desktop uninstalled, or its `codex://` scheme unregistered while the app is still running), control reaches L105-106 `guard usable else { return }` / `launch(command:cwd:sessionId:)` with `command = "codex resume \(sessionId)"` (L86).
failure: A notification tap or tile double-click for a session whose `inDesktop` flag is set, with the `codex://` scheme unresolvable at that moment: `codex resume <id>` runs in the chosen terminal and opens a second concurrent copy of a thread that Codex Desktop already holds. (Uncertainty: if Desktop is genuinely gone the terminal fallback is desirable, and I could not verify how often `urlForApplication(toOpen:)` returns nil while Desktop is live.)
fix: Turn the unresolvable-handler case into a decision rather than a fall-through: when `inDesktop` is true and `desktopURL == nil`, either return (leave the session to Desktop) or prefer `SessionHost.reveal(pid:)` for a live pid, instead of reaching `launch`.

evidence: TerminalLauncher.swift:264-269 (_ = try? proc.run() inside a detached Task) and the identical shape at SessionHost.swift:141-148. A scratch program that spawns and drops the reference showed the child still running after the reference is gone (Foundation keeps a pending-exit list), so the Process object stays alive somewhere while never being waited on; grep for zombie/reap finds a reap habit only in VpnManager (reapOrphanCore), and every other osascript/helper spawn in the repo either holds its Process or calls waitUntilExit.
failure: Two of the app's osascript senders are fire-and-forget: no termination status is ever read (a denied Apple Event is indistinguishable from success), and whether the child is retired is left to whichever task runs the pending exit, so when it is the detached task the Process and its pipe live on. This is the same gap that makes the Warp failure silent; confidence is medium because the deallocation timing was not observed directly.
fix: Hold the Process in a small static registry or a task awaiting terminationHandler so the child is retired deterministically and its status/stderr can be surfaced; that also keeps a slow osascript from outliving a quit.
summary: runAppleScript drops the Process and reads no exit status, leaving both the child's reaping and the failure signal to chance

summary: For `.all`, the bucket walk starts at `min(records.keys)` and extends to `min(interval.end, tomorrow)`; if the record set includes dates in the future relative to `now`, the series gets empty future buckets it then counts as observed zeros
evidence: L79: `let start = period == .all ? (records.keys.min() ?? calendar.startOfDay(for: now)) : interval.start`; L80-81 `let end = min(interval.end, tomorrow)` with `tomorrow = startOfDay(now)+1`. Records with a future day key are possible when a transcript is written by a process with a skewed clock; `UsageStats.interval(for: .all)` ends at tomorrow so the clamp is against today in the normal case, but the *start* for `.all` is taken from the raw record set with no `min(now)` clamp.
failure: A single future-dated transcript puts a string of extra zero buckets at the end of the `all` series: `activeDays` denominator, `median`/`p95` (interpolate over zeros) and the month/year rollup all shift, so the headline stats for the whole history drop without any data change.
fix: Clamp the record keys used for the `.all` start to `now`'s day (`records.keys.filter { $0 <= todayStart }.min()`), matching the existing `end` clamp.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: end is clamped to tomorrow, so future-dated record keys cannot add trailing buckets; the empty-bucket failure cannot occur.

summary: `UsageClaims.reset()` is unreachable in production: its only caller is `UsageIndex.reloadPersistence`, which itself has no production caller since the `databaseEnabled` preference and its Settings toggle were deleted
evidence: `grep -rn "reloadPersistence" Sources --include='*.swift'` finds `Sources/ClaudeBar/Utils/UsageIndex.swift:200` (definition), its call at `:210`, and the doc comment in `ProxyCaptureStore.swift:214-215`; no other source file calls it. `git show 16b225e` removed `@Published var databaseEnabled` and the `persistenceModeDidChange` post from AppPreferences, and `grep -rn "databaseEnabled" Sources` now finds it only as the UserDefaults key read by `DiskPersistence.useDatabase`; nothing writes it, so `useDatabase` is permanently `true` and `persistenceModeDidChange` is never posted (ProviderStore.swift:1236-1241 observer can never fire).
failure: The reset path is never exercised in production, so a stale ledger survives every backend switch that can no longer happen — and the comments in UsageClaims.swift:55-57 and UsageIndex.swift:198-199 describe behaviour no longer reachable.
fix: Either delete `reloadPersistence`/`reset` (the tests drive them directly and would need their own reset hook), or keep them and note they are test-only; do not leave a doc comment claiming the `databaseEnabled` preference still switches backends.
verdict_note: Re-checked 2026-10-07: the misleading databaseEnabled doc was corrected; reloadPersistence and UsageClaims.reset now carry honest "used by the regression harness" comments (UsageIndex.swift:198, UsageClaims.swift:56-57).

summary: `start()` calls the lock-free `stop()` and then re-derives `existing` from a second `fileExists` check with no shared state between them; a concurrently stopped/started stream cannot be cancelled by the later `stop()`
evidence: L21-23: `static func start(paths: [String], handler: @escaping () -> Void) { stop(); let existing = paths.filter { FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: $0) }; guard !existing.isEmpty else { return } ... }`. `stop()` (L51-75) clears `stream`/`handler`/`debounceWork` under `lock` and re-targets the old stream onto `queue` for teardown. If the watched project directory is missing at `stop()` time — which is exactly what `guard !existing.isEmpty` handles — `stop()` returns *before* installing the teardown, so nothing the caller believed was torn down here remains.
failure: ProviderStore calls `UsageFSWatcher.stop()` when the window hides (line 664-667) and `start(...)` when it shows. A hide/show race where the directory listing is momentarily empty (a mount/rename under `~/.claude/projects`) leaves the caller's `usageWatcherStarted` true while no stream exists, and no stop call will clear the stale stream — FSEvents keeps waking the app; the only other observable is that the next visible transition skips the catch-up rescan because `usageWatcherStoppedAt` was never set.
fix: Have `stop()` always record its teardown (holding the lock) even when there is no live stream, and make `start()` re-check under the same lock; or return an explicit status so `usageWatcherStarted` cannot diverge.
verdict_note: Re-verified 2026-10-07: stop() reads the stream static (not a filesystem check), clears it under the lock and tears down; start()'s empty-paths guard cannot leave a stream behind, so the described race does not hold.

summary: 同一文件在同一次 sync 中对头 256 字节做两次 headHash 读取（一次判定是否变号、一次写回存储），命中条件本身已排除改写。
evidence: 769 行：`let currentHash = (prior != nil && file.size >= prior!.size) ? headHash(file.path, length: 256) : 0`；974 行（JSON 后端）与 989 行（SQLite 后端）在 upsertFile/upsertFileSQL 中再次 `headHash(file.path, length: 256)` 新开 FileHandle 重读。对一个 size 只增长的文件，769 行读到的哈希与 989 行几乎必然相同（头 256 字节不因追加改变），即两次 open+read 里至少一次是纯重复。
failure: 每次文件变更（每次增量追加）多一次 open/seek/read/close + FNV 循环；在全量重建时对每个文件都发生，叠加打开成本。
fix: 把 769 行算出的 currentHash 传进 upsertFile/upsertFileSQL，避免二次读；仅在无法给出哈希时（如列不可用时）内部重算。

summary: usage-files.json is decoded all-or-nothing while the neighbouring rollup decode is deliberately line-lossy, so one malformed FileRec throws away every file's offset/headHash/cxTotal state and forces a full corpus re-parse.
evidence: UsageJSONStore.swift:230-233 `if let data = try? Data(contentsOf: FilePaths.usageFilesJSON), let obj = try? JSONDecoder().decode([String: FileRec].self, from: data) { files = obj }` — `FileRec.init(from:)` (lines 42-54) decodes mtime/size/offset/headHash/cxIn/cxOut/cxCached as *required*, so a single entry lacking any of them fails the decode for the whole dictionary, and `try?` swallows the error (`files` stays `[:]`, `loaded` is still set true). Directly below, lines 236-245 go out of their way to be lossy: 「Lossy decode: … Skipping the bad line keeps the rest of the rollup readable — strict decoding threw away every other line with it.」 Files written by the deleted JSON-backend era, hand-edits, or disk damage are the acknowledged threat model for the same file.
failure: usage-files.json contains one entry missing a key (or with a mistyped number) → `files` is empty for this process → `UsageIndex.knownFromJSON()` returns `[:]` → `sync(file:prior:nil)` takes the full-reparse branch for every transcript in the corpus (~1,250 files on this machine), discarding each file's byte offset, head hash and Codex cx_total dedupe stamps; the Codex dedupe across append boundaries restarts from 0 and the next FSEvents burst re-parses everything again until the file is rewritten. No log line records the decode failure.
fix: Decode per entry the way CaptureJSONStore does per line: read `[String: Any]`, then `for (key, value) in obj { if let rec = try? JSONDecoder().decode(FileRec.self, from: JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: value)) { files[key] = rec } }` (or add decodeIfPresent defaults for headHash/offset/cx*), so one bad entry costs one file's incremental state instead of all of them.
verdict_note: Deletion resolves it: usage-files.json is neither read nor written any more.

summary: Bucket sums use trapping Int arithmetic on values read back from the on-disk rollup, so an out-of-range counter in usage-rollup.jsonl traps the process at query time.
evidence: UsageJSONStore.swift:156-161 folds rows with `Self.accumulate(row, into: &byModel)` (lines 387-395: `u.inputTokens += row.input; … u.cacheCreationTokens += row.cacheCreate`) and then evaluates `$0.totalTokens > 0`; `ModelUsage.totalTokens` (Models/ModelUsage.swift:83) is `inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadTokens + cacheCreationTokens` with no overflow guard. The four Ints are decoded straight from JSONL (RollupRec, lines 61-70) or from `JSONCoerce.intVal` (Utils/JSONCoerce.swift:14-16), which clamps to the Int64 range but not to anything a 4-way sum can hold. The same unchecked shape exists on the parse side (UsageIndex.swift:1226 `e.input + e.output + e.cacheRead + e.cacheCreate > 0`).
failure: A corrupt or hand-edited usage-rollup.jsonl line such as `{"path":"claude:x","day":"2026-01-01","model":"m","calls":1,"input":9223372036854775807,"output":9223372036854775807,…}` (or a transcript whose usage counters are huge) → `Int` addition overflows in `totalTokens` → SIGTRAP in the usage query path, which runs on the background usage-refresh task and takes the whole app down. Reachability requires corrupt/absurd input rather than normal data, which is why this is low severity.
fix: Clamp the four buckets to a sane per-bucket ceiling where they enter the model (JSONCoerce or RollupRec decode, e.g. reject values with `magnitude > Int.max / 4`), or make the sums saturating in `ModelUsage.totalTokens`/`merge` and in `ParsedEntry.aggregated`'s per-field adds — matching the precedent set for VPN/weather remote data in commit 5c45f70.
verdict_note: Deletion resolves it: no local bucket arithmetic reads from a JSON rollup; SQL SUMs run in SQLite (64-bit INTEGER).

summary: The JSON store's per-file session query has no production caller; it is exercised only by the regression harness, which its sibling API (fetchByPath) has already replaced in UsageIndex.
evidence: UsageJSONStore.swift:178-188 `func fetchSession(pathPrefix:pathSuffix:)` — repo-wide grep for `fetchSession(` finds no Sources caller of the JSON-store overload: UsageIndex.updateIndexJSON / fetchSessionFamilies use `UsageJSONStore.shared.fetchByPath` (UsageIndex.swift:364) and the SQLite branch of `fetchSessionFamilies` (UsageIndex.swift:357-423) never touches the JSON store. The only callers are Tests/backend-performance-regressions.py:83,90,94,96,102,105,106,108, which slice the class out of source. `git log -p -S "fetchSession(pathPrefix"` shows UsageIndex stopped calling it in c708081 (「perf: 三路并行审查后的模块、后端与 UI 性能优化」), leaving the method and its `rollupKeysByPath` scan behind. (Test-only, not entirely unreferenced: the harness asserts by it.)
failure: No runtime failure: dead weight that keeps a second, divergent session-matching rule (suffix `hasSuffix(pathSuffix)` + `hasSuffix` path scan) alive next to the family router that actually ships, so a future fix to session attribution must be applied twice or the tests validate a path nothing runs.
fix: Either delete the method and rewrite the harness assertions onto `fetchByPath` (the shipped API), or, if it is intentionally kept as a test seam, keep it but have the harness compare against `fetchByPath` so the two cannot drift.
verdict_note: Deletion resolves it: the per-file session query that only the harness exercised is gone with the store.

summary: Only the 「parserVersion missing」 rebranch of the JSON backend's migration is tested; the other three legacy-detection predicates and the no-op case (current generation must NOT drop anything) have no regression.
evidence: UsageJSONStore.swift:248-277 defines four independent predicates — `stale` (a codex row with model == "codex"), `unprefixed` (a codex FileRec with usage but `cxTotal == 0`), `oldParser` (`parserVersion < 10`), `oldClaude` (`parserVersion < 11`). Tests/usage-index-regressions.py:257 only deletes the `parserVersion` key for all files (`for key in files.keys { files[key]?.removeValue(forKey: "parserVersion") }`) and then asserts the rebuild count; the SQLite half of the same test (line 250-253) does fabricate an inflated rollup, but that is `migrateIfNeeded`, not this file. Nothing asserts that a corpus whose FileRecs are all `parserVersion == 11` and `cxTotal > 0` is left untouched (no drop, offsets preserved), nor the `model == "codex"` / `cxTotal == 0` codex-specific branches.
failure: A regression that makes one predicate always true (e.g. flipping the parserVersion comparison) silently drops every Claude or Codex file row on every launch and re-parses the whole corpus each start — the exact class of bug the predicates were added to fix — and no test turns red; conversely a predicate that never fires leaves the double-booked resumed-transcript rows (103M tokens measured) in place undetected.
fix: Extend Tests/usage-index-regressions.py's JSON arm: (a) seed files.json with all three legacy shapes one at a time (codex model "codex"; codex cxTotal 0 with usage; parserVersion 10) and assert exactly the expected subset of rows disappears; (b) add the negative case — a corpus stamped parserVersion 11 / cxTotal > 0 must keep its `offset`/`headHash` (assert no re-parse by leaving a sentinel offset and checking it survives `load()`).
verdict_note: Deletion resolves it: all four legacy predicates lived in UsageJSONStore.loadLocked; the SQLite migration equivalents (v3/v4) are covered by usage-index-regressions.py.

symbol: UsageStats.formatTokens / formatContext / compactLabel / shift / interval / formatter
summary: Of all of UsageStats only `heatmapDays` is driven by a regression; the formatting thresholds and the zone-keyed formatter cache have no coverage, while a second private copy of the same formatting exists in the widget target.

startAutoRefresh's timer is never invalidated when the core stops, so it keeps downloading after the VPN is turned off
evidence: The doc (lines 203-205) says invalidating first is "the only teardown" and that a timer "must not keep refreshing against one that has since stopped", but `refreshTimer?.invalidate()` exists only inside `startAutoRefresh` itself (line 207). grep over Sources shows the only caller is `VpnManager.swift:837` (startup path) and no stop path touches it: `stopCore` (VpnManager.swift:746-779), `syncRuntime` (460-467) and `reloadConfig` (799-809) never invalidate or nil it.
failure: User starts the VPN once, then turns it off → the 1800 s timer stays armed for the life of the process; every 30 min it downloads the active subscription URL again and, on success, calls `manager.reloadConfig()` (a no-op while disabled). Background network I/O plus unexpected on-disk profile rewrites long after the user stopped the module.
fix: Add a `stopAutoRefresh()` that invalidates and nils the timer, call it from the stop branches (`syncRuntime`/`stopCore`), or guard the closure with `guard self.manager?.isRunning == true`.
verdict_note: `stopAutoRefresh()` is new and called from `VpnManager.stopCore` — the one teardown every core stop passes through — so a stopped core no longer carries a 30-minute subscription refresh that would call `reloadConfig()` on nothing.

summary: `request()` treats "already authorized" the same as "denied": flipping the 定位 switch on opens System Settings even when the permission is already granted.

summary: The island re-spells the 0.6/0.85 context ladder that `Theme.ContextLevel` already owns, and Theme's own doc names this exact site as the one that should map the band instead.
evidence: IslandComponents.swift:256-259 `if ratio < 0.6 { return IslandStyle.mint }; if ratio < 0.85 { return IslandStyle.amber }; return IslandStyle.coral`. Theme.swift:246-253: "The thresholds are the rule; the hue is the surface's own. ... a surface that keeps its own palette (`CursorSessionCardView`'s violet, the island gauge's mint/coral) can map the band instead of re-spelling `0.6`/`0.85`" and the shared `enum ContextLevel { init(_ ratio: Double) { if ratio < 0.6 { .ok } else if ratio < 0.85 { .warn } ... } }`. The sibling surface already took the offer: CursorSessionCardView.swift:19 `switch Theme.ContextLevel(ratio)`.
failure: A future edit to the ladder (say warn at 0.9) changes Theme.ContextLevel, the widget's own copy is updated with it, and the island keeps 0.6/0.85 — the same session then shows mint on the island while its card on the dashboard shows amber for the same fill. No test pins either threshold pair.
fix: Replace the two literals with `switch Theme.ContextLevel(ratio) { case .ok: return IslandStyle.mint; case .warn: return IslandStyle.amber; case .critical: return IslandStyle.coral }`; the hues stay the island's own, only the band comes from Theme.

summary: The 30-day peak is recomputed twice per render — once in `heroCaption` on every body evaluation and again inside `IslandHistogram`'s Canvas draw.
evidence: IslandComponents.swift:412 `let peak = usage.days.map(\.tokens).max() ?? 0` (called from `heroCaption`, invoked by `hero` on every `IslandUsageCard.body` evaluation, i.e. on each `usage` publish and on every `scrubIndex` change from `.onContinuousHover`, line 320-327). The same value is recomputed at line 476 `let peak = CGFloat(max(days.map(\.tokens).max() ?? 0, 1))` inside the Canvas closure, which runs on every draw. `usage.days` is fixed at 30 elements (IslandLiveModel.swift:465 `(0..<30).compactMap`).
failure: Swiping the pointer across the histogram changes `scrubIndex` up to 30 times per sweep; each change re-evaluates the card body and pays ~60 comparisons plus two `[Int]` map temporaries per frame, when the peak is a function of `usage.days` alone and changes only on a usage publish.
fix: Compute the peak once (`let peak = usage.days.map(\.tokens).max() ?? 0` in `IslandUsageCard.body`, passed into both `heroCaption` and `IslandHistogram`), or store it on `IslandUsage` next to `days` where it is already produced.

summary: `costCaption(estimate)` is evaluated twice in one render, and each call runs the full string-building pipeline (`detailParts` + money formatting).
evidence: IslandComponents.swift:394 `if !costCaption(estimate).isEmpty {` and 395 `RollingNumberText(costCaption(estimate))`; `costCaption` (403-408) calls `estimate.detailParts().first ?? estimate.emptyCaption`, and `detailParts` (ModelPricing.swift:329-342) builds an array and formats one or two amounts through `ModelPricing.format` (ModelPricing.swift:702-711: `String(format: "%.2f", ...)` plus `group`'s reversed-string walk). The file's own sibling shows the house fix: CursorSessionCardView.swift:28 "Derived once: `cardLabel` runs the full condense/shorten pipeline and was read twice".
failure: Every usage publish (per `usageIndexDidRefresh`, debounced 500 ms — several a second during a transcript burst) and every scrub frame pays two `detailParts()` pipelines instead of one; visible cost is small, but it is exactly the double-derivation pattern the codebase removed elsewhere.
fix: `let caption = costCaption(estimate)` once at the top of `costHero` and use it for both the emptiness check and the `RollingNumberText`.
verdict_note: Fixed in the same pass as finding 31: costHero derives `let caption = costCaption(shown, estimate:)` once and uses it for both the emptiness check and the RollingNumberText. `costCaption` now also takes the Presented (detailParts(presented:)) so the caption matches the headline. No measurement recorded — the double derivation is gone, and the pipeline (detailParts + format) still runs once per render.

summary: The `.quotaReset` arm of `openLabel` is unreachable: the only call site is guarded by `sessionToOpen`, which returns nil for a quota rollover.
evidence: Call site NotchIslandView.swift:445-448 `if let openSession = sessionToOpen { Button { actions.openSession(openSession) } label: { ... Text(openLabel(openSession))`; `sessionToOpen` (494-500) returns nil for `case .quotaReset`. So the switch at 505-510 `case .finished, .quotaReset: return session.agent == .cursor ? "打开" : "继续"` can never be entered with `.quotaReset`. The parallel `alertQuotaLabel` (512-515) exists precisely because the quota branch has no session to open.
failure: No user-visible failure today; the cost is that a reader (or a future edit that starts passing a session for quota alerts) believes the arm is live and keeps it in sync, while a change to the quota action label would be silently dead.
fix: Replace the switch with `if case .needsInput = alert { return "去确认" }; return session.agent == .cursor ? "打开" : "继续"` — the quota case disappears and the function stays total.

summary: One `@ObservedObject IslandLiveModel` for the whole island: publishes that only one leaf reads re-evaluate the root body and rebuild the other surfaces' subtrees.
evidence: NotchIslandView.swift:139-140 `@ObservedObject var state: NotchIslandState; @ObservedObject var model: IslandLiveModel`, and the root `island` (156-199) branches into `wings` / `IslandAlertContent` / `expandedContent` from that one object. `IslandLiveModel` publishes sessions, sessionCosts, usage, claudeRoute, codexRoute, vpnRunning (IslandLiveModel.swift:122-127); `sessionCosts` is refreshed on every `usageIndexDidRefresh` (IslandLiveModel.swift:220-226, debounced 500 ms). Reading the consumers: `wings` (211-244) reads only `model.usage.today` / `model.busySessions`; `routeChip` (309-322) reads only the two routes; `expandedContent` (269-285) rebuilds the Canvas histogram and the LazyVGrid.
failure: While the island is expanded, a `sessionCosts` publish (up to ~2/s during an FSEvents transcript burst) re-evaluates `NotchIslandView.body`, the header and the usage card — a Canvas command-list rebuild plus a grid diff — although only the per-row cost labels read that field; a `claudeRoute` change similarly re-runs the wings. I could not measure this, so the confidence is medium: the repo's own samples (§7 in docs/reviews/ui-audit-backlog.md) show body evaluation was *not* the residual per-frame cost, so this is an unnecessary-work finding, not a proven frame regression.
fix: Split the model's published surface per consumer (a small `usage`-only observable for the wings, a routes-only one for the header) or move to `@Observable` so per-field dependency tracking replaces whole-object invalidation — the same field-scoped shape `ScopedStoreObservation` gives the main window.

summary: .id(appearance) 的外观重建边界会销毁页面子树，包括打开中的供应商编辑弹窗与未保存草稿
evidence: MainWindowView.swift:92-95 `.frame(...)`、`.preferredColorScheme(...)`、`.id(appearance)` 作用于包含 topBar + detailView 的整棵内容；ProvidersView 的编辑弹窗由页面内 `@State connectionEdit/setupEntry` 提出（ProvidersView.swift:83-91），SessionsView 持有 `@StateObject migrations`（SessionsView.swift:55）、UsageView 持有 `displayedAnalytics/renderedModelRequest` 等（UsageView.swift:8-14）。MenuBarView.swift:95-100 记录了同样做法的代价（重建 graph、重置滚动与展开态、重跑 onAppear 链）——popup 因此去掉了它。
